title: BUG P1: hvfh.4.3 toast drainToastQueue forward-declaration shadowed by 'local function' (queue never drains)
close_reason: Completed: dropped 'local' from the drainToastQueue function definition (init.client.lua line 518) so it assigns to the existing forward-declared local at line 436 instead of shadowing it. The forward declaration 'local drainToastQueue' (line 436) was captured by showToastDirect's fade-out callback closure (line 514: drainToastQueue()), but 'local function drainToastQueue()' (line 518) created a NEW local that shadowed the forward decl — leaving the captured local nil. Result: when any toast faded out after TOAST_LIFETIME, the callback called nil() -> 'attempt to call a nil value', and the FIFO queue never drained (queued toasts stuck forever). Root cause: hvfh.4.3 (commit e53d153, SilverDog) used 'local function' instead of 'function' for the forward-declared local. luau-analyze flagged this as UninitializedLocal + FunctionUnused but it was treated as a warning. Same class of bug as the hvfh.8.2 undefined constants: pure-spec gate missed it because init.client.lua is not loaded by the pure specs. Fix: 'local function drainToastQueue()' -> 'function drainToastQueue()'. luau-analyze: 2 warnings -> 0. Pure-spec gate PASSED. Partial-staged 1-line change via git update-index; WildCat hvfh.3.1 WIP left unstaged.

title: TASK 42.4: Static-analysis config for Roblox Luau idioms (kill ~54 selene false positives)
description:
## Goal

Selene 0.31 reports ~54 parse 'errors' on init.client.lua that are actually valid Luau the project deliberately uses: compound assignment (+=, -=), typed locals (local x: any), generic-for with typed vars. They are noise that hides real parse regressions (a true SyntaxError like the WIP's 'return ContextMenu' went unnoticed partly because the count was already ~93 at HEAD).

## Fix

Add selene.toml (or extend the existing one — check repo root) with std = 'roblox' (selene ships a roblox std) and/or a luau std, so Luau-specific syntax parses. Verify the false-positive count drops to ~0 while REAL parse errors still surface. Also confirm luau-analyze is invoked with the Roblox API definitions (the ~800 'Unknown global UDim2/Enum/Instance' noise in raw invocation suggests missing definitions file — check how CI .github/workflows/tests.yml invokes it and mirror that locally).

## Considerations

- Do NOT 'fix' the Luau idioms themselves (rewriting += to x = x + y churns 7000 lines for zero behavior gain and conflicts with project style).
- Success metric: selene parse_error count on init.client.lua goes from ~54 to ~0; any NEW parse error remains visible.

Independent of 42.1 (config-only, no behavior change) but nice-to-have before 42.3 so the contract check isn't drowned in noise.
close_reason: Completed in a907836: selene.toml (std=roblox+luau) + generated roblox.yml. Parse errors 54 -> 0 (were Luau-idiom false positives). Real issues now visible: 3 enum errors filed as harborheist-5rcp; 27 warnings pre-existing. Silenced stylistic lints (roblox_manual_fromscale_or_fromoffset, empty_if, multiple_statements) per project convention.

title: EPIC 34: Animation & Motion Design — Micro-interactions, Transitions, Physics
description:
**BACKGROUND & RATIONALE:**

The current animation system is functional but lacks the polish of premium apps. Animations are mostly basic tweens without spring physics, staggered entrances, or contextual motion.

**CURRENT STATE:**
- Basic tweens for panel open/close
- Some hover effects (button scale, glow)
- Staggered list entrances (STAGGER_STEP = 0.035)
- No spring physics (everything uses easing curves)
- No gesture-based animations (swipe, pull-to-refresh)

**WHY THIS MATTERS:**
1. **Perceived quality**: Smooth, physics-based motion feels premium
2. **User feedback**: Animations confirm actions and guide attention
3. **Delight**: Subtle motion creates emotional connection
4. **Clarity**: Transitions help users understand spatial relationships

**IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGY:**
1. Create spring physics system (替代 easing curves for interactive elements)
2. Add micro-interactions (button press, toggle, success/error states)
3. Implement gesture-based animations (swipe to dismiss, pull-to-refresh)
4. Add contextual motion (elements respond to user actions)
5. Create transition library (fade, slide, scale, rotate presets)

**DEPENDENCIES:**
- Depends on EPIC 30 (design system) for consistent timing/spacing
- Should be done AFTER EPIC 31 (loading states) and EPIC 32 (accessibility)
- Can be done in parallel with EPIC 33 (toasts)

**CONSIDERATIONS:**
- Spring physics may be overkill for some elements (use judiciously)
- Mobile performance: complex animations may lag on low-end devices
- Accessibility: respect prefers-reduced-motion (if Roblox supports it)
- Consistency: all animations should feel part of the same system

**SUCCESS CRITERIA:**
- Spring physics system implemented and documented
- 10+ micro-interactions added (button press, toggle, success, error, etc.)
- Gesture-based animations work on mobile
- All transitions use consistent timing/easing
- Animations feel cohesive and premium

title: Implement spring physics system for interactive elements
description: REVISED: Roblox TweenService already has EasingStyle.Spring (added 2022). We don't need custom spring physics. REPLACED 2 EasingStyle.Back -> Spring: (1) EASE_POP definition (line 72) — used exclusively for scale-in/pop effects (button release bounce-back at L417, toast scale-in L995, sellStore prompt L1186, panel scale-in L1676, reveal card L5337, overlay scale-in) — Spring gives physics-based overshoot that's more natural than Back's synthetic curve; (2) Legendary reveal card inline Back at L4654 — same pop-in use case, the most dramatic catch gets the bounciest spring. Kept all Quad/Quint/Sine/Linear (documented why: fades/press/exit/timing where Spring overshoot is inappropriate). Gates: luau 734=734, selene unchanged, rojo OK, pure 104 pass, coverage gate pass. title: Add micro-interactions for button states (press, hover, success, error)
description:
**CONTEXT:**
Buttons currently have basic hover effects but lack rich micro-interactions that provide feedback and delight.

**WHAT TO DO:**
1. Enhance button press animation (spring-based scale + rotation)
2. Add hover state animations (subtle lift, glow pulse)
3. Implement success state (checkmark animation, color flash)
4. Implement error state (shake animation, red flash)
5. Add loading state (spinner, pulse animation)

**IMPLEMENTATION:**
```lua
-- Button micro-interactions
local function addButtonInteractions(button)
  -- Press animation (spring-based)
  local pressSpring = SpringService.create(1, SpringService.presets.stiff)
  button.MouseButton1Down:Connect(function()
    pressSpring:setTarget(0.95)
  end)
  button.MouseButton1Up:Connect(function()
    pressSpring:setTarget(1)
  end)
  
  -- Hover animation (subtle lift)
  button.MouseEnter:Connect(function()
    TweenService:Create(button, TweenInfo.new(0.2), {
      Position = button.Position + UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, -2)
    }):Play()
  end)
  button.MouseLeave:Connect(function()
    TweenService:Create(button, TweenInfo.new(0.2), {
      Position = button.Position + UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 2)
    }):Play()
  end)
  
  -- Success animation
  button.showSuccess = function()
    -- Flash green, show checkmark
    local originalColor = button.BackgroundColor3
    button.BackgroundColor3 = UI.state.success
    task.delay(0.3, function()
      button.BackgroundColor3 = originalColor
    end)
  end
  
  -- Error animation (shake)
  button.showError = function()
    local originalPos = button.Position
    for i = 1, 3 do
      TweenService:Create(button, TweenInfo.new(0.05), {
        Position = originalPos + UDim2.new(0, -5, 0, 0)
      }):Play()
      task.wait(0.05)
      TweenService:Create(button, TweenInfo.new(0.05), {
        Position = originalPos + UDim2.new(0, 5, 0, 0)
      }):Play()
      task.wait(0.05)
    end
    button.Position = originalPos
  end
end
```

**VERIFICATION:**
- All button states have distinct animations
- Animations feel responsive and natural
- Performance is acceptable (no lag)
- Animations work on both desktop and mobile
close_reason: EPIC 34 complete: Animation & Motion Design implemented with pressFeedback micro-interactions, hover affordances, Transitions reusable animation library (fade in/out, scale, slide), and touch/cancel handling preventing stuck animations

title: Exploit: stunned thief can SpawnBoat to teleport-escape stun penalty
description: Fellow-agent review (Hermes-K3). BoatService.spawnBoat teleports the player's character to the boat dock with no stun check. title: P0: Overlay input router missing — cast/bite/raid minigames cannot receive clicks (broken at HEAD since 6f1a0c8)
description:
## Summary

The single UserInputService.InputBegan overlay router (TASK 23.1 / hvfh.3.1) is MISSING from src/client/init.client.lua. The three overlay input handlers (overlayInputHandlers.cast at ~:5242, .raid at ~:4711, .bite at ~:6233) are registered but NEVER invoked — nothing routes input to them. The cast minigame, bite minigame, and raid minigame cannot receive any clicks/taps. Fishing is unplayable.

## Root cause (verified via git archaeology)

Commit 6f1a0c8 (EPIC 34: Animation & Motion Design, Jul 27) appended the toast-history block (harborheist-6388.4, 'Toast History Storage' comment + toastHistory table + addToHistory/getHistory/clearHistory) to the END of init.client.lua — overwriting the overlay router that previously lived there. The router's detailed comment block (~:6988-6997, 'the ONE UserInputService.InputBegan router. Lives at the BOTTOM of the file...') survived, but the actual UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect dispatch code was replaced.

Confirmed: router exists in 93be256 (hvfh.3.1, when introduced) at file end; git log -S 'overlayInputHandlers[activeOverlay] or nil' shows only 93be256 added it; grep of 6600d91 (pre-repair HEAD) = 0 matches. Broken in ALL commits 6f1a0c8..1047841 (current).

## Why it went unnoticed

The client has no headless test coverage: pure specs (lune) don't require the DataModel game instance, and the E2E suite (tests/e2e_stub.lua) drives server-side service seams directly, bypassing client UI input entirely. This is exactly EPIC 19 gap G6/G7 territory.

## Fix (verified against 93be256 original)

Append at the very END of init.client.lua, after the last overlayInputHandlers assignment (the lexical-scope reason is in the surviving comment):

  UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input, gameProcessed)
    local handler = activeOverlay and overlayInputHandlers[activeOverlay] or nil
    if handler then
      handler(input, gameProcessed)
    end
  end)

## Verification
luau-analyze 0 SyntaxErrors; rojo build succeeds; pure specs + coverage gate still pass. Runtime verification of the cast minigame needs Roblox Studio (Linux box cannot run it) — record as Studio-manual-verification per docs/CATCH_FLOW_RUNBOOK.md.

Found during HarborHeist-Dev deep review session 2026-07-30 (audit finding #1, independently confirmed). Unblocks the bead stack under this one.
close_reason: Fixed in 4a2fc0e: router restored at file end (verbatim from 93be256 design). Gates green (0 SyntaxErrors, pure specs + coverage pass, rojo build OK). Minigame runtime verification tracked in harborheist-orpl (requires Roblox Studio, not available on Linux).

title: TASK 14.26: Coalesce checkpoint saves (dirty-flag) — isSaving waits then re-saves, no collapse
description: FoggyTower review: thj.2 checkpoint saves claim to be 'coalesced by DataManager.save's isSaving guard', but the guard WAITS (up to 15s) then runs a FULL UpdateAsync again — N rapid transactions = N sequential DataStore writes (GetAsync+SetAsync each). Under load this risks DataStore budget throttling. Minimal design: session.saveDirty flag; in-flight save re-checks dirty at completion and runs at most one trailing write. Must preserve BindToClose/leave semantics (their saves must complete synchronously). Files: src/server/DataManager.lua.
close_reason: Completed: Dirty-flag coalescing for checkpoint saves. Non-shutdown saves set saveDirty+return (trailing write picks up changes). Leave handler uses isShutdown=true for synchronous wait. Pushed 15c626f.

title: EPIC 33: Toast Notifications & Feedback Systems — Hierarchy, Persistence, Actions
description:
**BACKGROUND & RATIONALE:**

The current toast notification system lacks hierarchy and persistence:
- All toasts look identical regardless of severity
- Toasts auto-dismiss after 3.6s with no way to extend or interact
- No action buttons (e.g., 'Undo' on delete, 'View' on achievement)
- Severe toasts (raid-victim, datastore errors) get lost in the queue

**WHY THIS MATTERS:**
1. **Information hierarchy**: Users need to distinguish between info, warnings, and critical errors
2. **Actionable feedback**: Some notifications need user action (undo, view details, retry)
3. **Critical alerts**: Raid attacks and save errors should persist until acknowledged
4. **Premium feel**: Stripe/Linear use sophisticated notification systems with actions and persistence

**IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGY:**
1. Create toast variants (info, success, warning, error, critical)
2. Add action buttons to toasts (undo, view, retry, dismiss)
3. Make critical toasts persistent (require manual dismiss)
4. Add toast queue with priority (critical > error > warning > info)
5. Add toast history panel (view past notifications)

**DEPENDENCIES:**
- Depends on EPIC 30 (design system) for consistent styling
- Should be done AFTER EPIC 31 (loading states) and EPIC 32 (accessibility)

**CONSIDERATIONS:**
- Persistent toasts need a dismiss mechanism (close button or timeout)
- Action buttons need to not interfere with game controls
- Toast history needs storage (session-only or persistent?)
- Mobile vs desktop may need different toast behaviors

**SUCCESS CRITERIA:**
- 5 toast variants with distinct visual styles
- Action buttons work on at least 3 toast types
- Critical toasts persist until dismissed
- Toast history panel shows last 20 notifications

title: Add action buttons to toasts (undo, view, retry, dismiss)
description:
**CONTEXT:**
Some notifications need user action (undo a delete, view details, retry a failed operation) but current toasts are display-only.

**WHAT TO DO:**
1. Extend toast system to support action buttons
2. Create action button component (small, right-aligned in toast)
3. Add action callbacks to showNotification()
4. Implement common actions:
   - Undo (for delete/sell operations)
   - View (for achievements/unlocks)
   - Retry (for failed operations)

**IMPLEMENTATION:**
```lua
local function showNotification(message, color, category, actions)
  -- actions = { { label = "Undo", callback = function() ... end } }
  
  -- Render action buttons in toast
  if actions then
    for i, action in ipairs(actions) do
      local btn = makeButton(toast, "secondary", {
        Size = UDim2.new(0, 60, 0, 24),
        Position = UDim2.new(1, -70 - (i-1)*65, 0.5, -12),
        Text = action.label,
      })
      btn.MouseButton1Click:Connect(function()
        action.callback()
        dismissToast(toast)

    end
  end
end
```

**USE CASES:**
- Sell fish: show "Undo" button for 3 seconds
- Achievement unlocked: show "View" button to open collection
- Failed purchase: show "Retry" button
- Critical error: show "Dismiss" button

**VERIFICATION:**

- Callbacks execute when clicked

- Multiple actions can coexist (max 2 per toast)

title: Create universal skeleton loader component
description:
**CONTEXT:**
The collection panel has a skeleton loader (showCollectionSkeleton), but it's custom-built for that panel. We need a reusable skeleton loader that can be used across all panels.

**WHAT TO DO:**
Create a generic skeleton loader factory:

```lua
-- Design system: skeleton loader
local function createSkeletonLoader(parent, config)
  -- config: { rows = N, rowHeight = N, gap = N, animated = bool }
  local skeleton = Instance.new("Frame")
  skeleton.BackgroundColor3 = UI.surface.secondary
  skeleton.BackgroundTransparency = 0.5
  corner(skeleton, CORNERS.md)
  
  -- Add shimmer animation
  if config.animated then
    local shimmer = Instance.new("UIGradient")
    shimmer.Color = ColorSequence.new({
      ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0, Color3.new(1, 1, 1, 0)),
      ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.5, Color3.new(1, 1, 1, 0.3)),
      ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(1, Color3.new(1, 1, 1, 0)),
    })
    shimmer.Rotation = 45
    shimmer.Parent = skeleton
    
    -- Animate shimmer
    task.spawn(function()
      while skeleton.Parent do
        local tween = TweenService:Create(shimmer, TweenInfo.new(1.5), {
          Offset = Vector2.new(1, 0)
        })
        tween:Play()
        tween.Completed:Wait()
        shimmer.Offset = Vector2.new(-1, 0)
      end
    end)
  end
  
  return skeleton
end
```

**USAGE:**
```lua
-- In panel open function
if not data then
  local loader = createSkeletonLoader(content, {
    rows = 5,
    rowHeight = 60,
    gap = SPACING.sm,
    animated = true,
  })
  -- Fetch data, then destroy loader and render real content
end
```

**RATIONALE:**
Skeleton loaders provide immediate visual feedback that content is loading. The shimmer animation adds polish and matches premium app patterns (Stripe, Linear, Vercel all use this).

**VERIFICATION:**
- Component works across different panel sizes
- Shimmer animation is smooth (60fps)
- No memory leaks (animation stops when skeleton is destroyed)
notes: Implemented by RainyLynx-Jul26. Created a universal createSkeletonRows(parent, config) factory at ~line 536 (after makeButton, in the primitive-helpers section). Configurable: rows (default 3), rowHeight (default IS_MOBILE 110/desktop 120), gap (default Theme.spacing.md=12, used only when creating a new UIListLayout), zIndex (default 26), animated (default true), barColor (default Theme.color.surface.elevated=UI.surfaceHi), radius (default Theme.corners.md=12). Uses the PROVEN cascading transparency-pulse animation from the existing showCollectionSkeleton — NOT the bead's proposed UIGradient shimmer, because Roblox ColorSequenceKeypoint has no alpha channel (the bead's Color3.new(1,1,1,0) is technically invalid; Color3 takes 3 args, and ColorSequence keypoints carry Color3 only, no transparency). The pulse pattern is already runtime-verified in the collection panel. The factory preserves existing parent UIListLayouts (FindFirstChildOfClass check) — only creates one for bare Frame parents. Self-terminating animation (task.spawn loop exits when bars[1].Parent becomes nil, same as the original). REFACTORED showCollectionSkeleton (now at ~line 2517) to delegate to the factory as a thin wrapper (rows=3, rowHeight=110/120, zIndex=26) — proves backward compat and eliminates ~24 lines of duplicated animation code. Factory defaults match the original values exactly (verified: Theme.color.surface.elevated=UI.surfaceHi, Theme.corners.md=12). Verification: luau-analyze 731->734 (+3 Unknown global: Instance/UDim/Enum — same pre-existing Roblox-globals type from the UIListLayout creation branch; zero LocalUnused/FunctionUnused added); selene unchanged (0/0/55); rojo build OK; pure suite 104 passed, coverage gate PASSED. Caveat: NOT runtime/visually verified in Roblox Studio (no Studio on Linux); the pulse animation is the same proven code, and factory structural correctness verified by static analysis + the refactored showCollectionSkeleton call (which exercises the factory's default code path). Unblocks 6 downstream loading-state beads (7h69.2-7h69.7) that can now call createSkeletonRows with panel-specific config.

title: Add loading spinners for quick operations
description:
Create subtle loading spinner component for quick operations (button clicks, toggles, purchases). Should:

1. Appear on the button itself (not full panel)
2. Disable button while loading
3. Show spinner icon + 'Loading...' text
4. Re-enable on completion
5. Handle errors with toast notification

Use cases:
- Purchase upgrade buttons in shop
- Raid opt-in toggle
- Lock/Alarm toggle buttons
- Claim income button
- Store/Sell buttons in inventory

Implementation:
```lua
local function withLoading(button, callback)
  local originalText = button.Text
  button.Text = 'Loading...'
  button.Active = false
  
  task.spawn(function()
    local ok, err = pcall(callback)
    button.Text = originalText
    button.Active = true
    
    if not ok then
      showNotification('Operation failed: ' .. tostring(err), UI.state.error)
    end
  end)
end
```
close_reason: Implemented withLoading() helper function for button loading states

title: DataManager: pendingSaveUserIds flag cleared by whichever save finishes first — stale-read window on rapid rejoin
description: Subagent finding (verified by parent). save() sets pendingSaveUserIds[uid]=true at line 664 and nils it at 728 unconditionally. load() waits on the flag at line 461. Two overlapping saves for the same userId (stale deferred leave-save + new-session autosave): the first to complete clears the flag while the second is still in flight; a concurrent load() then reads pre-save DataStore data = lost progress on rapid leave/rejoin cycles. title: Toast queue silently drops action buttons (write-only path)
description:
EVIDENCE: src/client/init.client.lua showNotification (~:2267). When MAX_VISIBLE_TOASTS (3) is reached, the queued entry is { message, color, category } (~:2284) — the 4th parameter `actions` is dropped. drainToastQueue (~:2262) calls showToastDirect(pending.message, pending.color, pending.category) without actions.

IMPACT: showToastDirect supports up to 2 action buttons + persistent-variant close button (~:2203-2255). Any future/current caller passing actions whose toast gets queued shows the toast WITHOUT its buttons — a half-rendered interactive element. Currently latent: audit found NO live caller passing actions today, and the server Notify remote (OnClientEvent -> showNotification, :7061) never carries actions. Filed as bug because the API contract is broken-by-omission; severity contained (latent).

FIX (small): (1) add `actions = actions` to the queue entry; (2) forward in drainToastQueue: showToastDirect(pending.message, pending.color, pending.category, pending.actions); (3) confirm the MAX_TOAST_QUEUE eviction loop (~:2292-2300) does not need action-aware eviction (it does not — severity-based only).

CONSIDERATIONS: persistent toasts (variant.persistent, e.g. datastore/raid-victim) are NEVER queued today because activeToastCount rarely blocks them (severity jump puts them at queue head). After the fix, a queued persistent toast must still render its close button — that falls out naturally since showToastDirect branches on variant, not on queue origin.

VERIFY (Linux): selene + luau-analyze zero-new-errors; scripts/run_tests.sh --pure green; rojo build. STUDIO CHECK (fold into harborheist-orpl): force 4 simultaneous toasts where the 4th has actions; confirm buttons render when it drains.
close_reason: Completed: Fixed toast queue to preserve action buttons when toasts are queued. (1) Added actions=actions to queue entry in showNotification; (2) Forwarded pending.actions in drainToastQueue's showToastDirect call. Currently latent (no live caller passes actions), but API contract is now correct. Tests: 607 passed/0 failed. Selene: 17 warnings (unchanged). Studio verification deferred to harborheist-orpl. Committed + pushed.

title: Shop clarity: purchase-success row micro-animation

title: Raid minigame: unify marker motion to ping-pong sweep (match bite minigame)
description:
PROBLEM: the two timing minigames in the game teach DIFFERENT motion languages for the same skill. Bite marker ping-pongs 0->1->0 on a 1.2s cycle (runMinigame, init.client.lua:6191-6260); raid marker sweeps ONCE linearly 0->1 over durationSeconds (default 8s) via a single TweenService tween (startRaidMinigame, :4996-5010). One-shot timing and rhythmic timing are different motor skills; the raid is the rarer, higher-stakes event, so players arrive at it with muscle memory trained on the WRONG motion model.

FIX: replace the linear tween with a ping-pong sweep driven by the same pattern as runMinigame (task.spawn loop, os.clock-based pos = triangular wave), with sweep period chosen so the 8s raid window contains ~4-5 full sweeps (period ~1.6-1.8s). Server contract is UNCHANGED: SubmitRaidResult takes markerPos [0,1] and the server re-derives tier from its own bounds (RaidService:835-903), so client motion model is a pure presentation choice — zero exploit-surface change. Remove the raidMinigameTween handle and its Cancel in stopRaidMinigame; keep the generation-guarded 8s expiry (harborheist-d6et) exactly as-is — the loop now owns marker position instead of the tween, so the expiry path stops the loop flag instead of cancelling a tween.

CONSIDERATIONS: (a) the raid marker starts at pos 0 — start the triangle at 0 moving right, matching the old initial direction; (b) raid marker styling (5px white bar + glow) is identical to the bite marker already, so motion unification completes the visual unification; (c) 8s durationSeconds is server-chosen per attempt — read it from challenge as today and compute position from elapsed time, never accumulating local dt (drift-proof).

WHY: one timing language across the game lowers the skill floor, makes the raid feel like a high-stakes VARIATION of fishing rather than a foreign minigame, and removes a tween-vs-loop duality that has already produced one latent bug class (d6et).

VERIFY (Linux): pure suite + selene + build. STUDIO CHECK (orpl raid runbook, RAID_TWO_PLAYER_RUNBOOK.md): marker sweeps back and forth for the full window; taps submit correct positions at both sweep ends; expiry at duration end still fires "Too slow!".
close_reason: Completed: Replaced linear TweenService sweep with os.clock-based ping-pong triangular wave loop (matching runMinigame pattern). raidMinigameActive flag replaces raidMinigameTween handle. stopRaidMinigame now sets flag false instead of tween:Cancel. Marker position interpolates (0,0)->(1,-5) via pos*-5. Sweep period 1.7s (~4-5 sweeps in 8s window). Generation-guarded expiry unchanged. Added 3 source-contract specs to RaidServiceLogic.spec. Pure suite 615/0 fail, selene 0 new warnings, build OK. Studio check (orpl raid runbook) deferred.

title: Raid targets: surface loot signal (stealable count + best rarity chip)
description:
PROBLEM: raid target rows communicate name + availability + cooldown only (renderRaidTargets, init.client.lua:4531-4760). A raider choosing between two available targets has zero information about which aquarium is worth the 6-minute raider cooldown and the 1-fish-per-raid cap. Meaningful target selection is a core PvP decision currently made blind.

GOOD NEWS (verified in RaidService.buildTargetSnapshot ~:374-381): the server ALREADY sends stealableCount for available targets (aquariumService.getStealableFish count) — the client simply never renders it. So the count portion is CLIENT-ONLY work.

FIX: (1) CLIENT: on available target rows, render "N fish in live-well" subtext; if stealableCount == 0 cannot happen (eligibility requires fish) but guard anyway. (2) SERVER (additive): in the available-target branch, compute bestRarity = highest Rarity among getStealableFish results (fish carry .Rarity; Legendary is excluded from stealable by design — IsRaidProtected — and Epic is weight-reduced at selection time, but presence signal is honest) and add bestRarity = <name> to the target entry. (3) CLIENT: render a small rarity-colored chip (RARITY_COLORS map, :3318) next to the row, e.g. "EPIC POOL" — reads as intel, not a promise (selection remains weighted-random server-side; caption the chip "best in pool" in the row subtext to avoid implying guaranteed steal).

FAIRNESS CHECK (important — do not regress PVP design): this does NOT leak Legendary presence (Legendary is never stealable, so it never appears in the pool) and does not leak exact species. It matches the transparency spirit of TASK 26.1.1/PVP-07 (show unavailable reasons rather than hide). If design later decides rarity intel is too strong, ship count-only and drop (2)+(3).

VERIFY (Linux): pure suite (RaidServiceLogic.spec can pin the additive key), selene, build. STUDIO CHECK (orpl raid runbook): available rows show count + chip; unavailable rows unchanged; zero-pool targets never appear.
close_reason: Completed: client half landed. Available raid-target rows now render a rarity-colored 'X POOL • best in pool' chip from server-sent bestRarity (RARITY_COLORS fallback); stealable-count subtext verified already live since hvfh.6.1.2. 4 ClientChrome contract assertions. title: Mobile: reachable HOW TO PLAY / shortcuts entry point (desktop has H key, mobile has nothing)
description:

PROBLEM: the SHORTCUTS panel (helpPanel, init.client.lua:6887-6985) is reachable ONLY via the H keyboard shortcut (:7032-7033) — and the platform with no keyboard is the platform that cannot discover how anything works. The panel itself is already mobile-aware (copy switches to "Tap an action button:", :6891).

(3) CONTENT: expand SHORTCUT_ROWS into a compact HOW TO PLAY — keep desktop key rows; on mobile show tap equivalents; prepend 3-4 one-line gameplay rows (Fish in the glowing zone at your dock / Store fish in your tank for passive income / Sell for instant cash / Buy upgrades at the Bait and Tackle shop (E)) — declarative table-driven rows as today; the panel is 480px with a scrolling list, capacity is fine.

CONSIDERATIONS: KeyboardNav:Register is desktop-only (helpClose registered at :6983-6985); the desktop chip participates in actionButtons so pressFeedback/key chips follow automatically. The mobile "?" button needs no KeyboardNav registration (touch-only).

VERIFY (Linux): pure suite (TouchTargets.spec — the 44px "?" passes automatically), selene, build. STUDIO CHECK (rswb): "?" visible top-right in portrait AND landscape; no collision with raid banner during a window; desktop bar shows HELP chip; H still works.

title: Toast system: add "zone" category (warning variant, ZONE chip) for spatial-guidance messages
description:
Blocks harborheist-a2ug.15 (its re-guidance toast needs this category). PROBLEM: TOAST_CATEGORIES (init.client.lua:2006-2010) has no key for positional/zone guidance, so the server not_in_zone toast (FishingService:92, no category) renders as a plain INFO chip — visually indistinguishable from trivia. Zone guidance is a WARNING-class signal (the player is doing something wrong) and deserves the warning variant (amber, 4.5s dwell).

FIX: (1) TOAST_CATEGORIES.zone = "ZONE"; (2) CATEGORY_TO_VARIANT.zone = "warning" (maps to amber warn color + 4.5s duration, zero new variant code — TOAST_VARIANTS.warning already exists, :2024-2030); (3) FishingService:92 not_in_zone notify gains category "zone". Note a2ug.3 independently adds categories to uncategorized calls; the zone key is created HERE (not in a2ug.3) to keep the client table change atomic with its consumer — if a2ug.3 lands first it must skip FishingService:92 and leave it to this bead (note is recorded in a2ug.3 description too).

CONSIDERATION: adding a key to both client tables in one commit avoids the mixed-deploy state (server sends category before client knows it) — order the client edit first in the same commit. Unknown categories already fall back to INFO chip safely (:2105 TOAST_CATEGORIES[category] or "INFO"), so even a stale client degrades gracefully.

VERIFY (Linux): pure suite + selene + build. STUDIO CHECK (orpl): cast outside a zone -> amber ZONE-chipped 4.5s toast.
close_reason: Completed: Added 'zone' toast category (ZONE chip + warning variant/amber/4.5s) for spatial-guidance messages. FishingService not_in_zone notify now uses category 'zone'. Unblocks a2ug.15. Commit c72dfa0, pushed. Quality gates: 607 pure specs, build OK, selene 0 new warnings, remote arity + overlay router OK.

title: Wandering-player re-guidance: re-arm the zone cue on repeated out-of-zone casts
description:
Depends on harborheist-a2ug.14 (uses the "zone" toast category for the prompt toast).

PROBLEM: the world-space zone cue (TASK 29.1, updateZoneCue, init.client.lua:5704-5810 — bobbing arrow + pulsing ring over your FishingZone) self-destructs the instant onboarding.HasCaughtFirstFish flips true, by design ("progress-gated, never dismiss-gated"). But a player CAN wander off after their first catch — mid-session distraction, chasing another dock, following a boat — and their next out-of-zone cast earns ONLY a text toast (FishingService:92 "Stand in a fishing zone at your dock!"). No spatial re-guidance ever returns, even after repeated lost casts.

FIX: track consecutive out-of-zone cast refusals client-side (the server toast arrives via Notify -> showNotification; simplest reliable hook: increment a counter in the "zone"-category toast path added by a2ug.14, reset on any successful RequestCast i.e. CastState(true)). On the SECOND consecutive refusal, re-arm updateZoneCue(state.dockIndex, false) — it re-attaches to the player dock because zoneCueDockIndex was cleared — AND fire one showOnboardingPrompt("returnToZone", "Follow the arrow back to your glowing zone!", warn) (dismissible via the existing prompt pattern). Destroy the re-armed cue on the next successful cast (CastState(true) handler -> updateZoneCue(state.dockIndex, true) path, or extend setFishState("waiting") edge — implementer picks; the cue-destroy call must reuse destroyZoneCue, never hand-rolled cleanup).

GUARDS: never re-arm while a raid/cast/bite overlay holds the slot (cosmetic but pointless overlap); never re-arm when dockIndex is nil (plaza spawner — updateZoneCue already no-ops); do not resurrect for players mid-raid-opt-in flow who are deliberately away from their dock — the 2-consecutive-refusal threshold already filters incidental one-off stray casts, which is the design intent.

WHY: retention-critical — the first session is where the zone cue exists, but week-1 wandering is where churn happens; re-guidance converts a dead-end error back into a spatial lesson using infrastructure that already exists.

VERIFY (Linux): pure suite + selene + build. STUDIO CHECK (orpl): catch one fish, walk away, cast twice out of zone -> cue reappears + prompt toast; cast successfully in zone -> cue gone, counter reset.
close_reason: Completed: wandering-player re-guidance landed. zoneRefusalHandler counts consecutive 'zone'-category toasts (a2ug.14); on the 2nd consecutive refusal (post-first-catch only, dock required, no cast/bite/raid overlay active) it re-arms updateZoneCue(state.dockIndex, false) + fires one dismissible returnToZone prompt (warn). render() preserves the re-armed cue across state pushes (HasCaughtFirstFish and not zoneCueRearmed); CastState(true) resets the streak + destroys the re-armed cue via updateZoneCue->destroyZoneCue. REVIEW FIX: initial insert landed the block mid-updateZoneCue (truncated its Heartbeat body) — caught by selene unscoped-variable warnings; fixed by completing the original function first. 10 ClientChrome contract assertions. Quality: pure 896/0, selene 0 errors/16 warnings (baseline), rojo build OK.

title: Sound refresh pass: replace Roblox-library placeholder SFX (needs asset pipeline decision)
description:

EVIDENCE: SOUNDS table (init.client.lua:619-633) maps the entire game feel to stock Roblox-library assets with revealing names: castLaunch = "Rubber band sling shot.wav", catchRare = electronicpingshort.wav pitch-shifted 1.3x (the SAME asset as biteAlert), catchLegendary = "HalloweenThunder.wav", buttonTick = "classic click" button.wav. The CODE seams are already perfect — 13 named keys, single playSound funnel, per-call volume/speed — so a future pass swaps SoundIds at one table with zero call-site churn.

title: Mobile landscape: action stack renders primary buttons (FISH/BAG/BOOK) off-screen on short viewports
description:
FOUND during a2ug plan-space review (2026-08-01) — pre-existing bug, not introduced by the epic. Blocks nothing but outranks the polish work: a core action being unreachable is a functional defect, not polish.

EVIDENCE (init.client.lua:5019-5028): the mobile action stack is a ScrollingFrame sized UDim2(0, 64, 0, #ACTIONS * MOBILE_STACK_PITCH) = 490px tall (7 x 70), AnchorPoint(1,1), positioned UDim2(1,-12,1,-MOBILE_STACK_BOTTOM=90), ScrollingEnabled = false. Top edge lands at viewportY - 580. On a short LANDSCAPE phone viewport (~360-414px tall; the R3 audit #7 aquarium-panel fix at :3186-3208 explicitly acknowledges short landscape as a supported mode), the top edge is at -166 to -220 — the stack clips off-screen and, because the layout is VerticalAlignment.Bottom with LayoutOrder ascending, the TOP items vanish: FISH (LayoutOrder 1), then BAG, then BOOK. The single most-used button in the game becomes invisible and untouchable in the orientation a player naturally rotates to while watching their bobber. Nothing in the stack re-fits on ViewportSize change (contrast with fitAquariumPanelHeight, which does).

FIX (decided in plan space): make the stack height viewport-aware — recompute on ViewportSize change (bind exactly like fitAquariumPanelHeight :3197-3207): maxStackH = viewportY - MOBILE_STACK_BOTTOM - SAFE_TOP - TOAST_HOST guard margin (suggest 8 + the 300px toast host only if toasts would overlap; simpler: viewportY - MOBILE_STACK_BOTTOM - SAFE_TOP - 8). When #ACTIONS * MOBILE_STACK_PITCH <= maxStackH (portrait, tablets): keep current fixed size and ScrollingEnabled=false — ZERO behavior change where nothing is broken. When it exceeds maxStackH (short landscape): clamp size to maxStackH AND set ScrollingEnabled=true so all 7 buttons remain reachable; keep ScrollBarThickness 0 (already set) and bottom alignment so FISH... wait — with VerticalAlignment.Bottom the FIRST items clip top; when scrolling enables, initial CanvasPosition must be 0 so FISH is visible FIRST (top items are the primary actions; scroll reveals BOAT/HELP-last items downward). Alternatively switch to VerticalAlignment.Top when clamped — implementer verifies whichever yields FISH-visible-at-top with no initial scroll.

CONSIDERATIONS: (a) updateOnboardingPromptOffset (TASK 28.2, :5110-5141) derives prompt position from the FULL stack content height (#ACTIONS * pitch) — after clamping, the prompt offset for short screens should derive from the CLAMPED visible height; its existing short-landscape clamp partially masks this today, but fix the source: expose the clamped stack height and read it there. (b) TouchTargets.spec: 60px holders unchanged — no spec impact. (c) When harborheist-a2ug.13 lands its corner "?" button it does NOT touch the stack; when the desktop HELP chip lands the mobile stack count is unchanged; so .13 and this bead are conflict-free.

WHY P1: core-loop input unreachable in a supported orientation = churn-grade defect for mobile players (the platform this UI hyper-optimizes for, per the device-profile comment at :42).

VERIFY (Linux): pure suite + selene + build. STUDIO CHECK (rswb): iPhone-SE-landscape-class viewport (~667x375): all 7 buttons reachable (FISH visible at top without scrolling); portrait unchanged (no scroll); rotation both ways re-fits; prompt never overlaps stack or HUD.
notes: 2026-08-01 audit correction (GoldenEagle-Jul31): FILE-LEVEL stale evidence — this bug is ALREADY FIXED in-tree. The stack clamps to the viewport via layoutMobileStack (~:5100-5160, markers harborheist-hqn1 + harborheist-xrfp): height clamped, 44px touch-target floor (MIN_TOUCH_TARGET/MIN_SCALE), scrolling enabled when clamping, re-fits on ViewportSize change. Committed and present at HEAD. Original audit sampled the stack CONSTRUCTION site (:5019-5028 fixed 490px) instead of the layout function that now owns sizing. Closing as already-fixed; Studio confirmation of the clamp behavior stays on the rswb visual-QA checklist.
close_reason: Already fixed in-tree by harborheist-hqn1/harborheist-xrfp (layoutMobileStack viewport clamp + 44px floor + scroll fallback). Audit error: stale file-level evidence; verified committed at HEAD.

title: Server notify colors: discovery-gold token + semantic color resolution in Remotes.notify
description:
REVISED 2026-08-01 (plan-space review): semantic map moved into UIPalette.lua (pure RGB data, lune-requireable) instead of Remotes.lua (requires game services = untestable headless); added reward key after finding QuestService:105 quest-complete gold.

BACKGROUND: EPIC 36 (nk22) made UIPalette.lua the single source of truth for the 24 base UI colors, and the CLIENT reads Theme.color.* tokens exclusively. The SERVER never migrated: ~49 remotes.notify/Remotes.notify calls across 10 files pass raw Color3.fromRGB literals, 8 of which are OFF-palette: warn (255,170,80)x20 vs palette warn (255,184,64); error (255,120,120)x12 vs bad (255,92,92); success (130,255,130)x10 vs money (134,239,172); info (120,220,255)x4 vs accentSoft (120,190,255); discovery/reward gold (255,215,0)x3 has NO token (FishingService:490 species discovery, QuestService:105 quest complete, CollectionService:278 milestone claim). Two call sites coincidentally match the palette exactly (perfect-cast 134,239,172 = money; good-cast 120,190,255 = accentSoft) — proof the intent was always palette colors. Every player-facing toast flows through these, so this drift is the single most visible color-consistency bug in the game.

SCOPE (foundation only; call-site migration is harborheist-a2ug.3): (1) Add base token UIPalette.colors.discovery = {r=255,g=215,b=0} — documents the gold already in use; distinct from quest (255,205,92) because discovery/reward is a celebration moment deserving its own premium gold. (2) Add semantic alias map UIPalette.notifyColorNames = { warn="warn", error="bad", success="money", info="accentSoft", discovery="discovery", reward="discovery" } — pure string->string data so test/pure_specs/Contrast.spec.lua can pin it under lune: every alias resolves via UIPalette.color() and meets WCAG AA on surface (mirror the existing audited-colors block). success->money (not good) because money mint IS the cash-gain color used in HUD +$ floaters/claim green — economic success reads as one color language. reward aliases discovery: quest-complete and species-discovery are the same celebration register. (3) src/server/Remotes.lua: extend Remotes.notify(player, message, colorOrKey, category) to accept EITHER a Color3 (legacy passthrough — REQUIRED permanently, the rarity-colored catch toast at FishingService:495-507 passes dynamic Color3 from GameConfig.Rarities) OR a semantic string key resolved via UIPalette. Unknown key: fall back to accentSoft + warn() once. Resolution stays SERVER-side so the wire format (Color3) is unchanged and all clients benefit.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES: (a) pure call-site migration with no helper — no enforcement, drift guaranteed to return; (b) deriving color from toast category — categories drive client chip labels/variants and several calls intentionally pair warn color with info-ish categories; keep the two axes independent; (c) map in Remotes.lua — untestable headless (original filing, corrected).

SAFETY: server services already require ReplicatedStorage.Shared modules; UIPalette top level is pure RGB tables = lune-safe per Contrast.spec comments.

VERIFY (Linux): pure suite green (Contrast.spec now pins the token + 6 aliases); rojo build. No Studio needed (server-side only).
close_reason: Completed: (1) Added UIPalette.colors.discovery = {r=255,g=215,b=0}. (2) Added discovery to Contrast.spec.lua statusColors array (passes WCAG AA 3:1 on all dark surfaces). (3) Extended Remotes.notify with NOTIFY_COLORS map accepting semantic string keys (warn, error, success, info, discovery) resolving to UIPalette tokens, with unknown-key fallback to accentSoft + warn(). Backward compatible — existing Color3 calls work unchanged. Tests: 607 passed/0 failed. Selene: 0 errors. Committed + pushed. Call-site migration is a2ug.3 (child).

title: Migrate ~46 server notify() call sites to semantic colors + fill missing toast categories
description:
REVISED 2026-08-01 (plan-space review): added explicit EXCLUSIONS and reward-key routing after code re-verification.

Depends on harborheist-a2ug.2 (helper must exist first). MIGRATION TABLE (only remotes.notify / Remotes.notify call sites with RAW literals — WorldBuilder part colors and world geometry fromRGB literals are OUT OF SCOPE): (255,170,80) x20 -> "warn"; (255,120,120) x12 -> "error"; (130,255,130) x10 -> "success"; (120,220,255) x4 -> "info"; (255,200,100) x1 (RaidService:858 failed-raid victim) -> "warn"; (120,200,255) x1 (RaidService:988 raid-waters entry) -> "info"; (134,239,172) x1 (FishingService:311 perfect cast) -> "success" (exact palette money already); (120,190,255) x1 (FishingService:313 good cast) -> "info" (exact accentSoft).

GOLD SITES — route by SEMANTICS, not color: FishingService:490 species discovery -> "discovery" (keeps "discovery" category); QuestService:105 quest complete -> "reward" (keeps "quest" category); CollectionService:278 milestone claim -> "reward" AND gains the "discovery" category (chip NEW! fits a collection celebration; today it has no category = INFO chip).

EXPLICIT EXCLUSIONS (do not touch): the catch toast at FishingService:495-507 passes rarityColor — a dynamic Color3 looked up from GameConfig.Rarities. That is ALREADY single-sourced and correct; the legacy Color3 passthrough in Remotes.notify exists for exactly this case. Any other site passing a computed Color3 variable (not a literal) is out of scope.

SECOND-ORDER FIX in the same pass — missing categories: many calls pass NO category, so the client renders the default INFO chip + 3.6s info duration regardless of severity (CATEGORY_TO_VARIANT drives duration: error 6s, warning 4.5s, info 3.6s). While touching each site, add the correct EXISTING category where absent. Guidance (category must match message semantics; duration follows variant): rate-limit / hands-full / rod-too-weak fishing refusals (FishingService:52,79,98,214,261) -> "cast"; left-zone + bite-timeout + slip-away (FishingService:206,243,339,358,398) -> "missed"; aquarium full/locked/no-fish (AquariumService:47,49,170,173; FishInventoryService:76,81,214) -> "economy" or "lock" as fits; sold/stored confirmations (FishInventoryService:146,235; AquariumService:192,194) -> "economy"; shop errors + purchase success (ShopService:72,76,126) -> "economy"; boat messages (BoatService:450,471; init.server.lua:127) -> "info"; dock-full (init.server.lua:182) -> "info". DO NOT invent new categories here — EXCEPTION: skip FishingService:92 (not_in_zone) entirely; it belongs to harborheist-a2ug.14 which creates the new "zone" category atomically with its client tables.

WHY THIS MATTERS: toasts are the primary system-to-player channel; pre-launch, literal-RGB drift vs one design-token language is exactly the amateur-vs-premium gap the operator asked to close, and correct categories give warnings/errors their proper 4.5s/6s dwell instead of vanishing at info speed.

VERIFY (Linux): rg proof — zero Color3.fromRGB remaining in any notify call (dynamic rarityColor exempt); pure suite + selene + rojo build green. STUDIO CHECK (orpl pass): trigger one toast of each migrated color; confirm warn/error/success/info/discovery now match the HUD/panel palette family.

Added missing toast categories to ~25 calls (cast, missed, economy, lock, info, discovery). Fixed FishInventoryService notify() wrapper to pass category (was dropped). rg verification: zero Color3.fromRGB remaining in any notify call. Tests: 607 passed/0 failed. Selene stable. Committed + pushed.

title: Bite-wait engagement: elapsed-time affordance on FISH button + first-wait expectation setting
description:
REVISED 2026-08-01 (plan-space review): verified SOUNDS.biteAlert IS already wired on BiteEvent (init.client.lua:7112, harborheist-6qyq) — no sound work needed here; do not re-audit.

PROBLEM: after RequestCast the server picks a uniform random bite delay of 2.0-6.0s (FishingService BITE_MIN_DELAY/BITE_MAX_DELAY). During that window the FISH button enters the "waiting" state (TASK 22.1 state machine, init.client.lua:5593-5690): desktop shows static "WAITING" with a slow stroke pulse; MOBILE shows literally "..." with zero context. New players have no idea how long a bite takes, repeatedly mash F (earning only the shake animation, TASK 22.2), and some conclude the button is broken. This is the longest recurring dead moment in the core loop and it currently communicates nothing.

DESIGN (decided during audit — implement as specified): (1) Desktop: animate the ellipsis — cycle "WAITING", "WAITING.", "WAITING..", "WAITING..." at ~0.4s cadence while fishState == "waiting". renderFishButton is idempotent and state-push-driven by design; drive the ellipsis from a lightweight task.spawn loop gated on fishState == "waiting", NOT per state push, and never fight renderFishButton ownership of label text outside waiting. (2) Mobile: hero stays "...", the key footnote label (captured per stack-button construction ~:5176-5210; store it in actionButtons like actionButtons.fish_label) animates "WAIT", "WAIT.", "WAIT..", "WAIT..." in the same cadence loop — the footnote normally shows the key letter "F", which on mobile is only a cross-platform footnote (m32r), so temporarily demoting it is safe. (3) First-wait expectation: on the first cast of a session where onboarding.HasCaughtFirstFish is false, fire showOnboardingPrompt("firstWait", "A fish usually bites within a few seconds — stay ready!", warn) and dismissOnboardingPrompt("firstWait") the moment BiteEvent arrives; ties into the existing dismissedPrompts pattern (TASK 9.2, :6030-6075), session-scoped, zero server changes.

EXPLICITLY REJECTED (do not re-litigate without new data): (a) progress bar / shrinking ring / elapsed-seconds counter implying ETA — the client deliberately does NOT know the server-picked delay (anti-exploit surface), any affordance implying a deadline would mislead, and counting seconds invites threshold frustration; dots are calmer and match the cozy aesthetic; (b) fake-out bobber dips / nibble animations — trains players to distrust the real BiteEvent signal, the worst possible lesson in a timing game; (c) cancel-cast button — cancellation already exists implicitly (walk out of the zone, FishingService:206) and a UI cancel invites accidental taps.

VERIFY (Linux): selene/luau-analyze clean, pure suite, rojo build. STUDIO CHECK (orpl): cast on desktop + mobile; ellipsis animates; mobile footnote animates WAIT; first-cast prompt appears then clears on bite; no pulse-tween restart churn on state pushes (fishPulseMode guard intact).
notes: 2026-08-01 fresh-eyes review (GoldenEagle-Jul31): three bugs found in the ORIGINAL a2ug.4 implementation (delivered inside c72dfa0), all fixed in 512961a and pushed. (1) CRITICAL: CastState handler assigned fishState directly (:7095/:7186) instead of setFishState, so the waiting-dots loop + firstWait hook never fired on the primary cast path — both now route through setFishState with the bite-ready guard preserved. (2) The stage-1 rescue's casting branch ran dismissOnboardingPrompt('firstCast') which hides the widget unconditionally, killing the firstWait prompt <1s after it appeared — now marks dismissed without hiding when firstWait owns the widget. (3) stopWaitingDots restored the footnote with a hardcoded 'F' — now captures + restores the original text. Gates: 607/607 pure specs, selene 17 (baseline), build OK. Lesson recorded: fishState has exactly two sanctioned writers — the declaration and setFishState; any future raw write is a bug by definition.
close_reason: Already implemented in codebase: (1) startWaitingDots/stopWaitingDots loop animates ellipsis at 0.4s cadence while fishState=='waiting' (lines 5582-5616); (2) fish_label/fish_footnote captured at button construction (lines 5094,5099) — desktop hero cycles WAITING..., mobile footnote cycles WAIT...; (3) first-wait onboarding prompt via showOnboardingPrompt('firstWait') gated on !HasCaughtFirstFish + firstWaitArmed flag (lines 5622-5644). All three components verified by code reading. No changes needed.

title: Cast overlay: show the concrete perfect-hit luck bonus instead of vague BONUS LUCK
description:
REVISED 2026-08-01 (plan-space review): exact config keys pinned and the design SIMPLIFIED — the bonus values are flat config (gear-independent), so the subtitle is set ONCE at overlay construction, not per cast.

PROBLEM: the cast timing overlay subtitle reads "CENTER HIT  •  BONUS LUCK" (makeOverlayFrame call, init.client.lua:5400-5402, built once at startup). The player is asked to skill-hit a narrow zone for a reward that is never quantified anywhere in the UI. Opaque mechanics read as decorative; quantified ones read as systems worth mastering.

FIX: set the subtitle at construction from GameConfig.MiniGame.accuracyLuckBonus (GameConfig.lua:62-66: perfect = 25, good = 12, ok = 0 — VERIFIED in code), e.g. "PERFECT +25 LUCK  •  GOOD +12 LUCK". Read the table fields, never hand-copied literals, and cite FishingService TASK 14.24 (Decision C, ~:300-320: effective zone = base + (luckBonus/maxLuck) x (ceiling - base)) in a comment so future balance retunes stay honest automatically.

DESIGN DECISION (revised): show the MARGINAL cast-timing prizes only — NOT a rod+bait+cast total (original filing). The timing bar buys exactly accuracyLuckBonus; rod/bait luck are already-owned stats not at stake in this moment, and showing a total would conflate owned stats with the prize on offer. The "luck" unit is already established with players via shop row subtexts ("+25 luck").

NO PER-CAST UPDATE NEEDED: accuracyLuckBonus is flat (no gear scaling — the rod only changes the bite-zone base, not the luck table), so a static construction-time set is exact. If a future balance pass makes the bonus gear-dependent, this bead gains a sibling to refresh the subtitle on CastState(true).

WHY THIS MATTERS: the cast minigame is the first skill expression a new player meets; making its payoff explicit converts a confusing bar into a legible risk/reward moment at near-zero cost.

VERIFY (Linux): pure suite + selene + build; confirm displayed numbers equal GameConfig values. STUDIO CHECK (orpl): subtitle renders on one line on mobile without clipping.
close_reason: Completed: Cast overlay subtitle now reads from GameConfig.MiniGame.accuracyLuckBonus.perfect/.good at construction time instead of vague 'BONUS LUCK'. Pure suite + selene (17 warnings, no new) + rojo build all green. Committed b1a78aa.

title: Reveal card: NEW DISCOVERY ribbon; absorb the duplicate discovery toast
description:
REVISED 2026-08-01 (plan-space review): suppression moved SERVER-SIDE after finding an ordering race in the original client-side design. The original plan had the client filter the discovery toast when the card was visible — but FishingService:490 fires the notify INSIDE handleSubmitCatchInput BEFORE returning the invoke result, and Roblox delivers the RemoteEvent before the InvokeServer response, so the toast ALWAYS arrives before the card exists. Client-side suppression would have missed 100% of the time.

Depends on harborheist-a2ug.2 (uses the new UIPalette discovery gold token for the ribbon).

PROBLEM: a first-ever catch of a species produces TWO competing celebration surfaces at the same instant: the reveal card (TASK 22.4, showRevealCard, init.client.lua:6276+) — which gives NO hint the catch is a collection first — plus a separate server toast "New species discovered: X!" (FishingService:490, category "discovery"). Two surfaces saying adjacent things at once dilutes both; the card is the premium moment and should absorb the discovery signal.

SERVER HALF: in the FishingService catch-success path (~:470-508): (1) track session.catchesThisSession = (session.catchesThisSession or 0) + 1 on the session runtime fields (same table family as session.casting etc.; NOT persisted — it resets each session, matching the client catchesThisSession counter that drives the card condition); (2) add isNewDiscovery = true to the invoke result table when the discovery block fires (additive field; pure specs should pin the new key); (3) SUPPRESS the discovery notify when the client will render a card for this catch: rarity is Rare/Epic/Legendary OR session.catchesThisSession == 1 (mirrors the client card condition at onMinigameTap ~:6540: catchesThisSession == 1 or Rare+). Keep firing the notify for all other discoveries (Common/Uncommon re-session catches) — it remains their only discovery surface. Update the comment near :490 to explain the suppression rule so future balance work does not reintroduce the duplicate.

CLIENT HALF: (1) onMinigameTap passes result.isNewDiscovery into showRevealCard; (2) showRevealCard(speciesId, rarity, value, isNew) renders a small ribbon/tag reading "NEW DISCOVERY" in UIPalette discovery gold, distinct from the rarity tag (card is 160px tall — audit spacing; likely shift the species-name label down ~10px or overlay the ribbon on the rarity top bar); (3) NO client toast filtering — the suppression is exact at the source.

EDGE CASES: first-session catch (client card condition catchesThisSession == 1) that is also a discovery -> card + ribbon, toast suppressed server-side (counter == 1), still exactly one celebration. Common/Uncommon discovery on a later session catch -> toast fires, no card (rarity gate), no ribbon. Rare+ discovery -> card + ribbon, no toast. Client and server session counters can drift only if a catch succeeds server-side but the client result is lost (disconnect) — worst case the toast fires AND the card shows once, the pre-fix behavior; acceptable.

VERIFY (Linux): pure suite (add result-key + suppression pins to FishingServiceLogic.spec), selene, build. STUDIO CHECK (orpl): catch a brand-new Rare+ species -> card with gold ribbon, NO separate toast; first catch of a session that is also new -> card + ribbon; new Common species later in session -> toast only.
close_reason: Completed: Server suppresses discovery toast when card-eligible (Rare+ or first session catch via session.catchesThisSession counter). Adds isNewDiscovery to catch invoke result. Client showRevealCard renders gold NEW DISCOVERY ribbon with 10px content shift. 11 source-contract specs added. Gates: 629/0 pure, selene 0 errors, build OK. Committed da9195b.

title: Shop clarity: category group headers (RODS / BAIT / TANK / DEFENSE / DOCK)
description:
PROBLEM: the shop renders 19 upgrade rows as ONE flat scrolling list (SHOP_CATALOG built at init.client.lua:4083-4101 via addCatalog order bases 0/10/20/30/40/50, rows from buildShopRow :4144). The only grouping signal is a 46px kind chip on each row (KIND_META :4103-4110). Six interleaved upgrade tracks with no section structure means scanning costs grow with every tier purchased — and the LOCK and ALARM tracks are conceptually one category (defense) presented as two.

FIX: insert section header labels into shopList between groups — RODS, BAIT, TANK, DEFENSE (lock + alarm rows under one header), DOCK.

SIMPLIFICATION (verified 2026-08-01 plan-space review): NO re-spacing needed. Rows use LayoutOrder = orderBase + level and level starts at 1, so the exact base values 0, 10, 20, 30, 50 are UNUSED — headers slot directly into them (RODS=0, BAIT=10, TANK=20, DEFENSE=30, DOCK=50) with correct integer LayoutOrder and zero changes to the existing order math. Alarm rows (41-43) sort under DEFENSE (30) naturally; keep the per-row KIND_META chips so lock/alarm rows remain visually distinct under the merged header.

Header styling: Theme.type.fonts.bold xs, text.tertiary, left-aligned, ~22px tall — matching the existing TARGETS / LIVE-WELL BREAKDOWN section labels in raid/aquarium panels (consistent in-game header language). Non-interactive: not registered with KeyboardNav (it only takes interactive elements, desktop-only registrations).

CONSIDERATIONS: shopList rows are built once at startup (buildShopRow loop :4298-4300) and refreshShop only mutates buttons — headers build once too, no re-render cost. Skeleton rows (harborheist-9yli) unaffected. Keep the flat scroll (no collapsible sections — over-engineering for 19 rows).

WHY: the shop is the progression engine of the game; its legibility directly drives upgrade comprehension and spend confidence. Grouping is the cheapest structural win.

VERIFY (Linux): pure suite (TouchTargets.spec unaffected — headers are labels not buttons), selene, build. STUDIO CHECK (rswb visual-QA pass): five headers in correct positions; DEFENSE covers lock I-III + alarm I-III; scroll intact on mobile sheet.
close_reason: Completed: Shop category group headers (RODS/BAIT/TANK/DEFENSE/DOCK). Multiplied catalog order bases x10, added buildSectionHeader(), placed 5 headers between row groups via UIListLayout sort. DEFENSE covers both lock+alarm. Unblocks a2ug.8/9/10. Commit eed6722, pushed. Quality gates: 607 pure specs pass, build OK, selene 0 new warnings, remote arity + overlay router contracts hold.

title: Shop clarity: current-to-next delta subtext on the purchasable row
description:
Depends on harborheist-a2ug.7 (both touch shop row construction; serialize to avoid conflicts).

PROBLEM: itemSubText (:4120-4144) describes each tier in isolation ("+25 luck", "Holds 35 fish • +15% income"). The question a player actually has — "what do I GAIN over what I own?" — requires mentally diffing two rows. Stripe-level polish answers the asked question, not the adjacent one.

FIX: for the single purchasable row per track (entry.level == currentLevel + 1, identified in refreshShop :4231-4300), rewrite the subtext as a delta: rod "+10 luck -> +25 luck"; tank "20 -> 35 fish • +0% -> +15% income"; lock "60s/120s -> 90s/90s"; alarm "3s -> 5s stun"; dock "+0% -> +20% income • Lamp". All inputs are already client-side (GameConfig.Rods/Baits/AquariumUpgradeTiers/Upgrades.Lock/Upgrades.Alarm/DockUpgradeTiers + state.rodLevel/baitLevel/upgradeLevel/lockLevel/alarmLevel/dockLevel). Refresh re-derives on every state push (refreshShop already runs on StateChanged), so no caching staleness. Keep the absolute description for OWNED and LOCKED rows (delta is meaningless there); only the actionable row speaks in deltas.

CONSIDERATIONS: mobile row height is 74px with a 30px-tall wrapped subtext label (:4172-4183) — a "x -> y" string is SHORTER than most current descriptions, so no layout risk; still set TextTruncate as backstop. This is the companion piece to the harborheist-cl05 unaffordable-shortfall messaging (the row now says what you gain AND what you lack).

VERIFY (Linux): pure suite + selene + build; unit-check delta strings against GameConfig tables by hand. STUDIO CHECK (rswb): own Basic rod -> Steel row reads "+10 -> +25 luck"; max a track -> no delta anywhere on that track.
close_reason: Completed: Added itemDeltaSubText function showing current->next deltas for all 6 upgrade kinds. buildShopRow captures subtext label; refreshShop sets delta on purchasable row, absolute on OWNED/LOCKED. 8 source-contract specs. selene 0 errors, 17 warnings baseline. Build OK. 5 pre-existing ClientChrome failures from a2ug.13, not this change. Committed 2265b6b.

title: Shop clarity: collapse maxed tracks into a single MAXED summary row
description:
Depends on harborheist-a2ug.7 (section headers must exist so a collapsed track still shows its group).

PROBLEM: a track at max tier still renders 3-4 rows, all with dead OWNED buttons (refreshShop sets Active=false, surface.elevated bg, text.tertiary — pixel-consistent with genuinely LOCKED rows, which harborheist-cl05 called out as a readability hazard). Late-game players scroll a 19-row list where most rows can never carry information again.

FIX: when currentLevel == max tier for a track, hide the per-tier rows of that track and show ONE summary row: "[kind chip] <TOP-TIER NAME> — MAXED (+25 luck)" — display the name of the OWNED top tier (e.g. Golden Rod at rod level 3), read from the same GameConfig table at index currentLevel, not a literal — with the kind color chip and no buy button. Rows are persistent instances (built once), so implement as Visible toggling inside refreshShop plus one lazily-created summary row per track; zero rebuild cost. DEFENSE header (from a2ug.7): lock and alarm collapse independently; hide the header only when BOTH are maxed (and apply the same header-visibility rule to any fully-maxed section).

EDGE CASE: profile downgrade via data migration/sanitize (Capacity recompute, N6) could un-max a track — Visible toggles re-evaluate every refreshShop call, so this falls out for free.

WHY: progressive disclosure of dead UI is a hallmark of premium apps; the shop list should shrink as the player completes it, ending at roughly 6 summary rows.

VERIFY (Linux): pure suite + selene + build. STUDIO CHECK (rswb): max a track -> one MAXED row showing the top-tier name; section header hides when all its tracks maxed; new player sees zero MAXED rows.
close_reason: Completed: Maxed tracks collapse to a single MAXED summary row. (1) buildSectionHeader now returns label + stores kinds array for section-level visibility. (2) shopMaxLevels computed from SHOP_CATALOG; getOrCreateSummaryRow lazily creates summary rows with kind chip + top-tier name + MAXED badge. (3) refreshShop toggles per-tier row.Visible and summary row.Visible; section headers hide when all kinds in section are maxed (DEFENSE: lock+alarm both maxed). Forward-declared shopMaxLevels and getOrCreateSummaryRow for selene. 5 source-contract specs added. Quality: pure 649/1 (pre-existing ClientChrome fail), selene 0 errors/17 warnings, build OK. Studio check (rswb) deferred.

description: In src/client/init.client.lua:874, fishDisplayName(fish) accesses fish.SpeciesId without checking if fish is nil. If the carried fish list contains a nil entry, the inventory render crashes. Add a nil guard returning a safe fallback.

title: BUG P1: startRaidMinigame called before its local-function definition (nil global — raid minigame never starts)
close_reason: Completed: dropped 'local' from startRaidMinigame definition (init.client.lua ~line 2309) so it assigns to a global instead of a file-level local. The function was called at line ~2152 inside renderRaidTargets' attempt.Activated callback (defined BEFORE the local-function definition at ~2309) with no forward declaration — so the closure captured a nil global and the raid minigame could never start. Pre-existing bug since 71f95f9 (raid UI panel), verified present in pre-hvfh.3.1 code; raid E2E bead (pe9a.8) still open so it went unnoticed. luau-analyze flagged it as FunctionUnused (the local was never referenced). Fix: 'local function startRaidMinigame' -> 'function startRaidMinigame' (global assignment); the callback resolves the global at runtime — by the time the RAID button is clicked, file load has already executed the global assignment. A forward-declaration + local approach was also attempted but clobbered by concurrent WildCat WIP; the global approach is valid for a single-file client script (no shadowing local exists, no security concern in server-authoritative client). luau-analyze: 1 FunctionUnused warning -> 0. Pure-spec gate PASSED. Partial-staged 1-line change.

title: P1: formatRaidTime forward-ref — raid target countdown rows crash render (nil global)
description: init.client.lua:2351 calls formatRaidTime() inside renderRaidTargets, but the local function is declared at :4084 — ~1600 lines LATER. Luau binds locals lexically at the definition site, so the :2351 call reads a nil GLOBAL forever. Whenever a raid target row has unavailableSeconds > 0 (locked/raid_protection/victim_cooldown), renderRaidTargets errors ('attempt to call a nil value'), the task.spawn thread dies, remaining target rows never render, and pollRaidTargets re-crashes every 3s. Same bug class as harborheist-7w5a / ajoy (load-order trap), but a runtime-caller variant so it doesn't kill the client on boot — only when the raid panel renders a countdown row. Pure specs don't load init.client.lua so the suite can't catch it; luau-analyze output is drowned in Roblox-global false positives. Found in round-2 UI/UX audit (RainyLynx-Jul26). Fix: move the formatRaidTime definition above renderRaidTargets (next to formatCash).
close_reason: Fixed: moved formatRaidTime definition from :4084 to :325 (before earliest caller renderRaidTargets :2363). luau-analyze confirms: HEAD flagged 'Unknown global formatRaidTime' at :2351 + LocalShadow at :4084; after fix 0 mentions, 0 SyntaxErrors, TypeErrors 645->644 (one real error removed, none added). Pure suite 100/100 + coverage gate green. Reservation released.

- Wide-screen layouts use space efficiently
- No conflicts with Roblox default shortcuts

- Keyboard shortcuts system
- Context menus for right-click actions
- Wide-screen layout optimization

## Dependencies

- Should complete after: EPIC 36 (tokens)
- Independent of: EPIC 37, EPIC 38, EPIC 39
- Elevated from P2 to P1 due to high impact for power users

Several mobile buttons are below the 44px minimum touch target guideline:
- Inventory action buttons (SELL/STORE): 38px on mobile
- Some panel controls: 32-36px
- Close buttons: 26-32px on mobile

**WHAT TO DO:**
1. Audit all buttons in init.client.lua for mobile touch target sizes
2. Increase any buttons below 44px to 44px minimum
3. Ensure touch target includes padding (visual size can be smaller, but hit area must be 44px)
4. Test on actual mobile devices (or Roblox mobile emulator)

**SPECIFIC LOCATIONS TO CHECK:**
- Line ~1934-1949: inventory row SELL/STORE buttons (currently 44px mobile, 38px desktop - OK)
- Line ~1394-1405: panel close buttons (currently 44px mobile - OK)
- Line ~1101-1110: sellStorePrompt close button (currently 36px mobile - NEEDS FIX)

- Line ~2602-2609: shop buyButton (currently 44px mobile - OK)

**IMPLEMENTATION:**
```lua
-- For buttons that need larger touch targets but smaller visual size:
local btn = makeButton(parent, {
  Size = UDim2.new(0, 32, 0, 32), -- visual size
  -- Add invisible padding via UIPadding or larger frame
})
-- OR just increase the button size to 44x44
```

**VERIFICATION:**
- All mobile buttons have ≥ 44px touch targets
- Visual design still looks good (may need layout adjustments)

title: Add keyboard navigation (Tab order, Enter/Space activation)
description:
**CONTEXT:**
Desktop users cannot navigate the UI with keyboard alone. There's no Tab order, no focus indicators, and no way to activate buttons with Enter/Space.

**WHAT TO DO:**
1. Add NextSelectionDown/Up/Left/Right properties to all interactive elements
2. Ensure Tab key cycles through interactive elements in logical order
3. Ensure Enter/Space activates focused buttons
4. Add focus indicators (visible outline on focused elements)

**IMPLEMENTATION:**
```lua
-- For each button/interactive element:
btn.NextSelectionDown = nextButton
btn.NextSelectionUp = previousButton
btn.NextSelectionLeft = leftButton
btn.NextSelectionRight = rightButton

-- Add focus indicator
local focusIndicator = Instance.new("UIStroke")
focusIndicator.Color = UI.accent
focusIndicator.Thickness = 2
focusIndicator.Transparency = 1 -- hidden by default
focusIndicator.Parent = btn

btn.Focused:Connect(function()
  focusIndicator.Transparency = 0
end)

btn.FocusLost:Connect(function()
  focusIndicator.Transparency = 1
end)
```

**LOGICAL TAB ORDER:**
1. HUD (cash card, carry pill)
2. Action bar buttons (FISH, BAG, BOOK, TANK, QUESTS, RAID, BOAT)
3. Panel content (when panel is open)
4. Panel close button

**VERIFICATION:**
- Tab cycles through all interactive elements
- Enter/Space activates focused buttons
- Focus indicator is visible and clear
- Tab order is logical (top-to-bottom, left-to-right)

title: Verify and fix color contrast ratios (WCAG AA)
description:
**CONTEXT:**
Many text colors may not meet WCAG AA contrast requirements:
- UI.textDim (148, 163, 184) on UI.bg (13, 20, 31) = ~4.2:1 (FAILS AA for normal text)
- UI.textFaint (100, 116, 139) on UI.bg (13, 20, 31) = ~2.8:1 (FAILS AA)
- UI.text (238, 243, 250) on UI.bg (13, 20, 31) = ~13:1 (PASSES AAA)

**WHAT TO DO:**
1. Audit all text/background color combinations
2. Calculate contrast ratios using WCAG formula
3. Adjust colors to meet 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text (18px+ or bold 14px+)
4. Update UI semantic tokens with accessible colors

**WCAG CONTRAST FORMULA:**
```
Relative luminance L = 0.2126 * R + 0.7152 * G + 0.0722 * B
(where R, G, B are linearized: if sRGB <= 0.03928 then sRGB/12.92 else ((sRGB+0.055)/1.055)^2.4)
Contrast ratio = (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05) where L1 is lighter
```

**SUGGESTED FIXES:**
- UI.text.secondary: lighten from (148, 163, 184) to (168, 183, 204) → ~5.2:1
- UI.text.tertiary: lighten from (100, 116, 139) to (130, 146, 169) → ~3.8:1 (OK for large text)

**VERIFICATION:**
- All text meets WCAG AA (4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large)
- Use online contrast checker to verify
- Test with color blindness simulators
- Ensure visual design still looks good
notes: Implemented by RainyLynx-Jul26. IMPORTANT: the bead's stated contrast figures were INCORRECT — I computed exact WCAG ratios (hand-verified). Actual: textDim(148,163,184) on bg/surface/surfaceHi = 7.20/6.53/5.56:1 -> ALREADY PASSES AA-normal (the bead claimed ~4.2:1 FAIL; wrong). text(238,243,250) = 12.79-16.57:1 (AAA). textFaint(100,116,139) = 3.88/3.52/3.00:1 -> FAILS AA-normal and borderline on surfaceHi. FULL AUDIT of all text/bg combos: text & textDim pass; every colored text (accent 4.82-6.25, accentSoft 7.20-9.33, warn 8.27-10.71, good 6.52-8.44, bad 4.71-6.10, boat 7.43-9.62, purple 5.24-6.79) on dark surfaces PASSES AA-normal; saturated-bg text-bearing buttons use ink (dark) -> PASS; white-on-saturated combos FAIL mathematically but are NOT used in the UI. textFaint usage classification: 12 of 16 usages are NORMAL-sized text (TextSize 9-14, mostly non-bold or bold<14px: empty-state messages at 14px regular, labels at 9-13px) -> all fail AA-normal at the old 3.88:1. FIX (only change needed): textFaint (100,116,139) -> (130,146,169) at init.client.lua:62, giving 5.83/5.29/4.50:1 (AA-normal on all surfaces); hierarchy text>textDim>textFaint preserved (new textFaint still darker than textDim); propagates to Theme.color.text.tertiary alias. Did NOT change textDim (already passes — the bead's suggested textDim lightening would be unnecessary churn). Added test/pure_specs/Contrast.spec.lua: a lune-safe pure-math WCAG regression guard pinning the AA contract (text/textDim/textFaint >=4.5:1 on bg/surface/surfaceHi + hierarchy). Verification: luau-analyze init.client.lua 731->731 (zero new), new spec clean (0 warnings), selene unchanged (0/0/55), rojo build OK, pure suite 104 passed (was 100; +4 new its), coverage gate PASSED. Caveat: not visually verified in Roblox Studio (no Studio on Linux); contrast ratios verified by exact WCAG computation + the new pure spec.
close_reason: Completed: full WCAG audit (bead's figures were wrong — textDim already passes at 7.20:1). Fixed the only real failure: textFaint (100,116,139)->(130,146,169) = 5.83/5.29/4.50:1 AA-normal, hierarchy preserved; propagates to Theme.color.text.tertiary. All other text/bg combos already pass (colored text on dark passes; saturated buttons use ink). Added pure-spec WCAG regression guard. Gates green: luau 731=731, selene unchanged, rojo OK, pure 104 passed, coverage pass. Caveat: not visually verified in Studio (no Studio on Linux); ratios verified by exact math + pure spec.
