title: EPIC 16: Cast-Accuracy Minigame Wiring (CastResult remote)
description:
BACKGROUND: The codebase has TWO separate timing minigames that were both implemented but only ONE was wired end-to-end:

  1. CAST-OVERLAY MINIGAME (client lines 996-1090): Triggered by CastState:FireClient(true, castTime). Shows a marker sweeping across a bar with a green "hit zone". Player clicks to stop it. Fires `CastResult:FireServer(accuracy)`. This measures CAST ACCURACY — did you release at the right moment during the cast windup?

  2. BITE MINIGAME (client lines 1183-1304): Triggered by BiteEvent. Shows a separate ping-pong marker. Player taps to stop it. Fires `SubmitCatchInput({hit=bool})`. This measures REACTION TIMING — did you respond fast enough when the fish bit?

PROBLEM: The cast-overlay minigame was fully built (UI, animation, input handling) but `CastResult` had NO server handler. The accuracy value was fired into the void. Meanwhile, GameConfig.MiniGame.accuracyLuckBonus (perfect=25, good=12, ok=0) was defined but never consumed — a dead config table that was clearly INTENDED to be driven by the cast accuracy.

DESIGN DECISION (user-directed, 2026-07-18): Wire CastResult rather than remove the minigame. The cast-overlay becomes a skill-based luck bonus: a well-timed cast grants a temporary luck boost that improves species rarity on the subsequent catch.

HOW IT WORKS (post-wiring):
  1. Server computes authoritative hit-zone bounds (centered randomly per cast) from RodDefinitions.minigameZoneSize
  2. Server sends bounds + castDeadline to client via CastState
  3. Client renders the zone from server bounds and animates the marker
  4. Player clicks → client sends CastResult with marker position
  5. Server re-derives accuracy tier from marker position vs server-authoritative bounds
  6. Server stores luckBonus on activeBites (consumed by the catch species roll later)

This is NOT the same as the bite minigame's security mitigation (N16's rng:NextNumber > zoneSize check). The cast overlay is a BONUS mechanism, not a gate — you can still catch fish without a good cast, but a good cast shifts the odds.

WHY THIS MATTERS: The fishing loop is the core engagement loop. Right now, casting is a passive wait (castTime delay). The cast-overlay minigame adds active skill expression to the FIRST half of the loop, complementing the bite minigame's reflex test in the second half. This gives players two skill checks per catch instead of one, deepening the moment-to-moment gameplay.

CONSIDERATIONS:
- The server must be authoritative on the hit-zone bounds (not the client) to prevent "always perfect" exploits
- The luckBonus is consumed by FishDefinitions.getRandomInZone's luck parameter, which shifts weights toward rarer species
- accuracyLuckBonus values (25/12/0) are substantial — a "perfect" cast adds 25 luck, equivalent to a Golden Rod (20) + Magic Bait (15) combined. This may need balance tuning post-launch.
- The cast overlay's existing `castHitZone` client variable must be replaced with server-provided bounds

RELATED EXISTING BEADS:
- harborheist-wqw.11 (TASK 14.11: Wire rod minigameZoneSize into client timing minigame) — partially overlaps; this epic subsumes it
- harborheist-fishing-system-rework-h2e.2 (TASK 3.2: Client timing minigame UI) — closed, but only the bite minigame was wired
close_reason: Completed: all 5 children closed — CastResult wiring live, accuracy tuning signed off (docs/ACCURACY_TUNING.md).

title: TASK 16.1: Server sends authoritative hit-zone bounds in CastState
description:
WHAT: Modify FishingService's Cast.OnServerEvent handler to compute per-cast hit-zone bounds from RodDefinitions and send them to the client in the CastState:FireClient call.

The client already expects a 4th argument (a table with hitZoneStart, hitZoneEnd, goodStart, goodEnd) — see init.client.lua:1402-1408. The server just wasn't sending it.

IMPLEMENTATION (partially done — this task completes and verifies it):
  1. Look up rodDef = GameConfig.RodDefinitions[equippedRodLevel]
  2. zoneSize = rodDef.minigameZoneSize or GameConfig.MiniGame.hitZoneWidth (0.3)
  3. goodSize = GameConfig.MiniGame.goodZoneWidth (0.5)
  4. Center the zone randomly: zoneCenter = rng:NextNumber(zoneSize/2, 1 - zoneSize/2)
  5. Compute bounds: hitZoneStart/End, goodStart/End
  6. Send as 4th arg: remotes.CastState:FireClient(player, true, biteDelay, { hitZoneStart=..., ... })
  7. Store bounds on activeBites for later CastResult validation

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] CastState:FireClient includes a 4th table argument with all 5 fields
- [ ] Hit-zone center is randomized per cast (not always center)
- [ ] Zone width matches the equipped rod's minigameZoneSize
- [ ] Bounds stored on activeBites for CastResult validation
- [ ] Client renders the zone from server-provided bounds (not hardcoded 0.35-0.65)

DEPENDS ON: Nothing (config tables already exist)

notes: REOPENED 2026-07-18: fresh-eyes review found TWO bugs in the zone geometry I wrote. (1) perfect/good widths were swapped — config hitZoneWidth=0.3 (narrow) is the inner PERFECT bullseye, goodZoneWidth=0.5 (wide) is the outer GOOD band; I'd mapped them backwards so 'perfect' was EASIER to hit than 'good'. (2) zone overflow: zoneCenter clamped on the INNER band let the WIDER good band overflow [0,1] at track edges (goodStart=-0.10, goodEnd=1.10). FIXED: clamp zoneCenter on the OUTER good band; hitZoneStart/End = inner perfect, goodStart/End = outer good; zone fits in [0,1].

All 4 bounds + castDeadline sent in CastState 3rd arg + stored on activeBites. luau verified.

title: TASK 16.2: Add CastResult server handler — compute accuracy tier, store luckBonus
description:
WHAT: Add a server-side handler for the CastResult RemoteEvent. It receives the client's reported marker position, re-derives the accuracy tier from the server-authoritative bounds (stored on activeBites by TASK 16.1), and stores the resulting luckBonus.

SECURITY: The server must NOT trust the client's claimed accuracy tier. It must re-compute the tier from the raw marker position against its own bounds. A client can lie about where the marker was, but the server clamps the resulting luckBonus to the config-defined maximums.

IMPLEMENTATION:
  remotes.CastResult.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, accuracy)
    -- accuracy is the marker position [0,1] when the player clicked
    local biteData = activeBites[player]
    if not biteData or biteData.castResultReceived then return end
    biteData.castResultReceived = true
    -- Clamp accuracy to [0,1] (client could send out-of-range)
    accuracy = math.clamp(type(accuracy) == "number" and accuracy or 0, 0, 1)
    -- Derive tier from server-authoritative bounds
    local tier
    if accuracy >= biteData.goodStart and accuracy <= biteData.goodEnd then
      tier = "perfect"
    elseif accuracy >= biteData.hitZoneStart and accuracy <= biteData.hitZoneEnd then
      tier = "good"
    else
      tier = "ok"
    end
    biteData.luckBonus = GameConfig.MiniGame.accuracyLuckBonus[tier] or 0
  end)

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] CastResult.OnServerEvent handler registered
- [ ] Handler validates activeBites exists and isn't already processed
- [ ] Marker position clamped to [0,1]
- [ ] Tier derived from server bounds (goodStart/End → perfect, hitZoneStart/End → good, else ok)
- [ ] luckBonus set from GameConfig.MiniGame.accuracyLuckBonus[tier]
- [ ] Client cannot inflate luckBonus by sending a crafted accuracy value

FILES: src/server/FishingService.lua (new handler, after Cast.OnServerEvent block)
DEPENDS ON: TASK 16.1 (needs bounds on activeBites)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] CastResult.OnServerEvent handler registered in FishingService.init
- [ ] Handler validates activeBites[player] exists and castResultReceived == false
- [ ] Marker position clamped to [0,1] (client can't send out-of-range)
- [ ] Tier derived from server bounds: goodStart/End → perfect, hitZoneStart/End → good, else ok
- [ ] luckBonus set from GameConfig.MiniGame.accuracyLuckBonus[tier]
- [ ] Duplicate CastResult submissions ignored (castResultReceived flag)
close_reason: CastResult handler added: clamps accuracy [0,1], re-derives tier from server bounds, sets luckBonus from config, double-fire guard. N16.

title: TASK 16.3: Apply cast-accuracy luckBonus in catch species roll
description:
WHAT: In SubmitCatchInput's catch resolution, add the cast-accuracy luckBonus to the rod+bait luck before calling FishDefinitions.getRandomInZone.

IMPLEMENTATION (one-line change at the existing luck computation):
  -- Before (current):
  local luck = rod.luck + bait.luck
  -- After:
  local luck = rod.luck + bait.luck + (biteData.luckBonus or 0)

This feeds into getRandomInZone's luck parameter, which multiplies each species' CatchWeight by (1 + luck/100 * (rarityOrder - 1)). A "perfect" cast (luckBonus=25) with a Golden Rod (luck=20) + Magic Bait (luck=15) gives total luck=60, which meaningfully shifts the species distribution toward rarer fish.

BALANCE NOTE: The accuracyLuckBonus values (25/12/0) are large relative to rod+bait luck (0-35 combined). This is intentional — cast skill should matter MORE than gear for rarity, rewarding active play. But it may need tuning after playtesting. Track in harborheist-release-prep-mxl.2 (economy balance pass).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] biteData.luckBonus added to the luck variable in SubmitCatchInput
- [ ] A "perfect" cast measurably increases rare-fish odds (verified via test casts)
- [ ] An "ok" cast (luckBonus=0) produces the same odds as before this change
- [ ] luckBonus consumed exactly once (idempotent if handler fires twice)

FILES: src/server/FishingService.lua (SubmitCatchInput handler, ~line 207)
DEPENDS ON: TASK 16.2 (needs luckBonus on activeBites)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] biteData.luckBonus added to luck variable in SubmitCatchInput catch resolution
- [ ] luck = rod.luck + bait.luck + (biteData.luckBonus or 0)
- [ ] Perfect cast measurably increases rare-fish odds vs ok cast (test verified)
- [ ] luckBonus consumed exactly once per cast (cleared after resolution)
- [ ] No behavior change when castResultReceived == false (luckBonus defaults 0)
close_reason: luck = rod.luck + bait.luck + biteData.luckBonus in SubmitCatchInput. Defaults 0. N16.

title: TASK 16.4: Update client cast-overlay to render server-provided hit-zone bounds

  - Set hitZoneFrame.Size = UDim2.new(bounds.hitZoneEnd - bounds.hitZoneStart, 0, 1, 0)
  - Set hitZoneFrame.Position = UDim2.new(bounds.hitZoneStart, 0, 0, 0)
  - Set perfectZoneFrame relative to hitZoneFrame using goodStart/goodEnd
  - When CastResult fires, pass the marker's current X.Scale position as `accuracy`

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] Cast overlay hit-zone width visually matches the equipped rod's minigameZoneSize
- [ ] Perfect zone (brighter green) renders inside the hit zone at server-specified bounds
- [ ] Better rods visibly show a wider target zone
- [ ] Marker position sent to server as a [0,1] float in CastResult

title: P2: Raw server reason strings leak to players on per-fish sell/store failure
description:
Inventory per-fish SELL/STORE handlers (~:1460-1470): on failure they toast 'Could not sell: ' .. result.reason. A fast double-tap produces 'Could not sell: fish_not_found' — raw snake_case server internals. SERVER_NOTIFIED_REASONS suppresses the 3 server-toasted reasons; everything else renders raw. Fix: map known reasons to friendly copy (fish_not_found -> 'That fish is already gone.', rate_limited -> 'Slow down a moment...') with a generic 'That did not work — try again.' fallback.

Found in round-2 UI/UX audit (RainyLynx-Jul26, 2026-07-26). Parent epic: harborheist-ivld:.

title: EPIC 17: Dock Upgrade Tree Feature
description:
BACKGROUND: The DockUpgradeTiers config table (GameConfig.lua:105-110) defines 4 tiers with incomeMultiplier (1.0 → 1.6) and cosmetic unlocks (LampPost, Planters, GoldenTrim). This config has existed since the initial PRD-compliance implementation but was NEVER WIRED — there's no purchase path, no income-multiplier consumption, no cosmetic rendering, and no UI.

The round-2 review (EPIC 15) flagged this as checklist item #15 (Advertised Multiplier Never Applied). The user directed: "wire as feature."

DESIGN: Dock upgrades are an INCOME MULTIPLIER progression path, distinct from Aquarium upgrades (which add capacity + a smaller income multiplier). This gives players two parallel investment tracks:
  - Aquarium upgrades: more fish capacity + moderate income multiplier (1.0-1.5)
  - Dock upgrades: NO capacity change, but a LARGER income multiplier (1.0-1.6) + cosmetic flair

This creates a meaningful choice: do you spend 8000 on a Mega Tank (more fish, 1.5x) or 10000 on a Golden Trim dock (same fish, 1.6x + cosmetics)? The answer depends on playstyle — hoarders want capacity, min-maxers want the higher multiplier.

PRD ALIGNMENT:
  - TASK 2.6 (closed) defined the tier structure
  - TASK 6.4 (open) covers the purchase flow — this epic IMPLEMENTS it
  - The cosmetic unlocks (LampPost, Planters, GoldenTrim) are per-tier visual rewards

WHY THIS MATTERS: The income loop (store fish → earn passive income → buy upgrades → store more fish) is the core retention loop. Adding a second upgrade track doubles the progression depth without adding new mechanics — it's pure economy expansion using existing systems.

CONSIDERATIONS:
- DockUpgradeTiers is 1-indexed (level 1 = base, free). Purchases start at level 2.
- The income multiplier STACKS with the Aquarium multiplier (both apply in incomePerSec). A maxed player (Aquarium 4 + Dock 4) gets 1.5 * 1.6 = 2.4x base income per fish.
- Cosmetic unlocks need visual implementation (lamp posts, planters, gold trim on the dock model). This is scoped as a separate task (TASK 17.5) and can be deferred post-launch if needed.
- The profile already has `Dock = { UpgradeLevel = 1, CosmeticUnlocks = {} }` — the schema is ready.

RELATED EXISTING BEADS:
- harborheist-economy-upgrade-system-pdq.4 (TASK 6.4: Dock upgrade purchase + income multiplier) — this epic fulfills it
- harborheist-game-content-definitions-pmr.6 (TASK 2.6: Dock upgrade tiers) — closed, defined the config

description:

IMPLEMENTATION (extends the N13 fix):
  -- After the aquarium multiplier block:
  local dockLevel = session.profile.Dock.UpgradeLevel or 1
  local dockTier = GameConfig.DockUpgradeTiers[dockLevel]
  if dockTier and dockTier.incomeMultiplier then

BALANCE: A maxed player (Aquarium 4: 1.5x, Dock 4: 1.6x) gets 1.5 * 1.6 = 2.4x base income per fish. With 75 fish at ~10 income/min avg, that's 75 * 10 / 60 * 2.4 = 30 coins/sec passive. This is strong but bounded by MaxUnclaimedIncome (50,000) and requires ~20,800 coins invested (8000 aquarium + 12800 dock). Payback at 30/sec is ~12 minutes — reasonable for an endgame investment.

- [ ] Multipliers stack (1.5 * 1.6 = 2.4, not 1.5 + 1.6 = 3.1)

- [ ] Income display updates correctly after dock purchase

title: TASK 17.6: Clamp Dock.UpgradeLevel in sanitize() against DockUpgradeTiers
description:
WHAT: The sanitize() function currently accepts Dock.UpgradeLevel if it's >= 1, but doesn't clamp it against the DockUpgradeTiers table length. A crafted save with UpgradeLevel = 999 would be loaded and honored, causing DockUpgradeTiers[999] lookups to return nil downstream.

This is checklist item #10 (Persisted Capacity Trusted Without Tier Cross-Check) applied to the Dock track. The same fix pattern used for Aquarium.UpgradeLevel (N6 in DataManager) should be applied here.

IMPLEMENTATION (in the Dock branch of sanitize):
  if type(data.Dock.UpgradeLevel) == "number" and data.Dock.UpgradeLevel >= 1 then
    clean.Dock.UpgradeLevel = math.floor(data.Dock.UpgradeLevel)
  end
  -- Clamp against authoritative tier table (mirrors the Aquarium N6 pattern):
  local DockUpgradeTiers = GameConfig.DockUpgradeTiers
  local dockLevel = clean.Dock.UpgradeLevel or 1
  if DockUpgradeTiers and #DockUpgradeTiers > 0 then
    dockLevel = math.max(1, math.min(dockLevel, #DockUpgradeTiers))
    clean.Dock.UpgradeLevel = dockLevel
  end

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] Dock.UpgradeLevel clamped to [1, #DockUpgradeTiers] in sanitize
- [ ] A crafted save with UpgradeLevel=999 is clamped to 4 on load
- [ ] Existing valid saves are unaffected
- [ ] Pattern mirrors the Aquarium.UpgradeLevel clamp (N6)

FILES: src/server/DataManager.lua (Dock branch of sanitize, ~line 190)
DEPENDS ON: Nothing (defensive hardening, can be done independently)

title: P1: RequestCast accepted mid-bite — activeBites overwrite corrupts in-flight catch validation
description: FishingService.lua: session.casting flips false at :179 BEFORE BiteEvent fires at :212, so during the entire 3.5s bite minigame the RequestCast :61 guard passes. title: EPIC 3: Fishing System Rework — Timing Minigame
description:
Replace the current auto-catch (cast→wait→free fish) with a timing-based minigame and species-based catch resolution per PRD FISH-01..FISH-08.

Current FishingService: player casts, waits castTime seconds, gets a fish automatically. PRD FISH-03 requires 'a short, readable timing minigame' — a moving marker the player must stop in a target zone. PRD FISH-04: success awards fish, failure = retry-ready. The minigame runs client-side for responsiveness (PRD perf table) but RESULT resolution is server-side. The server tells the client when a bite occurs; client runs the timing UI; client reports the timing result; server validates and resolves the actual species/value.

title: Context menu horizontal overflow on viewports narrower than menu width
description:
## Summary

ContextMenu.show() horizontal clamping in src/client/init.client.lua (~:790) is incomplete. When the menu doesn't fit right of the cursor it shifts left with math.max(0, x - menuWidth - 8) — clamping only the LEFT edge to 0. On viewports narrower than the 180px menu width, the menu still extends past the right screen edge (position 0 + width 180 > viewportW).

## Root cause

The right-edge correction clamps the minimum position but ignores that min + menuWidth must also fit. First principles: position must satisfy BOTH posX >= 0 AND posX + menuWidth <= viewportW. On viewportW < menuWidth that's impossible without also shrinking the menu or allowing off-screen — the pragmatic fix clamps into [0, max(0, viewportW - menuWidth)].

## Fix

  if posX + menuWidth > viewportW then
    posX = math.max(0, math.min(viewportW - menuWidth, x - menuWidth - 8))
  end

## Severity

USER-VISIBLE only on tiny viewports (<180px wide). Desktop-only feature (vasr binds skip IS_MOBILE), so this is an extreme edge case (severely resized desktop window). Not launch-blocking. Audit finding #3, HarborHeist-Dev session 2026-07-30.
close_reason: Fixed in 49ab0b0: position clamped into [0, viewportW-menuWidth] so the menu's right edge stays on-screen on narrow viewports. Gates green.

title: Create shadow/elevation system (low, medium, high)
description:
**CONTEXT:**
Panels and cards are flat with no depth cues. Premium apps use elevation shadows to create hierarchy.

**WHAT TO DO:**
1. Create 3 elevation levels with fake shadow frames (Roblox doesn't support real shadows in UI)
2. Apply elevation consistently:
   - low: cards, list items (subtle shadow)
   - medium: panels, modals (medium shadow)
   - high: overlays, toasts, floating buttons (strong shadow)
3. Add elevation transitions (panels lift when opened)

**IMPLEMENTATION:**
```lua
-- Fake shadow using layered frames with decreasing transparency
local ELEVATIONS = {
  low = { layers = 2, spread = 4, alpha = 0.15 },
  medium = { layers = 3, spread = 8, alpha = 0.2 },
  high = { layers = 4, spread = 16, alpha = 0.3 },
}

local function applyElevation(element, level)
  local config = ELEVATIONS[level] or ELEVATIONS.low
  for i = 1, config.layers do
    local shadow = Instance.new("Frame")
    shadow.Name = "Shadow_" .. i
    shadow.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.new(0, 0, 0)
    shadow.BackgroundTransparency = 1 - (config.alpha * (1 - (i-1)/config.layers))
    shadow.Size = UDim2.new(1, config.spread * i, 1, config.spread * i)
    shadow.Position = UDim2.new(0, -config.spread * i / 2, 0, -config.spread * i / 2)
    shadow.ZIndex = element.ZIndex - 1
    corner(shadow, CORNERS.lg)
    shadow.Parent = element
  end
end
```

**VERIFICATION:**
- 3 elevation levels render correctly
- Shadows don't interfere with click targets
- Performance is acceptable (fake shadows are just frames)
notes: Implemented by RainyLynx-Jul26. Created applyElevation(element, level) function at ~line 613, consuming Theme.shadows configs (low/medium/high with layers/spread/alpha) defined in uabg.7 — proves those token definitions are usable (single source of truth). Creates layered black Frames behind the element (ZIndex = element.ZIndex-1) with progressively increasing Size and decreasing BackgroundTransparency: innermost layer is most opaque, outermost is faintest. Registered as Theme.applyElevation (silences FunctionUnused; clean API for downstream beads: Theme.applyElevation(element, 'low')). Duplicate-safe: removes existing Shadow_N children before recreating (supports re-elevation on state change). Added shadow.Active = false so shadow frames don't intercept clicks in the area extending beyond the element (addresses the bead's verification criterion 'Shadows don't interfere with click targets'). INCLUDED ONLY STEP 1 (create the system/function). Steps 2-3 (apply to existing panels/cards/toasts + add elevation transitions on panel open) NOT done — they are visual changes requiring Roblox Studio verification (not available on this Linux box). Documented the UIListLayout caveat: apply to elements WITHOUT a UIListLayout (panels, toasts, prompts); for layout containers, wrap in a plain Frame and apply to the wrapper. title: Create gradient library (surface, accent, status gradients)
description:
**CONTEXT:**
Gradients are used inconsistently. Need a library of reusable gradient presets.

**WHAT TO DO:**
1. Create gradient presets:
   - Surface gradients (subtle background variations)
   - Accent gradients (buttons, highlights)
   - Status gradients (progress bars, health indicators)
   - Rarity gradients (fish rarity colors)
2. Document usage patterns
3. Apply consistently across UI

**IMPLEMENTATION:**
```lua
local GRADIENTS = {
  surface = {
    default = { from = Color3.fromRGB(26, 38, 57), to = UI.surface.primary },
    elevated = { from = Color3.fromRGB(36, 48, 67), to = UI.surface.secondary },
  },
  accent = {
    primary = { from = Color3.fromRGB(56, 152, 255), to = Color3.fromRGB(100, 180, 255) },
    success = { from = Color3.fromRGB(52, 199, 123), to = Color3.fromRGB(100, 220, 160) },
    warning = { from = Color3.fromRGB(255, 184, 64), to = Color3.fromRGB(255, 210, 100) },
    error = { from = Color3.fromRGB(255, 92, 92), to = Color3.fromRGB(255, 140, 140) },
  },
  rarity = {
    Common = { from = Color3.fromRGB(200, 200, 200), to = Color3.fromRGB(150, 150, 150) },
    Rare = { from = Color3.fromRGB(100, 150, 255), to = Color3.fromRGB(50, 100, 200) },
    Epic = { from = Color3.fromRGB(167, 139, 250), to = Color3.fromRGB(120, 80, 200) },
    Legendary = { from = Color3.fromRGB(255, 205, 92), to = Color3.fromRGB(255, 160, 50) },
  },
}

local function applyGradient(element, preset)
  local config = GRADIENTS[preset]
  if not config then return end
  local gradient = Instance.new("UIGradient")
  gradient.Color = ColorSequence.new(config.from, config.to)
  gradient.Rotation = 90
  gradient.Parent = element
  return gradient
end
```

**VERIFICATION:**
- All gradient presets render correctly
- Gradients are applied consistently
- Performance is acceptable

title: EPIC 18: Zero-Mock Unit Test Coverage (TestEZ)
description:
Umbrella for bringing the repo from ZERO automated tests to full unit-level coverage of all server services and shared modules, under a hard constraint: NO MOCKS / NO FAKES.

## CURRENT STATE (verified 2026-07-22, ChartreuseFox)
- No *.spec.lua / *.test.lua anywhere; no TestEZ; no test tree in default.project.json; no test runner script.
- Verification today is manual .rbxlx playthrough only (beads 13.1, 16.5).
- Machine has: rojo, selene, cargo. MISSING: Roblox Studio, wine, lune, run-in-roblox, wally/foreman/aftman.

## NO-MOCK CONSTRAINT (what it means here)
- Tests require() and exercise the REAL modules: real GameConfig tables, real service functions, real state.
- Determinism comes from Random.new(seed) — seeding the real RNG is NOT mocking.
- Pure-logic modules (GameConfig, DataManager sanitize/migrate, AntiExploitService, QuestService rotation) run as plain Luau — no Roblox API shims allowed; if a module can't run without a DataModel, it is tested inside a real DataModel (Studio/run-in-roblox), never against a fake DataModel.
- Persistence paths use a REAL Roblox DataStore (dedicated test DataStore, throwaway keys) when run in Studio; skipped with an explicit log line when API access is unavailable. No DataStoreService stubs.

## FRAMEWORK
TestEZ (Roblox-standard BDD: describe/it/expect) vendored into the repo. Runner decision (lune for pure-Luau vs run-in-roblox for DataModel-bound) is spiked in TASK 18.1 — this machine currently lacks both, so installation is part of the task.

## SCOPE (13 tasks)
18.1 harness -> 18.2 GameConfig -> 18.3 shared definitions -> 18.4 DataManager pure logic -> 18.5 FishingService -> 18.6 AquariumService -> 18.7 ShopService -> 18.8 FishInventoryService -> 18.9 RaidService -> 18.10 QuestService -> 18.11 AntiExploitService -> 18.12 Collection/Onboarding/AuditLog -> 18.13 coverage gate.
Services intentionally EXCLUDED from unit scope (covered by EPIC 19 e2e instead): WorldBuilder, DockManager, RodService, BoatService, StateSync, Remotes, AnalyticsService (DataModel/presentation-heavy; their logic is thin glue).

## DONE WHEN
Every in-scope module has a spec file exercising every exported function against the real implementation, the suite runs via one command with non-zero exit on failure, and the 18.13 coverage gate reports and enforces thresholds.
close_reason: Umbrella epic complete: all 13 subtasks (k5wz.1-.13) closed. TestEZ harness, 13 service unit-test suites, coverage measurement + enforcement gate all delivered. 100 pure-specs pass on Linux. Closed by RainyLynx during session bead-hygiene sweep.

## Runner Spike Results (SwiftFox, 2026-07-22)

### Runner A: lune (PURE BUCKET — WORKS ON THIS MACHINE)
- Installed: lune v0.10.5 (prebuilt Linux x86_64 binary from GitHub releases)

- Key constraint: lune require() resolves ./ ./-relative to the REQUIRING FILE, not CWD. fs.readDir uses CWD-relative paths. Extensions are stripped — require("path") looks for path.luau or path.lua, NOT path.spec.lua.
- @lune/fs provides readDir (directory listing), isDir, isFile. @lune/glob NOT available in 0.10.5 — implemented recursive scanner with fs.readDir.
- @lune/process provides process.exit (os.exit is nil in lune).

2. Coverage report artifact: per-module function coverage %, written to testlogs/coverage.txt (and printed).

Thresholds: 100% of exported functions exercised for GameConfig, DataManager pure helpers, AntiExploitService, QuestService, FishInventoryService, ShopService; >=90% for AquariumService, RaidService, FishingService, CollectionService, OnboardingService, AuditLogService (remaining % = DataModel-bound paths covered by EPIC 19 instead — each uncovered function must be listed in the report with a one-line reason).
4. Definition-of-done documentation: 'full unit coverage without mocks' is defined as the above — every exported function of every in-scope module executed at least once against the real implementation, plus the assertion density already encoded by 18.2-18.12.

## k5wz.4.1 Results (SwiftFox, 2026-07-22)

### Test Export
Added `DataManager._sanitize = sanitize` (3 lines, no behavior change) at end of DataManager.lua to make the local sanitize function accessible to the TestEZ spec.

**Case 1 — Valid v2 pass-through (7 tests):** Coins, Equipment, Aquarium, Collection, Onboarding, PvP, Defense, Dock all preserved on clean input.

title: EPIC 44: World-class UI/UX — motion, feedback & modality-specific refinement (desktop + mobile)
description:
EPIC 44 — World-class UI/UX refinement: motion, feedback, and modality-native polish for desktop + mobile.

== ORIGIN ==
Operator directive (2026-08-01, session GoldenEagle-Jul31): take the Harbor Heist UI/UX from good to WORLD-CLASS — the fit-and-finish bar set by products like Stripe — and hyper-optimize desktop and mobile SEPARATELY, playing to each modality's strengths instead of shipping one compromised layout. This epic is the execution vehicle for that directive.

== METHOD (how the work was derived, for future selves) ==
1. Full architecture re-read (AGENTS.md, README.md, docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.docx, all of src/client/init.client.lua ~7.5k lines, AnimationSystem/GradientLibrary/PanelAnimation/KeyboardNav/UIPalette).
2. A 12-area deep audit (HUD, panels, visual-language consistency, typography, motion, feedback, desktop UX, mobile UX, minigames, reveal card, onboarding, performance) producing ~60 findings.
3. Every candidate finding was RE-VERIFIED against current source before beading. Several audit claims were STALE and excluded (toast SAFE_TOP, catch audio, raid minigame title, shop disabled visuals, TOAST_FADE value, landscape stack scrolling) — the codebase moves fast; trust beads, but re-verify evidence lines before implementing.
4. De-duplication against EPIC 43 (harborheist-a2ug, premium polish audit) so nothing is double-tracked.

== DESIGN PHILOSOPHY (the bar we are holding) ==
- Stripe principle 1 — INTENTIONAL MOTION: every duration/easing exists for a reason. Entries decelerate (smooth arrival), exits accelerate but never feel rushed, springs only for physical bounce-back. Ratio discipline: close ~= 0.8x open, never 0.5x.
- Stripe principle 2 — HONEST, IMMEDIATE FEEDBACK: every input gets an acknowledgment within ~100ms; disabled things LOOK disabled; affordances are visible on every background; nothing silently clips or overflows.
- Stripe principle 3 — MODALITY-NATIVE: desktop = hover states, tooltips, keyboard-first flows, wide-screen balance; mobile = 44px targets, thumb zones, bottom sheets, scroll affordances, density control. Neither is a scaled version of the other.
- Stripe principle 4 — ONE VISUAL LANGUAGE: tokens over literals; one motion vocabulary; one zone vocabulary across minigames; documented in docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.docx.

== STRUCTURE ==
Seven workstream sub-epics (children): A motion harmony, B feedback and affordance, C minigame readability, D desktop modality, E mobile modality, F delight and UI performance, G verification/docs/handoff. Task-level beads hang under workstreams; design beads block their implementation beads; G.2 Studio matrix blocks final close.

== RELATIONSHIP TO OTHER EPICS ==
- EPIC 43 (harborheist-a2ug): the first polish pass (toasts, shop clarity, raid sweep, discovery). EPIC 44 is the NEXT tier — motion grammar, modality-specific refinement, delight. No overlap by construction (verified 2026-08-01).
- Studio-gated verification folds into harborheist-orpl (runtime pass) + harborheist-rswb (visual QA) — G.2 is the funnel.
- Reveal-card audio design (F) is blocked on a2ug.16 (sound asset pipeline decision).

== NON-GOALS ==
Panel layout redesigns; new gameplay systems; monetization; sound asset replacement (a2ug.16); server game-logic changes except the one CancelCast remote needed for Esc-cancel (D workstream).

== DEFINITION OF DONE ==
Every workstream child closed; pure-spec suite + selene (no new warnings over baseline) + rojo build green after EACH child; source-contract specs updated per repo convention; G.1 design-system doc updated; G.2 Studio matrix executed (or folded into orpl/rswb runs); G.3 final review posted.

title: Perf: split HUD 'ready' segment into its own label + tween transparency (kill the 5Hz full-line RichText rebuild)
description:
WS-F / PERF. HUD income-line write elimination.

PLAN-REVIEW CORRECTION (2026-08-01): the original prescription (bucketed string caching) does NOT fix the hot path. The 5Hz pulse animates the ready segment's font transparency by REBUILDING THE ENTIRE RICHTEXT STRING every 0.2s (updateIncomeLine ~:1757-1770: string.format with rate + ready + alpha). Alpha changes every cycle by design, so a string cache would miss 5x/sec forever — the caching idea only helped the idle branch, which is already a cheap 0.5s sleep (no rewrite there at all: render() owns the idle line).

ROOT CAUSE: the animated segment and the static rate share ONE label, so animating anything rewrites everything.

OPTIMAL FIX (simpler + bigger win): split into two labels — incomeRateLabel (static; rewritten only on state push / value change) + readyLabel (the '$N ready' segment; alpha pulse via tweened TextTransparency, zero string allocation). Position readyLabel inline after the rate (UIListLayout horizontal or manual offset measured from TextBounds).

PITFALLS: (1) mobile layout — the 178px card keeps the one-line no-layout-shift treatment (current code drops TextSize a notch when ready>0 — preserve that logic); (2) the 6+ digit mobile clip is a RECORDED accepted tradeoff in the source comment — do not 'fix' it here; (3) pulse period 2.4s Sine triangle — keep the exact curve, just drive it via transparency property instead of RichText attr.

VERIFICATION: pure suite; build; no spec needed. STUDIO CHECK: pulse identical visually; rate updates instantly on catch/sell/claim.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
DESIGN SIGN-OFF (2026-08-01, GoldenEagle-Jul31) — 4 questions resolved from actual code (FishingService.lua, AntiExploitService.lua, Remotes.lua):

Q1 CANCEL WINDOW: Pre-bite wait ONLY. session.casting==true is the authoritative 'cast pending, bite not yet fired' window (set RequestCast L102, flipped false in the task.delay callback L193 BEFORE BiteEvent fires L226). Cancel accepted IFF session.casting==true; once the bite fires (casting=false) cancel is a no-op (non-cancellable). No separate pre-server-ack phase exists (RequestCast is fire-and-forget RemoteEvent, no ack) so the window is simply the 2-6s pre-bite wait.

Q2 RATE LIMITING: NEW cancel_cast bucket = { maxCalls=5, windowSeconds=10 } in AntiExploitService.RATE_LIMITS, checked via antiExploit.checkRate(player,'cancel_cast') mirroring the cast bucket. Distinct from 'cast' (different spam vector; cancelling must never count against the casting budget). 5/10s is generous Esc-spam protection only.

Q3 POST-CANCEL STATE: Clear session.casting=false, activeBites[player]=nil, call rodService.endCast(player,false), fire remotes.CastState:FireClient(player,false,0) to hide the client overlay, AND bump a per-cast generation token castGen[player] so the in-flight task.delay bite callback becomes a no-op. NO profile/luck/rarity/species changes — cancel never refunds, re-rolls, or awards. The generation token is the critical race guard: task.delay returns void (Luau has no task.cancel for void delays), so without it the stale callback would fire spurious CastState:false + 'left the zone'/'hands full' notifies + a redundant endCast after cancel. Token captured per-cast (local myGen in RequestCast) and checked at the top of the bite callback; CancelCast bumps it so the stale callback's myGen no longer matches -> early return. This is the mechanism that 'cancels the pending bite timer'. Cleanup mirrors existing zone-leave/hands-full/catch paths (activeBites=nil + endCast(false)) — no forked logic.

Q4 BITE/RAID NON-CANCELLABLE: CONFIRMED. Cancel applies ONLY during the pre-bite wait (session.casting=true). Once the bite fires (BiteEvent sent, casting=false) the bite minigame is forfeit-by-design — player engages or lets the BITE_WINDOW sweeper (L236-246) time it out. Raid minigames (RaidService) out of scope.

RACE GUARD (both directions, serialized on server thread): (a) CancelCast before bite callback -> casting=false + activeBites=nil + castGen bumped -> callback sees gen mismatch -> no-op (clean cancel, no BiteEvent). (b) Bite callback first -> BiteEvent fired, casting=false -> CancelCast 'if not session.casting then return' -> no-op (fired bite non-cancellable). Either order safe.

NON-GOALS: no luck/rarity/species changes, no refunds, no cancel of fired bites/raid minigames. STUDIO CHECK deferred to kqbq.12.2 (client Esc wiring, init.client.lua — handled by the parallel session).

Children unblocked: kqbq.12.1 (server CancelCast remote + FishingService cancel path — I implement now, server files only) and kqbq.12.2 (client Esc wiring — deferred, contested init.client.lua).

title: Desktop: ultra-wide action bar — cap max width / re-balance on >2560px viewports
description:
WS-D / DESKTOP. Ultra-wide action-bar balance (P4 polish).

WHY: layoutDesktopBar shrinks buttons below 820px but never adapts ABOVE — on 2560px+/ultra-wide the bottom-center bar is a small cluster floating in a vast empty strip. Desktop composition should feel balanced at every width.

EVIDENCE: layoutDesktopBar ~:5300-5320; bar.AnchorPoint=(0.5,1); button width floor 76px, no ceiling.

TARGET: above ~1920px, scale button width modestly (e.g. 100 -> 108-112px) and/or widen gaps; cap the total bar width so it never exceeds ~40% of viewport. Keep keyboard chips legible (key chip scales with button).

PRIORITY RATIONALE (P4): niche viewport; do AFTER P2/P3 modality work; zero risk to standard widths (guard with a width threshold).

VERIFICATION: contract spec (threshold + cap math); pure suite; build. STUDIO CHECK: 3440x1440 and 3840x2160 — bar feels anchored, not lost; 1920x1080 unchanged.

Standard widths (<=1920px) hit neither branch -> btnW stays BAR_BTN_W (pixel-unchanged); shrink branch below ~820px preserved. 12 contract assertions in new test/pure_specs/DesktopActionBar.spec.lua (separate file to avoid colliding on the concurrently-edited ClientChrome.spec.lua). title: Perf: skip no-op list rebuilds via content hash (NOT full row-diffing — premise corrected)
description:
WS-F / PERF. List render efficiency.

PLAN-REVIEW CORRECTION (2026-08-01): the original premise ('50+ fish inventories') is WRONG for this game. Verified against source: carried fish cap at 5 (MaxCarried=5) grouped into <=15 species rows; STORED fish render as a 5-line RichText rarity summary in the aquarium panel, NOT as rows (:3085 comment confirms stored fish are deliberately not row-rendered); shop = 19 rows + headers (further collapsed by a2ug.9 when tracks max out); collection = 15 species; quests/raid lists are a handful. The realistic max list is ~20 rows. A key-based row-reuse/diffing architecture is OVER-ENGINEERING for 20 rows — instance churn at that scale is noise, and the refactor risk (a2ug.10 flash tokens, cl05 state colors, inventory context menus) outweighs it.

RESIDUAL PROBLEM WORTH FIXING: render() rebuilds lists on EVERY StateChanged push even when that list's content didn't change (e.g. a cash-only update rebuilds the inventory DOM). Cheap, honest fix: per-list content signature (concatenated keys+counts — e.g. species:count pairs for inventory, kind:level:state for shop) — skip the rebuild when the signature matches the last render. ~15 lines per list, zero architecture change.

DO NOT DO: row pooling, keyed reuse maps, scroll-position-preserving diffs. If a future feature introduces a genuinely large list (e.g. per-fish stored rows), file a new bead then.

VERIFICATION: contract spec (signature guard exists per list); pure suite; build. STUDIO CHECK: open inventory, trigger unrelated state change (cash tick) — no visible re-render flicker.
acceptance_criteria: Signature-skip on inventory + shop + collection; identical visible behavior; no diffing architecture introduced.
close_reason: Completed: Added lastShopSignature content-hash guard to refreshShop() — skips no-op row-update + maxed-collapse pass when shop visible state unchanged (per-kind: level + maxed + affordability). Inventory (lastInventorySignature) and Collection (lastCollectionSignature) guards already existed. 20 new spec assertions in ClientChrome.spec.lua. Quality: 839/0 pure, selene 0 err/16 warn baseline, rojo build OK. No diffing architecture introduced.

title: Mobile: toast density — 52px min-height + action buttons eat vertical space; compact mobile toast layout
description:
WS-E / MOBILE. Toast density on small screens.

WHY: mobile toasts carry a 52px min-height (to fit 44x44 action buttons) and stack up to 3 — on a ~375px-tall landscape phone that stack covers a big share of the viewport during noisy moments (raid window + catches + quest progress).

EVIDENCE: toastMinSize ~:2067-2089 (52px mobile); MAX_VISIBLE_TOASTS=3; action buttons 44x44 mobile.

TARGET: compact mobile layout — action buttons become icon-only 44x44 inline-right (keeping the 44px target law), tighter text padding, and a viewport-relative stack cap (~30% of height) with a small +N more overflow indicator when the queue exceeds it. Desktop unchanged.

PITFALLS: TouchTargets.spec asserts 44px actions — icon-only must stay 44x44; queue eviction policy (MAX_TOAST_QUEUE) unchanged — only VISUAL stacking changes; raid-victim toasts are high-priority — never let the overflow cap hide them silently (category-priority ordering).

VERIFICATION: contract spec + TouchTargets.spec green; pure suite; build. STUDIO CHECK: raid-window spam on a small phone — toasts readable, screen usable, overflow indicator truthful.
acceptance_criteria: Mobile stack <= ~30% viewport; 44px actions preserved; overflow indicator; specs green.
close_reason: Completed: mobile toast density landed. (1) MAX_VISIBLE_TOASTS_MOBILE viewport poll (1Hz) scales the visible cap so the toast stack stays under ~30% of viewport height, clamped 1..3 — maxVisibleToasts() consumed by showNotification + drainToastQueue. (2) Mobile action buttons: 64px text pills -> compact 44x44 pills (44px touch-target law on both axes; MIN_TOAST_H_MOBILE_ACTIONS=52 single-sourced), text narrows to clear the buttons (math.min(#actions,2)). (3) toastOverflowChip (+N more) under the stack reports queued backlog on mobile, refreshed on enqueue/drain. Desktop unchanged. REVIEW FIXES (fresh-eyes pass): text-narrowing capped at 2 rendered buttons; close-button branch moved off literal 52 to the shared token; comment honesty (cap budget excludes overflow chip; 'icon-only' -> 'compact 44x44 pills'). TouchTargets.spec updated (44x44 action branch, token-based min-height contract). 8 ClientChrome contract assertions. Quality: pure 925/0, selene 0/16 baseline, rojo build OK. STUDIO CHECK (orpl/rswb): raid-window spam on a small phone — toasts readable, screen usable, overflow chip truthful.

title: WS-A: Motion & timing harmony — one intentional motion vocabulary
description:
Workstream A of EPIC 44. WHY: the motion system is 90% disciplined (EASE presets exist) but the remaining 10% breaks the spell: panel close 0.16s vs open 0.28s (rushed), press compression too shallow (0.96/0.12s), desktop hover at press speed (0.12s), and backdrop taps during the open slide dismiss mid-animation (.17.3).

PLAN-REVIEW CORRECTION (2026-08-01): the original press-easing prescription (Quad In) was physically WRONG — spring compression decelerates into resistance, so Quad Out is correct; .2 now targets depth/duration, not easing direction. This is why plan-space review exists.

SCOPE: .1 panel close harmony, .2 press feel, .3 hover pacing, .17.3 open input gating, .17.1 motion catalog (incl. REJECTION log), .17.2 Theme.motion centralization (blocked by .1/.2/.3/.17.1).

DESIGN RULE (encode in .17.2): entries decelerate (Quint Out 0.22-0.28), exits ~0.8x of entry (0.22 close vs 0.28 open), press = Quad Out 0.10 at 0.94 depth, release = Spring, hover = Quad Out 0.20, finger-tracking always 1:1 instant, never Spring for fades/exits.

comments.text:
MOTION AUDIT (2026-08-01, GoldenEagle-Jul31) — read-only catalog; kqbq.17.2 centralizes into Theme.motion. Line numbers approximate (file under active edit); code PATTERNS exact.

== PRESET BLOCK (init.client.lua ~:223-244) ==
EASE_OUT  = TweenInfo.new(0.22, Quint, Out)  -- 14 sites
EASE_POP  = TweenInfo.new(0.28, Spring, Out) -- 6 sites
EASE_FAST = TweenInfo.new(0.12, Quad, Out)   -- 12 sites
EASE_HOVER= TweenInfo.new(0.2, Quad, Out)    -- 8 sites (desktop only)
EASE_PRESS= TweenInfo.new(0.10, Quad, Out)   -- 1 site (pressTween, kqbq.2)
EASE_IN   = TweenInfo.new(0.16, Quad, In)    -- 0 sites (entry-accel, currently unused -> kqbq.17.2 may drop or repurpose)
EASE_TOOLTIP (0.15, Quad, Out) -- PROPOSED in kqbq.20.1, NOT YET IMPLEMENTED.

== TweenService:Create SITES (62 total) ==
44 use a named preset (71%): EASE_OUT x14 (collection row highlight, toast entrance x6, panel exit/backdrop, capacity bar, lock color), EASE_FAST x12 (scrollbar auto-hide, HUD appear/hide, toast/card reveals, panel mid-point snap), EASE_POP x6 (button release, toast scale-in, legendary/standard card reveal, bonus cash pop, overlay reveal), EASE_HOVER x8 (button hover scale/color/glow/shadows x2 for enter+leave), EASE_PRESS x1 (pressTween).
9 use a variable: pressTween(=EASE_PRESS) L1036; fade(=TweenInfo.new(TOAST_FADE=0.4,Quad,In)) L2119; ti/elementTi (computed staggering framework) L1391/1467/1506; step(=0.05 Quad InOut) L7034.
9 are inline TweenInfo.new literals -> the centralization candidates + exceptions below.

== Anim:* TRANSITIONS (9, all preset-aligned) ==
Panel open=0.28 (EASE_POP): Anim:slide up L2939, Anim:scale fit L2953. Panel close=0.22 (EASE_OUT): Anim:slide down L2851/L2899, Anim:scale 0.9 L2868/L2919, Anim:fade backdrop L2878/L2934/L2954. Gesture (no duration): Anim:swipeDismiss L7080, Anim:pullToRefresh L7093. NOTE: AnimationSystem.lua itself creates TweenInfo INLINE with BACK easing (Transition:slide/scale/fadeSlide ~:456/475/518 use TweenInfo.new(dur, Back, Out); rotate ~:495 Quad Out) -- the named presets are NOT passed through. kqbq.17.2 should surface Theme.motion presets into the Anim namespace (or accept a TweenInfo) so even Anim:* transitions resolve to the centralized tokens.

== INLINE TweenInfo.new LITERALS: consolidation candidates + exceptions ==
CANDIDATES (should become presets in kqbq.17.2):
  - L964 ripple: TweenInfo.new(0.35, Quad, Out) -> NEW EASE_RIPPLE (0.35 is unique; 0.22 EASE_OUT is too short for the ripple to expand visibly).
  - L6788 rarity flash tail: TweenInfo.new(0.45, Quad, In) -> NEW EASE_FLASH (optional; accelerating reveal tail, intentional In).
  - L2119 toast fade: TweenInfo.new(TOAST_FADE=0.4, Quad, In) -> optional NEW EASE_TOAST (or keep the TOAST_FADE constant).
REJECTION LOG (justified exceptions -- do NOT re-flag as inconsistencies):
  - L1856 cash-gain float 0.8s Quint Out: cash gains are semantic info the player must READ -> extended visibility, distinct tier. Keep.
  - L2119 toast fade 0.4s Quad IN: intentional accelerating exit (snappy dismissal) -- the rare case In is correct. Keep (constant TOAST_FADE).
  - L5973 fish-button pulse 0.32/0.85s Sine InOut REPEATING (-1, true): context-driven loop (cooldown fast / ready slow). Cannot be preset. Keep.
  - L6759 legendary card reveal 0.5s Spring (vs standard 0.28 EASE_POP): intentional RARITY GRADING (legendary = slower, bouncier). Keep.
  - L6771 epic+ card stroke pulse 0.55s Sine InOut REPEATING: breathing effect during card display. Keep.
  - L6788 rarity flash tail 0.45s Quad IN: dramatic reveal tail that ACCELERATES (not EASE_OUT decel). Keep (or EASE_FLASH preset).
  - L7034 fish-button shake 0.05s Quad InOut (looped x4): mechanical rapid shake -- tight timing is the point. Keep.
  - L7727 minigame marker sweep TweenInfo.new(duration, Linear) variable: SERVER-driven per-attempt duration; Linear is correct for server-synced timing bars; os.clock physics (cast/bite/raid sweeps). Out of scope for preset centralization.
  ALSO (from the kqbq.17.1 spec): backdrop drag-dismiss transparency is per-frame INSTANT by design (finger-tracking 1:1; only release eased) -- instant is correct, not a preset miss.

== NEW PRESETS FOR kqbq.17.2 ==
1. EASE_RIPPLE (0.35, Quad, Out) -- L964 ripple (required).
2. EASE_FLASH (0.45, Quad, In) -- L6788 reveal flash tail (optional).
3. EASE_TOOLTIP (0.15, Quad, Out) -- per kqbq.20.1 tooltip spec (when kqbq.10 lands).
4. EASE_TOAST (0.4, Quad, In) -- L2119 toast fade (optional; or keep TOAST_FADE constant).
5. Decision: EASE_IN (0.16) has 0 sites -- kqbq.17.2 may DROP it or repurpose (e.g. as the toast/flash In baseline).

== kqbq.17.2 CENTRALIZATION PLAN ==
Move the presets into a Theme.motion table (e.g. Theme.motion.easeOut / .pop / .fast / .hover / .press / .ripple) sourced from one place, and route every TweenService:Create + Anim:* transition through Theme.motion.* (replace the bare EASE_* locals with Theme.motion lookups). Surface Theme.motion into AnimationSystem.lua so Anim:slide/scale/fade use the centralized tokens (currently Back-easing inline). Lune-testable via a Theme.motion mirror spec. Contract spec: assert Theme.motion exists + every preset duration/easing, + that the ripple (L964) uses the ripple preset. Do NOT touch the rejection-log exceptions.

== SUMMARY ==
62 TweenService:Create (44 on presets, 71%), 9 Anim:* (all aligned), 2 required new presets (EASE_RIPPLE; EASE_FLASH optional) + EASE_TOOLTIP pending kqbq.10, 8 justified exceptions logged, AnimationSystem Back-easing inline is the main centralization target.

title: Panel-open input gating: backdrop taps during the 0.28s open slide dismiss mid-animation
description:
WS-A / MOTION (added in plan review 2026-08-01). WHY: showPanel sets backdrop.Visible=true immediately (:2864) and backdrop.Activated is always connected (:2890) — a tap during the 0.28s slide-up fires hidePanels mid-animation: the panel snaps away before it ever arrives. Double-tap-prone mobile users hit this constantly when opening panels.

TARGET: suppress backdrop dismissal while an open animation is in flight — set a panelOpening flag at showPanel start, clear it when the open tween completes (and on hidePanels); backdrop.Activated returns early while set. 0.28s of ignored background taps is imperceptible; mid-animation dismissal is jarring. Alternative considered: queue the dismiss for after open — REJECTED (opening a panel then instantly closing it reads as a glitch; ignore is cleaner).

PITFALLS: flag must clear on EVERY exit path (switch, hidePanels, overlay pre-emption) or the backdrop dead-locks; panel-switch path (old slides down, new slides up) — the flag covers the whole transition.

VERIFICATION: contract spec (flag + guard); pure suite; build. STUDIO CHECK: tap backdrop rapidly while opening shop on mobile — panel completes its entrance; taps dismiss normally after.
close_reason: Completed: panelOpening guard + panelOpenToken generation counter suppress backdrop dismissal during the 0.28s open animation. Set in showPanel before backdrop.Visible; token-guarded task.delay(Theme.motion.pop.duration) clears on open-complete; hidePanels clears on every dismiss path (close/drag/Esc/overlay pre-emption). backdrop.Activated gated on (not panelOpening). 8 ClientChrome contract assertions. NOTE: code landed within commit bd95113 (concurrent same-identity session's git add swept this WIP into the kqbq.10 commit). Quality: pure 881/0, selene 0 errors/16 warnings (baseline), remote-arity OK, overlay-router OK, rojo build OK.

NO opacity/transparency changes (this codebase signals disabled via COLOR SWAP, not opacity — keep that convention). NO hover feedback on disabled controls (guard MouseEnter like the context-menu at ~:739). Semantic bg:

  - surface.secondary (darker) = LOCKED-TIER/NOT-YET-AVAILABLE (mirror cl05 LOCKED).
  - status.disabled (brownish-red) = SYSTEM ERROR/CRITICAL-UNAVAILABLE (mirror the claim 'SAVING UNAVAILABLE').
Apply to the [A] debounce sites (give them a brief disabled visual during the debounce window — e.g. surface.elevated + tertiary text + Active=false, restore on re-enable) and fix the [B] gaps (claim: add Active=false while unhealthy; lock RECHARGE: add Active=false). Keep [C] reference patterns as-is (already conform). kqbq.18.2 contract spec: assert Theme.color.status.disabled + Theme.color.text.tertiary referenced; assert debounce sites set Active=false; assert claim adds Active=false when not storeHealthy. title: Design question: money green vs status good green are near-identical — differentiate or merge

title: WS-C: Minigame readability & core-loop feel — cast/bite/raid speak one visual language

Audit findings: marker glow is 75% transparent and barely visible against the track (:583) — the player stares at this 5-10s per catch; cast overlay zones are unlabeled (narrow=perfect, wide=good is learned by trial); tap gives no local acknowledgment before the server responds (~100-200ms of dead air); and the three overlays evolved separately so zone colors/labels are not a shared vocabulary (a2ug.11 unified marker MOTION; this finishes visual unification).

title: Minigame tap acknowledgment: neutral input-received flash before server responds
description:
WS-C / MINIGAME. Tap acknowledgment: neutral input-received flash (+ haptic tick on mobile).

WHY: on minigame tap the overlay closes and the player waits ~100-200ms for the server result with ZERO local acknowledgment — dead air at the most tense moment.

TARGET: instant NEUTRAL ack on tap — marker freeze + brief marker scale-pop (1.0->1.15->1.0, ~0.15s) or short neutral-white track flash — PLUS hapticTick() on mobile (the haptic system already exists; a tap with no haptic is a missed modality win). SCOPE: bite + raid taps. Cast tap already gets bar-fill feedback — VERIFY at implementation; add only if it also has dead air.

HARD RULE (DECISION-C anti-exploit posture): the ack must NEVER imply success/failure — no green/red, no zone-colored flash; outcome stays server-authoritative. If the ack is still playing when the result arrives, result presentation takes over cleanly (no double-flash).

VERIFICATION: contract spec; pure suite; build. STUDIO CHECK: throttled-network emulation — ack bridges the latency gap; no perceived input loss on desktop click or mobile tap.

title: Motion: button press feel — deepen compression to 0.94 at 0.10s (KEEP Quad Out — ease-In reasoning was physically wrong)
description:
WS-A / MOTION. Button press-down tactility.

PLAN-REVIEW CORRECTION (2026-08-01): the original bead prescribed Quad IN on the theory that a press should 'accelerate into the surface'. That physics is backwards: pressing a real button compresses a spring — resistance BUILDS with travel, so motion DECELERATES into the press. Quad OUT (starts fast, settles in) is the physically accurate model AND the perceptually responsive one (visible change begins on frame 1; ease-In's slow start reads as input lag at 100ms scales). Stripe/iOS practice agrees: press feedback is front-loaded.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG TODAY: compression depth 0.96 is subtle and duration 0.12s is a touch slow — the press reads as a gentle dip rather than a tactile click.

TARGET: keep easing Quad Out; duration 0.12 -> 0.10s; depth 0.96 -> 0.94. Release keeps EASE_POP Spring (correct rebound). Ripple + haptic wiring order untouched (5rcp.3/.4 load-bearing).

EVIDENCE: init.client.lua :985 pressTween = EASE_FAST used for Scale=0.96. Implement as a dedicated EASE_PRESS = TweenInfo.new(0.10, Quad, Out) preset so intent is named.

STUDIO A/B (record outcome in notes): if 0.94 still feels mushy on desktop hover-press combos, try 0.08s before touching easing direction.

VERIFICATION: contract spec (EASE_PRESS preset + used only at press site); pure suite; build.
acceptance_criteria: EASE_PRESS = 0.10s Quad Out exists; depth 0.94; release/ripple/haptics untouched; contract spec green; Studio A/B outcome recorded.
close_reason: Completed: Added EASE_PRESS = TweenInfo.new(0.10, Quad, Out) preset. pressTween now uses EASE_PRESS instead of EASE_FAST. Press compression depth changed 0.96 -> 0.94 for tactile click read. Release stays EASE_POP (Spring). 5 source-contract assertions added to ClientChrome.spec.lua. Quality: 674/0 pure, selene 0 errors/17 warnings (baseline), rojo build OK.

title: WS-D: Desktop modality — hover, keyboard, wide-screen; desktop is not scaled-up mobile
description:
Workstream D of EPIC 44. WHY: the operator explicitly asked for modality-specific hyper-optimization. Desktop strengths: cursor hover (progressive disclosure), physical keyboard (speed + escape hatches), screen real estate (balanced composition at any width). Audit findings: action bar shows key chips but no hover tooltips (shortcuts only discoverable via H panel), Esc cannot bail out of a cast (needs server cooperation — client-only cancel would desync the pending 2-6s bite), ultra-wide viewports leave the bottom bar as a small cluster in a vast empty strip.

SCOPE: .31 tooltip design spec (blocks .10), .10 tooltip implementation, .12 Esc-cancel design (blocks .32/.33), .32 server CancelCast, .33 client Esc wiring, .13 ultra-wide balance. KEYBOARD PHILOSOPHY: Esc = close/bail current context (panels, prompts, onboarding already work — extend to cast); tooltips = name + shortcut + one-line hint; never tooltip while a panel/minigame owns input.

title: Tooltip design spec: visuals, timing, content, keyboard parity (blocks .10)
description:
WS-D / DESKTOP (blocks .10 implementation). Decide and RECORD: (1) visual: surface.elevated bg, Theme.corners.compact, xs text, 1px stroke, elevation low; max width ~220px; (2) timing: 0.35s hover delay, 0.15s fade in (align with EASE_HOVER from .2), instant hide on leave/press; (3) content per action: NAME / one-line hint / [KEY] — strings sourced from the action definitions so tooltips never drift from bindings; (4) keyboard parity: KeyboardNav focus shows the same tooltip (gx6h synergy); (5) suppression: hidden while activePanel/minigame/context-menu owns input, during drag, on touch; (6) positioning: above button, flip below when space is short, clamp to viewport.

PLAN-REVIEW ADDITION — SCOPE NOW INCLUDES THE HUD CARD: the HUD balance card is clickable (opens aquarium) with a desktop hover lift, but nothing says it opens anything. Add a HUD tooltip variant: 'Open your aquarium — stored fish earn /sec' (live income from state; position: below the card, top-left anchored). Same shared tooltip instance, different anchor rules.

OUTPUT: decisions in notes -> .10 implements them verbatim.

Decisions: visual (surface.elevated bg, corners.compact 5px, xs/xxs text, 1px stroke, shadows.low, max 220px, arrow), timing (0.35s show delay + 0.15s Quad-Out fade EASE_TOOLTIP, instant hide), content (NAME/hint/[KEY] from a single ACTION_INFO table folded with SHORTCUT_ROWS so tooltips+H panel never drift), keyboard parity (KeyboardNav:GetFocusedElement() shows tooltip with no delay), suppression (IS_MOBILE OR activePanel OR isOverlayActive cast/bite/raid OR context-menu/drag), positioning (one shared instance, above+centered default, flip below near top, X-clamp, ZIndex 30-32 already reserved in the ladder), HUD card variant (below+left, live income via formatIncomeRate(state.incomePerSec)). Unblocks kqbq.10 (P2 tooltip impl, init.client.lua).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
TOOLTIP DESIGN SPEC (2026-08-01, GoldenEagle-Jul31) — VALIDATED against current code; kqbq.10 implements verbatim. All draft recommendations confirmed real; refinements below.

== SOURCE OF TRUTH ==
ACTIONS table (init.client.lua ~5326): each entry { id, label, short, key, color }. Keys: fish=F, store=G, collection=C, aquarium=T, quests=Q, raid=R, boat=B, help=H. SHORTCUT_ROWS (Help panel ~7376) already holds a desc per key. DECISION: kqbq.10 must fold tooltips + the H panel into ONE source so they never drift — define a single ACTION_INFO table keyed by action.id carrying { name, hint, key }, and re-derive SHORTCUT_ROWS from it. ACTION_INFO content (one-line hints, mirror SHORTCUT_ROWS intent):
  fish      name='Cast Line'      hint='Fish in the glowing zone at your dock'      key=F
  store     name='Fish Bag'       hint='Carried fish — store or sell'              key=G
  collection name='Collection'    hint='Discovered species & milestones'           key=C
  aquarium  name='My Aquarium'    hint='Your tank — stored fish earn cash/sec'     key=T
  quests    name='Quests'         hint='Active objectives & rewards'               key=Q
  raid      name='Raid Waters'    hint='Raid other players tanks for fish'         key=R
  boat      name='Spawn Boat'     hint='Cosmetic boat at your dock'                 key=B
  help      name='Shortcuts'      hint='Toggle this keyboard-shortcuts panel'      key=H

== 1. VISUAL ==
- bg: Theme.color.surface.elevated (=UIPalette surfaceHi RGB 30,43,63).
- corner: Theme.corners.compact (5px) via corner().
- text: NAME Theme.type.sizes.xs(12) Theme.type.fonts.bold Theme.color.text.primary; HINT Theme.type.sizes.xxs(11) Theme.type.fonts.med Theme.color.text.secondary. Stack NAME over HINT (UIListLayout or fixed offset).
- KEY CHIP: small rounded chip ~20x18, corner Theme.corners.snug(6), bg Theme.color.surface.primary, key letter Theme.type.fonts.bold xxs(11) Theme.color.text.tertiary — matches the button footnoteLabel style. Sits right of the NAME.
- stroke: 1px via stroke() helper, Theme.color.stroke @ transparency ~0.85.
- elevation: Theme.shadows.low (2-layer).
- max width: constant TOOLTIP_MAX_WIDTH = 220 (hard-coded; ~10-12 chars wrap). padding Theme.spacing.sm(8) x Theme.spacing.md(12).
- arrow: small 8x8 rotated square (ZIndex 31) below tooltip when shown above button, above tooltip when flipped below — optional polish; if it complicates positioning, ship without arrow in v1 (kqbq.10 may defer). DECISION: include the arrow (cheap, anchors the tooltip to the button).

== 2. TIMING ==
- show delay: 0.35s hover via task.delay; CANCEL the pending show on MouseLeave/press/suppression (clear the handle).
- fade-in: 0.15s, BackgroundTransparency 1->0 + child TextTransparency 1->0, EASE = TweenInfo.new(0.15, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out) (define EASE_TOOLTIP; 25% faster than EASE_HOVER 0.2s so the tooltip leads the button-hover lift).
- hide: INSTANT (Visible=false + cancel pending show + cancel fade tween) on MouseLeave/press/any suppression. No fade-out (snappiness; avoids lingering over a closed panel).

== 3. CONTENT ==
NAME (ACTION_INFO[id].name) / one-line HINT (ACTION_INFO[id].hint) / [KEY] chip (ACTION_INFO[id].key). Strings sourced ONLY from ACTION_INFO so tooltips never drift from the H panel (see SOURCE OF TRUTH). No hardcoded tooltip strings ad hoc.

== 4. KEYBOARD PARITY (gx6h synergy) ==
KeyboardNav:GetFocusedElement() (KeyboardNav.lua) returns the focused GuiButton. When it matches an actionButtons[id], show that button's tooltip IMMEDIATELY (NO 0.35s delay — keyboard/gamepad focus is deliberate) via the same show path; hide on focus change/blur. The existing 3px accent UIStroke (KeyboardNav:ApplyFocus) stays; the tooltip supplements it. No new KeyboardNav API needed — just poll GetFocusedElement() on a focus-change signal (extend KeyboardNav to expose a focus-changed event, or check in the existing input loop).

== 5. SUPPRESSION ==
Never show + instantly hide when: IS_MOBILE (no hover tooltips on touch); activePanel ~= nil (any panel open); isOverlayActive('cast') or isOverlayActive('bite') or isOverlayActive('raid') (a minigame owns input); OR the context menu is open (check the existing context-menu active flag if present). Also suppress during an active drag. Cancel any pending 0.35s show when a suppressor becomes true. Recommended predicate: local suppress = IS_MOBILE or activePanel ~= nil or isOverlayActive('cast') or isOverlayActive('bite') or isOverlayActive('raid').

== 6. POSITIONING ==
- ONE shared tooltip instance (created once, parented to screenGui), repositioned per button (no per-button instances). Active=false so it never intercepts mouse / breaks MouseLeave.
- default: ABOVE the button, horizontally centered on it; if space above < tooltip height + arrow, FLIP below; clamp X so the tooltip stays within the viewport (shift toward center if it would overflow an edge). Use button.AbsolutePosition/AbsoluteSize + workspace.CurrentViewportSize (or the screenGui AbsoluteSize).
- recompute on ViewportSize change (rotation/resize) via the existing viewport-change handler.
- ZIndex 30 (container) / 31 (arrow) / 32 (label+chip) — the canonical ladder already RESERVES 30-39 for tooltips (above panels 26-27, below overlays 40-43 + toasts 55-57). Confirmed.

== 7. HUD CARD VARIANT ==
The HUD balance card (hud frame @ Position 0,14/SAFE_TOP+6, Size 224x78 desktop; hudClick ZIndex 4, opens aquarium on Activated, hover-lift via EASE_FAST) gets a tooltip:
- content: NAME 'My Aquarium' + HINT 'Open your tank — stored fish earn ' + formatIncomeRate(state and state.incomePerSec or 0) (LIVE income, same source as incomeRateLabel). No KEY chip (it is a click target, not a hotkey) — instead a tiny 'click' affordance is optional; DECISION: no chip, the lift already signals clickability.
- positioning: BELOW the card (card is top-left so above would overflow the top edge), LEFT-aligned to the card (anchor x = hud.AbsolutePosition.X), top edge at hud.AbsolutePosition.Y + hud.AbsoluteSize.Y + Theme.spacing.xs(4). Same ZIndex 30-32.
- timing/suppression: same 0.35s show delay, 0.15s fade, instant hide; suppress on panel/minigame/mobile. Same shared instance, different anchor rule (below+left vs above+centered).

== IMPL NOTES for kqbq.10 ==
- Desktop-only guard (IS_MOBILE) at the top of the show path.
- Reuse makeButton's MouseEnter/MouseLeave for the trigger; do NOT re-parent buttons.
- Keep one shared tooltip + one task.delay show handle + one fade tween; always cancel both before starting a new show.
- Contract spec (ClientChrome.spec.lua or a new Tooltip.spec): assert EASE_TOOLTIP 0.15s, TOOLTIP_MAX_WIDTH=220, ZIndex 30, the suppression predicate, ACTION_INFO sourced (names/keys match ACTIONS), HUD variant uses formatIncomeRate(state.incomePerSec).
- STUDIO CHECK (fold into orpl/rswb): hover all 7 desktop buttons + the HUD card; 0.35s delay feels right; never sticks; never overlaps an open panel; flips below near the top edge; keyboard focus shows the tooltip with no delay; mobile shows nothing.

All 7 dimensions validated against current code — no blocking gaps.

title: WS-E: Mobile modality — thumb zones, sheets, scroll affordances, density
description:
Workstream E of EPIC 44. WHY: mobile is the dominant Roblox modality; it must feel NATIVE, not ported. Audit findings: the landscape action stack is scrollable when it overflows (a2ug.17 made buttons reachable) but NOTHING signals scrollability — the bottom button looks cut off; scrollbars (4px, text.tertiary) are always visible on lists = visual clutter on a small screen; bottom sheets have drag-to-dismiss (90px threshold) but no grab-handle affordance so discoverability is poor; 52px min-height toasts stack up and eat a short viewport.

SCOPE: .8 stack scroll fade-edge affordance, .9 scrollbar auto-hide on idle, .34 bottom-sheet grab handle + first-open hint, .16 toast density. HARD RULES: 44px minimum touch targets (TouchTargets.spec must stay green); respect SAFE_TOP/notch insets; landscape phones (~375px height) are the binding constraint — test every change against them.

title: Bottom-sheet grab-handle affordance + first-open hint
description: WS-E / MOBILE. Mobile panels are drag-to-dismiss bottom sheets (90px threshold, spring-back) but NOTHING signals draggability — new players hunt for the X. Mobile-native fix: (1) grab-handle pill (36x4px, text.tertiary at ~0.5 alpha, Theme.corners.pill) centered at the top edge of every mobile panel, inside the drag zone; (2) one-time first-open hint: subtle 6px bounce of the sheet (up-down, 2 cycles, Sine InOut) the FIRST time any panel opens in a session — teaches the gesture without a word. PITFALLS: handle must not intercept the drag (it lives inside the existing drag-detection zone; verify InputBegan routing still reaches the panel drag handler); keep handle clear of the close X (top-right) and title; hide handle on desktop. STUDIO CHECK: fresh session on phone — handle visible, bounce fires once, drag-to-dismiss discoverable without instructions.
close_reason: Completed: bottom-sheet grab-handle affordance + first-open hint. (1) Grab-handle pill matched to spec: 36x4, text.tertiary @0.5, Theme.corners.pill, centered at top edge, decorative Frame (never intercepts drag). (2) One-time first-open bounce hint: 6px up-down, 2 cycles (1 reversing repeat), Sine InOut 0.3s, fired after the pop entrance settles, once per session, mobile-only. 7 ClientChrome contract assertions. Quality: pure 930/0, selene 0/16 baseline, rojo build OK. STUDIO CHECK: fresh session on phone — handle visible, bounce fires once, drag-to-dismiss discoverable.

title: WS-F: Delight, empty states & UI performance — the gasp factor without the jank
description:

title: Preserve list scroll position across panel close/reopen
description:

title: Reconcile GradientLibrary tuned colors with UIPalette + fix HUD gradient seam
description:
WS-F / VISUAL LANGUAGE (added in plan review 2026-08-01). WHY: 6 gradient presets use tuned Color3.fromRGB values that exist nowhere in UIPalette (GradientLibrary.lua ~:66-99 — e.g. surface.default starts 26,38,57 vs palette surface 20,30,46). Worst case: the HUD card sets BackgroundColor3 = surface.primary (bg 13,20,31) then applies surface.hud gradient starting 24,36,54 — UIGradient blends toward the gradient keys, so the card's top edge is visibly BRIGHTER than its base with a muddy discontinuity. Token-discipline rule from DESIGN_SYSTEM: palette is the single source of truth.

TARGET: for each tuned gradient color, either (a) promote it into UIPalette.colors as a named token (preferred when the tuning is intentional — document why) or (b) re-derive it from existing tokens via Lerp. Fix the HUD seam specifically: align surface.hud gradient's start key with the card's base color (or drop the base to match the gradient's visual midpoint). Record decisions in notes; .23.1 doc update records the final language.

PITFALLS: gradients are multiplicative-perceptual — verify on dark panels in Studio, not by math alone; Contrast.spec may need new cases if any text sits on a re-tokened gradient.

VERIFICATION: contract spec (no raw fromRGB in GradientLibrary outside a documented exception list); pure suite; build. STUDIO CHECK: HUD card top/bottom continuity; panel gradients match their surfaces.
notes:
DECISIONS (2026-08-01 GoldenEagle-Jul31):
1. surfaceMid (26,38,57) promoted to UIPalette as named token — intentional mid-surface highlight between surface (20,30,46) and surfaceHi (30,43,63). surface.default gradient now references UI.surfaceMid.

title: Motion: desktop hover runs at press speed (0.12s) — should be deliberate ~0.2s via EASE_HOVER
description:
WS-A / MOTION. Desktop hover pacing.

WHY: hover tweens (scale 1.02, color lighten, glow, shadow layers) run at EASE_FAST 0.12s — identical to press speed. Hover should signal I am interactive, deliberately; at press speed it reads twitchy and is indistinguishable from the press itself. Desktop-only (IS_MOBILE guard already exists).

EVIDENCE: init.client.lua :1013+ MouseEnter/MouseLeave tweens all EASE_FAST (scale/color/glow/shadow_x).

TARGET: introduce EASE_HOVER = TweenInfo.new(0.2, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out) and route ALL hover tweens through it. Press keeps its own preset (.2); the two become perceptually distinct: hover = smooth invitation, press = tactile snap.

PITFALLS: (1) hoverShadows loop tweens each layer — change the shared preset, not per-layer math; (2) leave MouseLeave return-to-rest on the same preset for symmetry; (3) do not alter hover TARGET values (1.02 scale, 0.1 lighten, 0.9 glow) — only pacing.

VERIFICATION: contract spec; pure suite; build. STUDIO CHECK: sweep cursor across action bar + panel buttons; motion smooth and intentional, no flicker at boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: EASE_HOVER preset exists; all MouseEnter/MouseLeave tweens use it; press path untouched; contract spec green.
close_reason: Completed: Added EASE_HOVER = TweenInfo.new(0.2, Quad, Out) preset. All 8 hover/leave tweens (scale, color, glow, shadow x2 enter + x2 leave) changed from EASE_FAST to EASE_HOVER. Press path stays on EASE_PRESS (0.10s) — perceptually distinct from hover (0.2s). 9 source-contract assertions added to ClientChrome.spec.lua (8 positive + 1 negative). title: Feedback: ripple is hardcoded white — invisible on light (secondary/ghost) buttons; derive from button luminance
description:
WS-B / FEEDBACK. Adaptive ripple color.

WHY: the press ripple is hardcoded white (:915) — on light backgrounds (secondary/ghost buttons, surface.elevated) white-on-light is invisible, so those buttons give NO press flash. Stripe rule: every input acknowledged, on every background. This is also one of only ~3 remaining raw Color3.fromRGB sites outside UIPalette/Theme — finishing it advances the token-discipline goal.

EVIDENCE: init.client.lua :915 ripple.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255,255,255) unconditionally. (Sibling :1225 shimmer white is CORRECT — shimmer sits on dark skeleton tiles; leave it.)

TARGET: compute perceived luminance of button.BackgroundColor3 at press time (0.299R+0.587G+0.114B); dark button -> white ripple (current), light button -> dark ripple (Theme.color.text.primary or ink). Keep size/expansion/0.35s fade identical.

PITFALLS: (1) compute at PRESS time, not construction — button bg can change with state (shop affordable/unaffordable swaps colors); (2) respect the existing ripple transparency envelope — only the color adapts; (3) ripple parent clips — do not change ZIndex/ClipDescendants.

VERIFICATION: contract spec asserting luminance branch; pure suite; build. STUDIO CHECK: press primary (dark) vs ghost/secondary (light) — ripple visible on both.
acceptance_criteria: Ripple color derives from live button luminance; white-on-dark and dark-on-light both visible; no raw literal left at :915; shimmer untouched.
close_reason: Completed: Ripple color now derives from button luminance (0.299R + 0.587G + 0.114B). Dark buttons (lum < 0.55) get white ripple, light buttons (lum > 0.55) get ink-dark ripple. Verified against all key button colors: accent(0.530→white), good(0.574→ink), bad(0.552→ink), surface(0.113→white). Code committed in a56a5a2, 4 source-contract specs committed in 3129023.

Default to the settle-alpha approach unless implementer finds it noisy in Studio.

title: Mobile: action-stack scroll affordance — fade edge + hint when stack is scrollable (short landscape)

title: SAFE_TOP computed once at load; HUD never adapts to orientation/viewport changes
description:
## Summary

SAFE_TOP (src/client/init.client.lua ~:417) is computed ONCE at module load by calculateSafeTop(). It reads workspace.CurrentCamera (nil-safe fallback to 1920x1080) for landscape detection and GuiService:GetGuiInset() for notch height. Neither is ever re-read, so a device rotation (portrait <-> landscape changes both the inset and the isLandscape branch) permanently misaligns every HUD element positioned with SAFE_TOP (hud, carryPill, toastHost, sellStorePrompt, raidBanner — 9 call sites).

## Root cause + why fixing is NOT trivial

Recomputing SAFE_TOP is easy; the hard part is that all 9 consuming positions are assigned ONCE at UI construction (e.g. hud.Position = UDim2.new(0, 14, 0, SAFE_TOP + 6)). A dynamic fix requires either a layout callback registry or converting each to a function that recalculates on ViewportSize changes — touching 9 unrelated UI sections. That blast radius is why this was deliberately scoped OUT of the fxfx repair.

## Why P3 (not a regression)

This behavior is IDENTICAL to pre-fxfx HEAD (old code: local SAFE_TOP = math.max(inset.Y, IS_MOBILE and 12 or 8) — also computed once, also never updated, without even the landscape branch). The fxfx work strictly improved correctness (orientation-aware + notch compensation at load). The remaining gap is a pre-existing architectural limitation, not a new bug.

## Proposed approach (for whoever picks this up)

Add a bindViewportWidth-style handler that, on ViewportSize change, recomputes SAFE_TOP and calls a registry of reposition callbacks — OR (simpler) only recompute on camera swap/orientation change events, not every resize. Audit finding #2, HarborHeist-Dev session 2026-07-30.
close_reason: Fixed in 006d387: SAFE_TOP is now mutable and recomputed via refreshSafeTop() on any viewport change (wired into the existing bindViewportWidth handler). 5 reposition consumers registered (hud, carryPill, toastHost, sellStorePrompt, raidBanner); onboardingPrompt + mobile stack already re-derive in their own resize handlers.

description:
## Goal

Client UI has zero headless coverage (pure specs don't load the DataModel; E2E drives server seams). description:
Umbrella for end-to-end integration test scripts that drive the REAL game (real server services, real remotes, real DataStore where available) and produce GREAT, DETAILED structured logs for every run.

## CURRENT STATE (verified 2026-07-22, ChartreuseFox)
- No e2e scripts, no test harness, no logging infrastructure. Manual playthrough only (HarborHeist_test.rbxlx).

## WHAT "E2E" MEANS HERE
- A test client script inside a real Roblox server session drives the REAL RemoteEvents/RemoteFunctions (RequestCast, SubmitCatchInput, RequestStoreFish, RequestClaimIncome, RequestPurchaseUpgrade, RequestRaidAttempt, etc. — 11 events + 17 functions in src/server/Remotes.lua) and asserts on REAL server state via GetState snapshots and observed events.
- No service is stubbed. Where a flow needs money/time, the harness uses real server-side paths (income accrual, session credit through the same code the income loop uses, or the real RaidService window API) — never client-side forgery.

## STRUCTURED LOGGING (the point of the epic)
- A TestLogger module emits JSONL: ISO8601 timestamp, level, scenario id, step id, message, data payload, and full state dumps on assertion failure.
- Every scenario logs: setup, each remote call (name + args + response), each assertion (expected vs actual), timing, and a final summary (pass/fail counts, durations).
- Artifacts land in testlogs/ (gitignored) and are captured by CI.

## KNOWN ENVIRONMENT LIMIT (must be respected)
This machine (2026-07-22) has NO Roblox Studio and no run-in-roblox. TASK 19.1 includes the runner spike (install/verify, or document the exact external requirement). ## SCOPE (10 tasks)
19.1 harness+logger -> 19.2 lifecycle -> 19.3 fishing -> 19.4 aquarium economy -> 19.5 shop -> 19.6 persistence round-trip + v1->v2 migration -> 19.7 lock/defense -> 19.8 raid (19.8.1 automated single-player, 19.8.2 two-player runbook) -> 19.9 abuse/rate-limit -> 19.10 CI+docs.

## DONE WHEN
One command runs the whole suite headless (or the documented Studio runner), every scenario emits JSONL logs a human can audit line-by-line, failures dump full state, and CI gates on exit code.
