title: TASK 19.1.1: TestLogger module — JSONL structured logs, state dumps, summaries
description:
Deliverable: tests/e2e/TestLogger.lua (shared by all scenarios).

## REQUIRED FEATURES
1. JSONL events, one per line: {ts (ISO8601 UTC), level (DEBUG/INFO/STEP/ASSERT/ERROR), scenario, step, msg, data}.
2. Scenario lifecycle API: startScenario(id, description), step(id, description), assertEq(name, expected, actual) / assertTrue / assertNear(tolerance), finish() — every assert logs expected vs actual; on failure ALSO logs a full state dump (GetState snapshot + relevant local state).
3. Remote-call logging helper: wrapRemote(name, fn, args) logs the call args, response payload, and latency for every remote invocation — this is what makes the logs 'great and detailed' for audits.
4. Sinks: print() (captured by runner stdout) AND file append under testlogs/<scenario>-<runid>.jsonl where the environment allows file writes (document where it cannot).
5. Summary report: per-run totals (scenarios pass/fail, asserts run, durations) printed last and written to testlogs/summary-<runid>.json.
6. Timer API: timeIt(name, fn) for perf-sensitive flows (income tick timing).

NO external deps; pure Luau so it runs in both lune and DataModel buckets.

title: TASK 19.9: E2E — abuse & anti-exploit battery (spam, forgery, bad payloads)
description:
Scenario: tests/e2e/scenarios/Abuse.lua. The hostile-client suite — everything an exploiter would try, driven through REAL remotes.

## CASES (each: action -> expected rejection -> assert zero state mutation -> assert logSuspicious/rate-limit side effects per real contract)
1. Spam every RemoteFunction past its limit (cast/store/sell/buy/lock/raid_attempt/get_state at the real RATE_LIMITS) -> rate_limited responses; server suspicious-log entries asserted via AuditLogService where visible.
2. Forged fishing tier: SubmitCatchInput claiming perfect with out-of-zone position -> server-derived tier used (mirror of 18.9.3 at the wire level).
3. Impossible timing: SubmitCatchInput/SubmitRaidResult far outside the real windows -> rejected.
4. Bad payloads: wrong types (string for number), negative amounts, huge numbers, nils, tables-with-holes -> rejected, no crash; server stays healthy (subsequent GetState OK).
5. Unknown/never-registered remote names invoked via raw RemoteFunction path -> error handled (assert server does not crash).
6. Replay: same purchase/store request fired twice rapidly -> exactly one effect.
7. Currency forgery: any client attempt to set Coins directly (no such remote exists — assert NO remote exposes it; rg the client for StateChanged writes and assert client never mutates server state).

LOG: every forged call's args + server response verbatim; this file doubles as the security audit trail.

- [ ] All 7 case groups passing + logged
- [ ] Server health asserted after the battery (GetState still OK)
- [ ] Zero-mutation proof attached to every rejection

title: EPIC 8: Raid & Defense System — Scheduled Opt-In
description:
PRD PVP-01..PVP-12 + Recommended V1 Raid Rule. MASSIVE rework of the current always-on theft.

Current: any player can steal from any unlocked aquarium anytime (50% chance, 20s cooldown). PRD demands: scheduled raid windows (every 20-30 min, last 5 min), opt-in via Raid Waters pier or dock flag, new-player protection (PVP-01), lock tools, cooldowns, per-victim immunity, legendary protection, capped losses, server-only validation.

This is the 'deliberate spice, not the entire product' — bounded tension that creates social stories without griefing. FILES: src/server/RaidService.lua (new, replaces steal logic in AquariumService.handleSteal)

## BACKGROUND & JUSTIFICATION
Part of the Harbor Heist V1 build — migrating the current prototype to full PRD compliance (see PRD.md). The current codebase is a working server-authoritative prototype with 5 rarity tiers, basic cast/store/sell, passive income, and basic theft/lock PvP. The PRD demands a richer experience: structured data, 12-20 species, timing minigame, claimable income, collection book, upgrade tree, scheduled opt-in raids, onboarding, analytics, and anti-exploit. Every bead serves the overarching goal: a cozy fishing-aquarium game with optional bounded PvP heists that creates social stories without griefing.

## PRD TRACEABILITY
See PRD.md for the authoritative spec. PRD requirement IDs (e.g. FISH-01, AQUA-03, PVP-05) are referenced in task acceptance criteria.

title: DEC-1: Passive income scope (online-only vs capped offline)
description:
PRD Open Decision #1. AQUA-04 says 'accrues only while in-game for V1' but the income model section implies elapsed-time calculation with a cap — tension.

RECOMMENDATION: V1 online-only accrual with a claimable income pool (don't auto-add to cash), capped to prevent extreme accumulation. Offline earnings deferred to V1.1.

UX RISK (important): Switching from auto-income to claimable income is a significant behavior change. Players used to cash ticking up passively may feel 'punished' if they forget to claim. Mitigation: make CLAIM button prominent, auto-claim on logout save, show a glowing '+$X ready to claim' indicator. If playtesting shows confusion, consider a hybrid: small auto-claim threshold + manual claim for the rest.

BLOCKS: Epic 5 income model + DataStore key versioning (1.6). PRD refs: AQUA-04, AQUA-05.
notes: DECISION: V1 online-only accrual + claimable pool. UnclaimedIncome accumulates while player is online, capped at MAX_UNCLAIMED. Player must CLAIM via button. Auto-claim on logout save. Does NOT persist on load (resets to 0). Offline earnings deferred to V1.1. Rationale: simplest exploit-resistant model that still creates the claim interaction the PRD wants (AQUA-05).

title: Deep codebase review — findings, fixes, and hardening roadmap
description:
## Background

A comprehensive, first-principles code review of the entire harbor_heist codebase was conducted on 2026-08-01. Every file in src/ was read and analyzed: all 17 server services (~8,500 lines), all shared modules (GameConfig, PlayerProfile, FishInstance, FishDefinitions, UIPalette, PanelAnimation, ZoneDefinitions), the 8,617-line client init.client.lua, AnimationSystem (847 lines), GradientLibrary (194 lines), KeyboardNav (319 lines), and the full test suite (18 pure-spec files + 12 studio specs).

Three immediate fixes were applied in commit 1252fc7 (bead harborheist-6qps, now closed):
1. FishingService bite-fired guard — handleSubmitCatchInput could process a catch before the bite callback fired BiteEvent
2. KeyboardNav connection cleanup — Enable() leaked InputBegan connections on each cycle
3. Duplicate comment removal from init.client.lua

This epic tracks ALL remaining findings from that review — connection leaks, defensive coding gaps, design decisions to document, performance evaluations, and architecture strengths to preserve as institutional knowledge.

## Project Context

Harbor Heist is in a closed V1 test phase, ready for launch pending final balance/decision finalization. The codebase is server-authoritative with 17 services, DataStore persistence with v1→v2 migration, anti-exploit rate limiting, and a heavily-polished mobile-first UI. The review's overarching goal is to ensure no correctness, memory, or security defects remain that could surface in production under real player load.

## Scope Summary

### Connection Leaks (P2-P3) — highest priority for production:
Six distinct connection-leak patterns were identified across the client. Each creates Roblox signal connections (GetPropertyChangedSignal, InputBegan, MouseButton1Down, Tween.Completed) without storing the connection handle for later disconnection. Over a long session (hours), these accumulate memory and orphaned closures that fire on destroyed instances.

### Defensive Coding (P3) — medium priority:
Two audit tasks: (a) client state.* accesses without nil guards in 3 specific locations, (b) DockManager direct property access at 3 locations without FindFirstChild safety.

### Design Decisions (P4) — documentation:
Three findings where current behavior is a deliberate V1 design choice rather than a bug. These need documentation so future agents don't "fix" them without understanding the tradeoff:
- AntiExploitService suspiciousLog never cleared on leave (intentional audit retention)
- StateSync full-snapshot push every income tick (V1 simplicity over delta-sync complexity)
- recomputeMobileToastCap infinite 1Hz poll (acceptable for V1 single-client)

### Architecture Assessment (P4) — institutional knowledge:
Document the patterns that work well so they're preserved: DataManager's rejoin-race protection, RaidService's TOCTOU fish-transfer, server-authoritative catch/raid resolution, sanitize() depth, v1→v2 migration with rollback anchor.

## Dependency Structure

All child issues are parent-child dependents of this epic. No cross-issue blocking dependencies exist — each finding is independently actionable. Fix order should follow priority (P2 leaks first, P3 audits second, P4 docs last).

title: Toast AbsoluteSize connection never disconnected — per-toast memory leak
description:
## Finding

**File:** src/client/init.client.lua:2181
**Severity:** P2 (Important — accumulates over session)

```lua
toast:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize"):Connect(function()
    wrap.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, math.max(MIN_TOAST_H, toast.AbsoluteSize.Y))
end)
```

## Root Cause

Each toast created by showToastDirect() connects a GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize") handler to size the wrapper frame. The connection is never stored in a variable and never disconnected in the dismiss() function (line 2304). When the toast is dismissed and wrap:Destroy() is called (line 2318), the connection becomes orphaned — it still references the destroyed `toast` and `wrap` instances.

## Impact

Over a long play session, a player receives dozens to hundreds of toasts (catch notifications, raid alerts, quest completions, shop confirmations, income claims). Each leaked connection keeps a closure alive in memory with references to destroyed GUI objects. Symptoms:
- Gradual memory growth (each closure + its captured upvalues)
- Potential errors after destruction if AbsoluteSize changes fire on a destroyed instance (Roblox may suppress this, but the closure still holds references)
- The `activeToastCount` decrement and queue drain work correctly (dismissed guard + per-call local), so functional behavior is fine — this is purely a resource leak

## Fix Approach

Store the connection in a local variable and disconnect it in the dismiss() closure:

```lua
local sizeConn = toast:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize"):Connect(function()
    wrap.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, math.max(MIN_TOAST_H, toast.AbsoluteSize.Y))
end)
```

Then in dismiss() (around line 2304), before the fade tween:
```lua
if sizeConn then
    sizeConn:Disconnect()
    sizeConn = nil
end
```

## Considerations

- The connection fires once on initial layout (AutomaticSize sets the height), then rarely again unless the toast text changes (it doesn't post-creation). So the per-toast overhead is small, but it's still a leak with no upper bound.
- Roblox may garbage-collect the connection if both the signal source and the callback's captured refs are destroyed, but relying on GC for connection cleanup is explicitly discouraged in the Roblox docs — connections should be explicitly disconnected.
- The toast system already has excellent dismiss-time cleanup (the dismissed guard, per-call local dismiss, queue drain). This is the one gap in an otherwise well-structured lifecycle.

## Project Context

The toast system is the primary notification surface for the entire game — catches, raids, quests, shop, economy, and onboarding all funnel through it. A player in an active raid window with frequent catches could see 10+ toasts per minute. Over a 30-minute session, that's 300+ leaked connections. Not game-breaking for V1 closed test, but should be fixed before open launch.
acceptance_criteria: toast:GetPropertyChangedSignal connection stored in local sizeConn; sizeConn:Disconnect() called in dismiss() before fade tween; sizeConn set to nil after disconnect; no behavioral change — toast sizing works identically; pure specs pass + coverage gate green; selene 0 errors on init.client.lua
close_reason: Fixed: toast AbsoluteSize connection now stored as local sizeConn (init.client.lua:2209) and disconnected+nil'd in dismiss() before the fade tween (:2338-2341), behind the dismissed guard so double-dismiss can't re-disconnect. No behavioral change — wrap sizing logic untouched. 5 ClientChrome source-contract assertions incl. source-ordering (dismiss < disconnect < fade) and single-connection uniqueness. Quality: pure 965/0, coverage gate green, selene 0e/16w baseline, rojo build OK.

title: StateSync snapshot optimization — evaluate delta-sync for income ticks
description:
## Finding

**File:** src/server/StateSync.lua (snapshot function) + src/server/AquariumService.lua (startIncomeLoop)
**Severity:** P4 (Performance evaluation — V1 design tradeoff, not a bug)

The income loop (AquariumService.startIncomeLoop) pushes a full stateSync.push(session) to every player with income > 0 every IncomeTickSeconds (1 second). Each push calls StateSync.snapshot(), which builds a complete state table including:

- carriedFish: array of up to 5 FishInstance records (~100 bytes each)
- storedFish: array of up to 75 FishInstance records (~100 bytes each)
- liveWellCounts: per-rarity count map
- All profile fields (cash, levels, timers, onboarding, etc.)

For a player with a full aquarium (75 fish), this is ~7.5KB of fish data + ~1KB profile data = ~8.5KB per push, every second.

## Analysis

This is a V1 design tradeoff, not a bug:

1. **Correctness**: The full snapshot ensures the client always has the complete state. Delta-sync protocols introduce complexity (versioning, ordering, dropped-packet recovery) that V1 doesn't need.
2. **Simplicity**: The client render() function can treat every StateChanged event as a complete state replacement — no merge logic, no delta application.
3. **Actual payload**: For most V1 players, the aquarium isn't full. A new player with 5 stored fish sends ~500 bytes of fish data + 1KB profile = ~1.5KB/s. This is well within Roblox's remote bandwidth limits.
4. ** harborheist-os9 optimization**: The income loop already skips pushes when income is 0 (empty aquarium, locked, etc.), so only players with active income are pushed. This was a significant optimization from the original "push every second regardless" design.
5. **Fish array is the bottleneck**: The storedFish and carriedFish arrays are the largest payload. A delta-sync would send only the changed entries (fish added/removed), but that requires the client to maintain state and merge deltas.

## Evaluation Criteria

A delta-sync optimization would be warranted IF:
- Average concurrent players (CCU) × snapshot size exceeds Roblox's per-server remote bandwidth budget
- Profiling shows the snapshot building/parsing is a measurable CPU cost
- Players report rubber-banding or desync from dropped snapshots

None of these are observed in V1. The full-snapshot design is appropriate for the closed test phase.

## Considerations

- If delta-sync is eventually implemented, the natural split is:
  - Income tick: send only {cash, unclaimedIncome, incomePerSec} (the 3 fields that change every tick)
  - Action-driven pushes (store/sell/claim/lock/raid): send full snapshot (infrequent, state actually changed)
- This split would reduce the per-second payload from ~8.5KB to ~100 bytes for income-only ticks.
- The harborheist-os9 optimization (skip zero-income pushes) already reduced the push frequency significantly. The kqbq.15 shop signature skip reduced client-side render cost on unchanged state.

## Recommendation

Do NOT implement delta-sync for V1. Document the tradeoff so future optimization work has the context:

```lua
-- V1 DESIGN: full-snapshot push every income tick. This sends ~1-8KB/player/sec
-- depending on aquarium size. Acceptable for V1 CCU targets. If CCU grows or
-- profiling shows bandwidth pressure, split into:
--   income tick: push {cash, unclaimedIncome, incomePerSec} only
--   action push: full snapshot (store/sell/claim/lock/raid)
-- See harborheist-review-aug2026-6yp6.10 for evaluation context.
```

## Project Context

StateSync.snapshot is the single serialization point for all client-visible state. The income loop is the highest-frequency caller (1Hz per player with income). The full-snapshot design was chosen for V1 simplicity and correctness. This task documents the tradeoff and defers optimization to post-launch when real CCU data is available to make the decision.
close_reason: Superseded by 6yp6.9 (merged). The StateSync snapshot optimization evaluation is one of three V1 design decision documentation tasks consolidated into 6yp6.9. All three are comment-only changes that one agent can do in a single session.

title: recomputeMobileToastCap — evaluate lifecycle of 1Hz viewport poll loop
description:
## Finding

**File:** src/client/init.client.lua:2148-2156
**Severity:** P4 (Design evaluation — acceptable for V1, evaluate for V2)

```lua
recomputeMobileToastCap()
task.spawn(function()
    while true do
        recomputeMobileToastCap()
        task.wait(1)
    end
end)
```

## Analysis

A 1Hz infinite loop polls the camera viewport size and recomputes the mobile toast visible cap (how many toasts can fit before the overflow chip shows). The loop:

1. Runs on every client (but recomputeMobileToastCap early-returns on desktop — `if not IS_MOBILE then return end`)
2. Polls workspace.CurrentCamera.ViewportSize every 1 second
3. Adjusts MAX_VISIBLE_TOASTS_MOBILE (clamped 1-3) based on viewport height

The loop is correct and the computation is cheap (one multiplication + clamp). The concern is lifecycle:

- The loop runs for the entire client session (no exit condition)
- It's a coroutine (task.spawn), so it doesn't block the main thread
- It's the only consumer of viewport size for toast density

## Considerations

- **Why polling instead of event-driven?** workspace.CurrentCamera.ViewportSize changes on screen resize / rotation / device change. A GetPropertyChangedSignal("ViewportSize") connection would be more efficient than polling. However, the poll is 1Hz (not per-frame) and the computation is O(1), so the overhead is negligible.
- **Exit condition**: The `while true do` pattern is standard in Roblox client scripts — the script lives for the client session and is garbage-collected when the client disconnects. No explicit exit needed.
- **Multiple loops**: This adds one more infinite loop to the client. The client already has: the render loop (RunService.RenderStepped or heartbeat), the scrollbar auto-hide idle polls (6 × task.spawn loops), and the income pulse loop. One more 1Hz poll is not a problem.

## Recommendation

Two options:
1. **Keep as-is (V1)**: The 1Hz poll is acceptable. No change needed. Document why it's a poll instead of event-driven.
2. **Event-driven (V2 polish)**: Replace with a GetPropertyChangedSignal("ViewportSize") connection + a CurrentCamera change watcher (matching the aquarium viewport pattern). This eliminates the poll but adds 2 connections (which need the cleanup pattern from 6yp6.4).

For V1, keeping the poll is simpler and the performance impact is negligible. The event-driven refactor would be a natural companion to fixing the aquarium viewport connection leak (6yp6.4).

## Project Context

The toast density system was added in harborheist-kqbq.16 for mobile landscape phones where 3 toasts of 52px cover too much of the viewport. The 1Hz poll handles screen rotation smoothly (toast cap adjusts within 1 second of rotation). The design is appropriate for V1 — this task is documentation only, no change needed unless paired with the aquarium viewport fix.
close_reason: Superseded by 6yp6.9 (merged). The recomputeMobileToastCap poll evaluation is one of three V1 design decision documentation tasks consolidated into 6yp6.9. The related dependency to 6yp6.4 (viewport connection) is preserved in the merged bead's description.

title: Code review architecture assessment — document strengths and patterns to preserve
description:
## Purpose

Document the architecture strengths and well-designed patterns identified during the deep code review, so future agents and developers understand what works well and why it should be preserved.

## Assessment Summary

The harbor_heist codebase is well-architected for a V1 multiplayer game. The code demonstrates thorough attention to race conditions, security, data integrity, and edge-case handling. No critical security or data integrity bugs were found during the review. The three fixes applied (6qps) were correctness and memory hygiene, not security or data-loss issues.

## Patterns to Preserve

### 1. DataManager Rejoin-Race Protection (src/server/DataManager.lua)

The most sophisticated pattern in the codebase. Three interlocking mechanisms prevent data loss from the rapid-leave-rejoin race:

- **activeSessionsByUserId[userId]**: Maps UserId → active session. A deferred leave-save checks this inside UpdateAsync — if the player has already rejoined (new session replaced the old one), the stale save returns oldData unchanged (no-op). This prevents a stale leave-save from clobbering fresher rejoin data.
- **pendingSaveUserIds[userId]**: Count of in-flight saves per UserId. load() waits (bounded to 16s) for pending saves to complete before reading GetAsync, so a rapid rejoin doesn't load stale pre-save data.
- **saveDirty coalescing**: When a checkpoint save arrives while another save is in-flight, it sets saveDirty instead of queuing. The in-flight save's trailing write picks up all accumulated changes, collapsing N rapid checkpoint calls into at most 2 sequential DataStore writes.

All three are keyed by UserId (stable across rejoins), not Player object (destroyed on leave). This is correct and well-documented in comments.

### 2. FishingService Cast Generation Token (src/server/FishingService.lua)

The castGen[player] monotonic token solves the "uncancelable task.delay" problem elegantly:

- Each cast stamps a generation id. The task.delay bite callback captures the id at closure time.
- CancelCast bumps the generation. When the stale callback fires, `castGen[player] ~= myGen` → early return.
- This avoids the need for task.cancel (which Luau doesn't support for task.delay) and prevents stale callbacks from firing BiteEvent, notifies, or rodService.endCast on a cancelled cast.

This pattern should be used for ALL task.delay callbacks that can be invalidated by user action.

### 3. RaidService TOCTOU Fish Transfer (src/server/RaidService.lua)

The resolveRaidSuccess function implements a robust TOCTOU (Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use) defense for fish theft:

1. Weighted-pick selects a target fish from the victim's list
2. Re-find the selected fish by reference in the LIVE list (not the captured snapshot)
3. Re-validate IsRaidProtected before removal
4. Wrap the transfer (remove from victim + insert into attacker) in a pcall — if it throws between removal and insertion, the fish is rolled back to its original index
5. Post-transfer side effects (immunity, notifications, saves) are explicitly outside the transaction

This prevents fish duplication (fish in both aquariums) and fish loss (fish in neither) from partial-failure race conditions.

### 4. Server-Authoritative Catch Resolution (src/server/FishingService.lua)

The fishing catch system maintains server authority at every layer:

- Cast accuracy: client sends raw marker position [0,1]; server re-derives the tier from its OWN stored bounds
- Luck bonus: derived from server-authoritative cast bounds, not client-claimed
- Catch re-roll: server rolls rng:NextNumber() against effectiveZone — client can't achieve 100% catch rate
- Species/rarity: fully server-rolled via FishDefinitions.getRandomInZone with server-side rng
- Value/income: from FishInstance (server-created at catch time), never client-modifiable

A forged "always perfect" client is capped at the perfect-honest rate. A forged "always hit" client is capped by the re-roll. This is the correct anti-exploit design for a client-trust-minimizing game.

### 5. RaidService Minimum-Time Check (src/server/RaidService.lua)

The harborheist-yxdh minimum-time check in submitRaidResult prevents timing forgery in the raid minigame:

- The client tweens the marker from 0→1 over durationSeconds linearly
- The server records startTime when the challenge is issued
- On submission, it calculates minNeeded = position × duration (minimum time for the marker to reach the reported position)
- If elapsed < minNeeded - NETWORK_GRACE (0.5s for latency), the submission is rejected as "too_fast"

This catches bots that intercept the zone bounds and report a forged perfect position instantly — an impossible feat for a legitimate player who must wait for the marker to sweep.

### 6. DataManager Deep Sanitize (src/server/DataManager.lua)

The sanitize() function is the last line of defense against corrupted DataStore data:

- Every field is type-checked before assignment
- Numeric fields are clamped to valid ranges (coins, capacity, upgrade levels, timer timestamps)
- Fish are validated via FishInstance.validate() (instance ID, species existence, sell value, income)
- Quests are structure-validated (type, target, reward, progress)
- Onboarding flags are whitelisted to the 5 known keys (junk keys are dropped)
- Legacy v1 data is converted (flat fields → structured profile, rarity indexes → FishInstances)
- Collection milestones handle both map-form and legacy array-form
- JSON round-trip coercion is handled (tonumber on RecentTargetTimestamps string keys)

This is the correct depth for a DataStore consumer — never trust persisted data.

### 7. v1→v2 Migration with Rollback Anchor (src/server/DataManager.lua)

The migration design uses a NEW DataStore key (_v2) instead of overwriting v1:

- v2 is read first; if empty, v1 is read, sanitized, and written to v2
- v1 is left intact as a rollback anchor for the closed-test grace period
- Migration is logged (print, not warn — it's expected, not an error)
- The migrated profile is immediately persisted to v2 (deferred one frame) so a disconnect before the first autosave still persists

This is the correct pattern for a breaking format change in a live game — rollback is possible, a bad migration can't permanently corrupt the only copy.

### 8. PlayerProfile.clampCoins NaN Rejection (src/shared/PlayerProfile.lua)

The clampCoins function explicitly rejects NaN:

```lua
if value ~= value then return 0 end
```

NaN passes Lua's type() guard (type(NaN) == "number") but propagates through math.min/max/floor. (NaN < cost) is always false, so a NaN-coined player can buy everything for free. The identity check `value ~= value` is the standard NaN test (NaN is the only number not equal to itself). This is a subtle but critical security fix.

## Patterns to Watch (Not Bugs, But Risk Areas)

1. **Full-snapshot push every income tick**: Appropriate for V1, evaluate for V2 (see 6yp6.10)
2. **Infinite loops with `while true do`**: Standard in Roblox, but each adds a coroutine. Track the count.
3. **task.delay callbacks referencing player/session state**: Always check player.Parent and session validity (see the bite callback guard in FishingService and the stun callback guard in RaidService)
4. **Connection lifecycle**: The codebase has a mix of explicit-disconnect and fire-and-forget patterns. Establish a convention (see 6yp6.1-6yp6.6)

## Project Context

This architecture assessment is the positive counterpart to the bug fixes. It documents what the codebase does RIGHT so that future refactors don't accidentally remove these protections. Each pattern has a detailed comment in the source code explaining the reasoning — this document aggregates them for high-level visibility.

title: Static connection leaks in init.client.lua — scrollbar (6 sites) + action stack (1 site)
description:
## Finding

**File:** src/client/init.client.lua — 7 total call sites
**Severity:** P3 (Low — static single-creation connections, no per-action accumulation)

Two related patterns of the same defect in init.client.lua:

### Pattern 1: applyScrollbarAutoHide (6 call sites)
**Definition:** line 553 | **Callers:** lines 3474, 3909, 4310, 4830, 5017, 8125

```lua
local function applyScrollbarAutoHide(scrollingFrame)
    scrollingFrame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("CanvasPosition"):Connect(function()
        -- fade/idle logic
    end)
end
```

The connection is never returned to callers, never stored, never disconnected.

### Pattern 2: Mobile action stack (1 site)
**Line:** 5930

```lua
stack:GetPropertyChangedSignal("CanvasPosition"):Connect(function()
    -- fade visibility logic for overflow indicator
end)
```

Same pattern — connection created, handle discarded.

## Root Cause

Both are fire-and-forget decorators that assume the decorated frame's lifetime equals the session lifetime. This is true today (all 7 frames are created once at module scope and never destroyed), so the connections don't accumulate per-action. However, the connections CAN'T be cleaned up if the frames are ever destroyed, and this violates Roblox's explicit best-practice of disconnecting all signal connections.

## Impact

- 7 permanent connections for the entire client session. No per-action accumulation.
- Very low memory impact. The connections fire on scroll events but the callbacks are lightweight.
- The functional behavior is correct (scrollbar fades on idle, appears on scroll; action stack overflow indicator fades).
- This is a defensive improvement, not an active leak. The toast leak (6yp6.1) and AnimationSystem leak (6yp6.5) are the true accumulating leaks.

## Fix Approach

Return the connection from applyScrollbarAutoHide so callers CAN disconnect if needed:

```lua
local function applyScrollbarAutoHide(scrollingFrame)
    local conn = scrollingFrame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("CanvasPosition"):Connect(function()
        -- ...
    end)
    return conn
end
```

For the action stack, store in a module-level variable:
```lua
local actionStackScrollConn = stack:GetPropertyChangedSignal("CanvasPosition"):Connect(function()
    -- ...
end)
```

## Considerations

- The helper also creates a task.spawn infinite loop (1.2s idle poll). This loop runs for 6 frames × session lifetime. Acceptable for V1. A RunService.Heartbeat consolidation is a V2 optimization.
- Scrollbar auto-hide is mobile-only (desktop keeps persistent thin bar), so on desktop these connections fire but the fade logic is a no-op — minor wasted work.
- Originally tracked as two separate beads (6yp6.2 scrollbar + 6yp6.3 action stack). Merged because they're the same pattern, same file, and an agent fixing one would naturally fix both.

## Project Context

Scrollbar auto-hide was added in harborheist-kqbq.9 (mobile polish). The action stack overflow indicator was added in harborheist-kqbq.8. Both are mobile-first features where the connection management was deprioritized in favor of the visual behavior. This bead consolidates the defensive cleanup work for both into one scoped task.
acceptance_criteria: applyScrollbarAutoHide returns connection handle; action stack connection stored in module-level variable; all 7 sites have trackable connection handles; no behavioral change to scrollbar or overflow indicator; pure specs pass; selene 0 errors
close_reason: Fixed per acceptance scope: applyScrollbarAutoHide now captures + returns the CanvasPosition connection handle (init.client.lua:557, return at :577); action-stack scroll connection stored as module-level local actionStackScrollConn (:5992) with selene allow(unused_variable) annotation to hold the 16w baseline. No behavioral change; no Destroying wiring (7 frames are session-lifetime; bead scope = handle trackability). 3 ClientChrome contracts incl. def<conn<return ordering and 7-reference count (1 def + 6 calls). Quality: pure 978/0, coverage gate green, selene 0e/16w baseline, rojo build OK.

title: Mobile action stack CanvasPosition connection never disconnected
description:
## Finding

**File:** src/client/init.client.lua:5930
**Severity:** P2 (Important — persistent connection for session lifetime)

```lua
stack:GetPropertyChangedSignal("CanvasPosition"):Connect(function()
    -- fade visibility logic for mobile action stack overflow
end)
```

## Root Cause

The mobile action stack (the scrollable list of action buttons at the bottom of the mobile screen) creates a CanvasPosition connection to fade edge indicators when the stack is scrolled. The connection is created at module initialization scope and never stored in a variable or disconnected.

## Impact

- One permanent connection for the entire session. Fires on every scroll of the action stack.
- The action stack is created once and never destroyed, so this is a static leak (1 connection, not per-action).
- Very low memory impact, but follows the same anti-pattern as the scrollbar connections.

## Fix Approach

Store the connection in a module-level variable. Since the action stack is never destroyed in V1, this is a defensive improvement:

```lua
local actionStackScrollConn = stack:GetPropertyChangedSignal("CanvasPosition"):Connect(function()
    -- ...
end)
```

## Considerations

- The action stack scroll indicator is a mobile-only feature. On desktop, the connection fires but the indicator logic is a no-op.
- If the action stack is ever rebuilt (e.g. for a dynamic action system), the old connection would need to be disconnected first — this is why storing the handle matters even for single-creation patterns.

## Project Context

The mobile action stack was part of the original mobile UI layout. The scroll indicator was added for affordance (harborheist-kqbq.8). Low priority but included in the connection-leak sweep for completeness.
close_reason: Superseded by 6yp6.2 (merged). The action stack connection leak is the same pattern as the scrollbar connections — same file, same fix. Consolidated into 6yp6.2 to avoid an agent picking up two beads for one scoped task.

title: Aquarium viewport connection — stale connection not disconnected on camera change
description:
## Finding

**File:** src/client/init.client.lua:3435-3443
**Severity:** P2 (Important — accumulates on camera changes, which are rare)

```lua
if IS_MOBILE then
    local function bindAquariumFit(cam)
        if cam then
            cam:GetPropertyChangedSignal("ViewportSize"):Connect(fitAquariumPanelHeight)
        end
    end
    bindAquariumFit(workspace.CurrentCamera)
    workspace:GetPropertyChangedSignal("CurrentCamera"):Connect(bindAquariumFit)
end
```

## Root Cause

bindAquariumFit() creates a new ViewportSize connection on the camera each time it's called. The workspace.CurrentCamera property changed connection calls bindAquariumFit on every camera change. However, the OLD camera's ViewportSize connection is never disconnected — each camera change (respawn, cutscene, dock rejoin) adds a new connection while keeping the old one alive.

## Impact

- Camera changes are relatively rare in Roblox (mainly on respawn and certain transitions), so accumulation is slow.
- Each leaked connection fires fitAquariumPanelHeight on viewport size changes for a camera that's no longer active — wasted work + potential layout glitches if the old camera's ViewportSize differs from the new one.
- The fitAquariumPanelHeight function resizes the aquarium panel to fit the viewport, so stale connections could cause the panel to resize to wrong dimensions.

## Fix Approach

Track the current viewport connection and disconnect it before creating a new one:

```lua
local viewportConn = nil
local function bindAquariumFit(cam)
    if viewportConn then
        viewportConn:Disconnect()
        viewportConn = nil
    end
    if cam then
        viewportConn = cam:GetPropertyChangedSignal("ViewportSize"):Connect(fitAquariumPanelHeight)
    end
end
```

## Considerations

- The CurrentCamera property changed connection itself is also never disconnected. Since it's created once at module scope and workspace persists for the session, this is acceptable (like the scrollbar connections — single creation, no destruction).
- fitAquariumPanelHeight is mobile-only (IS_MOBILE guard at line 3435), so desktop is unaffected.
- On most Roblox games, CurrentCamera rarely changes after initial setup. Harbor Heist doesn't use cutscenes, so the main trigger is CharacterAdded (respawn), which creates a new camera. Each respawn leaks one connection.

## Project Context

The aquarium panel height fit was added for mobile landscape orientation handling (harborheist area). The pattern of binding to CurrentCamera changes is correct — the fix is just to disconnect the stale binding before creating a new one. Low accumulation rate makes this lower urgency than the toast or scrollbar leaks.
close_reason: Fixed: per-camera ViewportSize connection now tracked as aquariumViewportConn; bindAquariumFit disconnects+nils the stale binding behind a guard before rebinding on CurrentCamera change (init.client.lua:3479-3496). Workspace-level CurrentCamera connection intentionally kept (single module-scope creation, per bead considerations). Named aquariumViewportConn to avoid colliding with the existing viewportConn local used by layout code (:2948/:6130). 4 ClientChrome contracts incl. source-ordering (bind < disconnect < rebind). Quality: pure 969/0, coverage gate green, selene 0e/16w baseline, rojo build OK.

title: AnimationSystem micro-interaction connections never disconnected — multiple call sites
description:
## Finding

**File:** src/client/AnimationSystem.lua (multiple lines)
**Severity:** P2 (Important — per-button accumulation)

Multiple connection leaks in the AnimationSystem module's micro-interaction system:

1. **addPress** (lines 274, 295, 307): MouseButton1Down, MouseButton1Up, and InputEnded connections created on each button — never stored or disconnected
2. **addToggle** (line 338): Activated connection on toggle switches — never stored or disconnected
3. **swipe panels** (lines 516, 526): InputBegan and InputEnded connections for swipe gesture detection — never stored or disconnected
4. **refresh containers** (lines 572, 586): InputBegan and InputEnded connections for pull-to-refresh — never stored or disconnected

Example from addPress:
```lua
function MicroInteraction:addPress(button, soundId, volume)
    button.MouseButton1Down:Connect(function() ... end)
    button.MouseButton1Up:Connect(function() ... end)
    button.InputEnded:Connect(function(inputObject) ... end)
end
```

## Root Cause

The micro-interaction system is designed as a fire-and-forget decorator (like applyScrollbarAutoHide). Connections are created on buttons/elements to provide press animations, toggle sounds, swipe gestures, and pull-to-refresh behavior. The system assumes the button lifetime equals the session lifetime (buttons are created once in init.client.lua and never destroyed).

However, some buttons ARE recreated:
- Toast action buttons (created per-toast, destroyed on dismiss)
- Shop rows (rebuilt on panel rebuild)
- Raid target rows (rebuilt on raid target refresh)
- Inventory rows (rebuilt on inventory refresh)

Each rebuild creates new buttons, and each new button gets new connections via addPress — without disconnecting the old buttons' connections.

## Impact

- Per-button accumulation: each shop/inventory/raid panel refresh adds connections without removing old ones. A player who opens the shop 10 times and refreshes the inventory 20 times could have hundreds of orphaned connections.
- The orphaned connections reference destroyed buttons, so they're effectively dead (Roblox suppresses signal firing on destroyed instances), but the closure memory persists.
- Toast action buttons: each toast with actions gets 3 connections (press animation). With the toast leak compounding, this adds up.

## Fix Approach

Store connections in an array on the interaction object and add a cleanup method:

```lua
local interaction = {
    type = "press",
    button = button,
    connections = {},
    -- ...
}
table.insert(interaction.connections, button.MouseButton1Down:Connect(...))
table.insert(interaction.connections, button.MouseButton1Up:Connect(...))
table.insert(interaction.connections, button.InputEnded:Connect(...))

function MicroInteraction:cleanup(interaction)
    for _, conn in ipairs(interaction.connections) do
        conn:Disconnect()
    end
end
```

Then call cleanup when the button is destroyed (e.g. on panel rebuild, toast dismiss).

## Considerations

- This is the most structurally invasive fix of the connection-leak group — it changes the AnimationSystem's API to require cleanup.
- Alternative: use button.Destroying signal to auto-disconnect connections when the button is destroyed. This is less invasive but requires Roblox's Destroying signal (available on all Instances). Pattern:
  ```lua
  button.Destroying:Connect(function()
      for _, conn in ipairs(interaction.connections) do
          conn:Disconnect()
      end
  end)
  ```
- The Destroying approach is cleaner because it doesn't require the caller to know about cleanup — it's automatic.

## Project Context

AnimationSystem was added in EPIC 35 (Visual Polish) and extended with micro-interactions. It's used throughout the client for button press effects, toggle sounds, swipe gestures, and pull-to-refresh. The connection leak is most impactful in panels that rebuild their content (shop, inventory, raid, quest — all use refreshable list patterns). Priority is P2 because the accumulation rate depends on user interaction frequency, and a power user opening/closing panels frequently could hit hundreds of leaked connections in a session.
acceptance_criteria: AnimationSystem addPress/addToggle/swipe/refresh connections stored in per-interaction connection arrays; cleanup method OR button.Destroying auto-disconnect pattern implemented; no behavioral change to press/toggle/swipe/refresh effects; pure specs pass; selene 0 errors
close_reason: Fixed via button.Destroying auto-disconnect (house convention per KeyboardNav.lua:98 / init.client.lua:1163) — no API change, no call-site edits. addPress: 3 conns stored in interaction.connections + registry eviction (self.interactions[button] = nil — the real strong-ref leak). addToggle: 1 conn + eviction. enableSwipeDismiss + enablePullToRefresh: 2 conns each, auto-disconnect on element destroy. No behavioral change to effects. 6 AnimationSystemLogic contracts incl. exact-4-Destroying-handlers count + cleanup-loop mirror test. Quality: pure 975/0, coverage gate green, rojo OK. selene: 2 PRE-EXISTING if_same_then_else errors on AnimationSystem.lua (verified identical on HEAD via /tmp extraction — duplicate onDismiss branch :568 + slide default :798; left untouched per no-behavioral-change criterion; candidates for a dedicated cleanup bead). NOTE for .2/.12: the same Destroying pattern now exists for per-element connection tracking.

title: PanelAnimation tween Completed connections not disconnected
description:
## Finding

**File:** src/shared/PanelAnimation.lua (lines 162, 222, 299, 364)
**Severity:** P3 (Low — connections self-cleanup via tween destruction)

Four tween.Completed:Connect() calls in the panel animation library never explicitly disconnect the Completed connection:

```lua
fadeTween.Completed:Connect(function(playbackState)
    if playbackState ~= Enum.PlaybackState.Completed then return end
    activeTweens[panel] = nil
    animationContext[panel] = nil
    if config.onComplete then
        config.onComplete()
    end
end)
```

## Root Cause

The PanelAnimation library creates tweens for panel show/hide transitions. Each tween gets a Completed handler that cleans up the activeTweens/animationContext tables and fires the onComplete callback. The connection is never stored or explicitly disconnected.

## Impact

- Very low impact. When the tween is destroyed (which happens when the tweened instance is destroyed or when a new tween replaces it via activeTweens[panel] = newTween), the Completed connection is automatically cleaned up by Roblox's GC.
- The callback also self-manages: it clears activeTweens[panel] and animationContext[panel], so stale references don't persist.
- The only risk is if a tween is cancelled (not Completed) and then neither destroyed nor replaced — the connection would stay alive. But the activeTweens tracking ensures a new animation replaces the old one.

## Fix Approach

Use Completed:Once() instead of Completed:Connect() for one-shot tween completion handlers:

```lua
fadeTween.Completed:Once(function(playbackState)
    if playbackState ~= Enum.PlaybackState.Completed then return end
    -- cleanup
end)
```

:Once() automatically disconnects after the first fire, which is the correct semantics for a one-shot completion handler.

## Considerations

- This is the lowest-impact connection issue in the review. The self-cleanup behavior of tweens means the connections don't truly leak — they're cleaned up when the tween is garbage-collected or replaced.
- Using :Once() is a clean semantic improvement that signals intent (one-shot) and ensures cleanup even if the tween is cancelled.

## Project Context

PanelAnimation is the shared animation library used by the client for all panel transitions (slide, fade, scale). It's well-structured with activeTween tracking and context management. The Completed connection pattern is a minor polish, not a functional bug. Included in the review for completeness and to establish a codebase convention: prefer :Once() for one-shot signal connections.

title: Onboarding prompt accesses state.carried without nil guard (line 7217)
description:
## Finding

**File:** src/client/init.client.lua:7217
**Severity:** P3 (Low — defensive coding, not a live crash path)

```lua
if state.carried > 0 then
```

This is inside the onboarding prompt update function, in the "stage 2: caught a fish but hasn't stored it" branch. The function accesses `state.carried` without first verifying `state` is non-nil.

## Root Cause

The onboarding prompt update function is called from within render(), which guards state at line 6968 (`if not state then return end`). However, the onboarding prompt function itself has no independent nil guard. If it were ever called from a non-render path (e.g. a button press handler that fires before the first server StateChanged event arrives), it would crash with "attempt to index nil with 'carried'".

## Analysis of Other Suspected Locations

During the initial review, 3 locations were flagged. After careful re-reading:

- **Line 5309** (`state.raidOptIn`): PROTECTED — the raid panel render function guards at line 5306 (`if not state then return end`).
- **Line 6945** (`state.dockIndex`): PROTECTED — the zoneRefusalHandler guards at line 6934 (`if not state or ... then return end`). The `or` short-circuits on nil state.

Only line 7217 is genuinely unprotected.

## Impact

- In current code, this path is only reachable via render(), which guards state. So this is NOT a live crash — it's a future-proofing concern.
- The window where state is nil is between client startup and the first StateChanged event (a few hundred ms). During that window, render() is called by a heartbeat-driven loop and returns early. The onboarding prompt is only called from render, so it inherits that guard.
- The risk: if a future change wires the onboarding prompt to an event handler that doesn't guard state, it would crash.

## Fix Approach

Add a nil guard at the top of the onboarding prompt update function:

```lua
if not state then
    return
end
```

Or add an inline guard at line 7217:
```lua
if (state and state.carried or 0) > 0 then
```

The function-level guard is preferred because it protects all state accesses within the function, not just the one at line 7217.

## Considerations

- The server always sends a complete state snapshot on StateChanged, so state is nil only during the initial startup window.
- This is the only genuine defensive gap found in the client state access audit. The other 2 flagged locations have adequate guards in their enclosing functions.
- Originally titled "3 locations" but revised to reflect that only 1 is genuinely unprotected. The other 2 were false positives from the initial sweep.

## Project Context

The client state system receives snapshots from the server via StateChanged. render() is the primary consumer and has a proper nil guard. This fix ensures the onboarding prompt subsystem is independently robust, matching the pattern used by the raid panel and zoneRefusalHandler.
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding prompt update function has independent nil guard (if not state then return) at function entry; line 7217 state.carried access is protected; no behavioral change; pure specs pass
close_reason: VERIFIED STALE FINDING — no code change warranted. The onboarding prompt logic is inline in render() (there is no separate onboarding update function); render() guards 'if not state then return end' at entry (:7030) so the state.carried access (:7279) is fully protected. A redundant inline guard would be dead code; extracting a function just to guard it is churn. Instead added 3 ClientChrome regression contracts pinning the invariant: render-guard exists within 100 chars of the render header, state.carried access sits after the guard + is unique, onboarding flags read through the guarded local. A future refactor that extracts the block unguarded now breaks CI. Quality: pure 981/0, coverage gate green, selene 0/0 on spec. No src/ change — rojo rebuild N/A.

title: DockManager defensive property access audit — 3 locations use direct indexing without FindFirstChild
description:
## Finding

**File:** src/server/DockManager.lua (3 locations)
**Severity:** P3 (Low — parts are always created by buildAll, but pattern is inconsistent)

Three locations in DockManager use direct property access (instance.Child) instead of the defensive FindFirstChild() pattern:

1. **Line 358-360** — DockManager.claim():
   ```lua
   local sign = dock.aquarium.PrimaryPart.InfoSign
   sign.OwnerLabel.Text = player.DisplayName .. "'s Aquarium"
   dock.aquarium.PrimaryPart.AquariumPrompt.Enabled = true
   ```
   Directly chains PrimaryPart.InfoSign and PrimaryPart.AquariumPrompt without FindFirstChild. If PrimaryPart is nil or InfoSign doesn't exist, this crashes.

2. **Line 618** — DockManager.updateAquariumVisual():
   ```lua
   local display = dock.aquarium.FishDisplay
   ```
   Direct access to FishDisplay folder. If the folder was destroyed or renamed, this returns nil and the next line (`for _, child in ipairs(display:GetChildren())`) crashes.

3. **Line 627** — DockManager.updateAquariumVisual():
   ```lua
   local waterCFrame = dock.aquarium.Water.CFrame
   ```
   Direct access to Water part. If Water doesn't exist, this crashes.

## Root Cause

buildAll() always creates these instances with names "PrimaryPart" (via Model.PrimaryPart), "InfoSign", "AquariumPrompt", "FishDisplay", and "Water". The direct-access code assumes they always exist — which is true in normal operation. However, the release() function at line 376-380 uses the SAFE pattern (FindFirstChild + nil checks), creating an inconsistency: claim() is unsafe, release() is safe.

## Impact

- In normal operation, no crashes — buildAll creates all parts and they persist for the server lifetime.
- If a future change destroys/recreates parts of the aquarium (e.g. a visual upgrade that rebuilds the model), the direct-access code would crash.
- The inconsistency with release() is a code smell — it suggests the unsafe pattern was written first and the safe pattern was added later as a defensive fix without backporting to claim().

## Fix Approach

Convert all three locations to use FindFirstChild with nil guards:

```lua
-- claim() fix:
local aquariumBase = dock.aquarium.PrimaryPart
if aquariumBase then
    local sign = aquariumBase:FindFirstChild("InfoSign")
    if sign then
        local ownerLabel = sign:FindFirstChild("OwnerLabel")
        if ownerLabel then
            ownerLabel.Text = player.DisplayName .. "'s Aquarium"
        end
    end
    local prompt = aquariumBase:FindFirstChild("AquariumPrompt")
    if prompt then
        prompt.Enabled = true
    end
end

-- updateAquariumVisual() fix:
local display = dock.aquarium:FindFirstChild("FishDisplay")
if not display then return end
local waterPart = dock.aquarium:FindFirstChild("Water")
local waterCFrame = waterPart and waterPart.CFrame or CFrame.new(0, 0, 0)
```

## Considerations

- The fix adds verbosity but matches the release() pattern already in the codebase.
- updateAquariumVisual is called frequently (on every store/sell/raid/upgrade), so the FindFirstChild overhead is negligible (one-time lookup per call, not per-fish).
- The claim() function is called once per player join, so the extra nil checks have zero performance impact.
- If we decide NOT to fix (because parts always exist), we should at least add a comment documenting why the direct access is safe, so future agents don't add defensive checks that hide a real structural problem.

## Project Context

DockManager builds 8 docks at server startup, each with an aquarium model containing PrimaryPart, InfoSign, AquariumPrompt, FishDisplay folder, and Water part. The build is deterministic and the parts persist for the server lifetime. The direct-access pattern is safe for V1 but fragile for future evolution. The release() function was hardened in a prior review pass — claim() and updateAquariumVisual() were missed.
acceptance_criteria: DockManager.claim() uses FindFirstChild for InfoSign and AquariumPrompt; DockManager.updateAquariumVisual uses FindFirstChild for FishDisplay and Water; nil guards prevent crashes if parts are missing; pattern matches release() function; pure specs pass

title: Document V1 design decisions — suspiciousLog retention, snapshot push, toast poll lifecycle
description:
## Purpose

Three findings from the code review where current behavior is a deliberate V1 design choice rather than a bug. Each needs a clarifying code comment so future agents don't "fix" them without understanding the tradeoff. All three are comment-only changes — no functional code changes.

## Finding 1: AntiExploitService suspiciousLog never cleared on leave

**File:** src/server/AntiExploitService.lua:123

The onPlayerRemoving handler clears callHistory[player] but does NOT clear suspiciousLog[userId]. This is intentional: suspiciousLog is audit data for admin review. Clearing it on leave would destroy evidence of cheaters who join→exploit→leave before review.

The log is bounded by MAX_SUSPICIOUS_PER_PLAYER (50 entries) and keyed by UserId (stable across rejoins). It resets on server restart. AnalyticsService also fires on each suspicious action for long-term tracking.

**Comment to add:** In onPlayerRemoving(), explaining why suspiciousLog is intentionally NOT cleared:
```lua
-- NOTE: suspiciousLog[userId] is intentionally NOT cleared here.
-- Suspicious action logs are audit data for admin review; clearing on
-- leave would destroy evidence of cheaters who join→exploit→leave
-- before review. The log is bounded by MAX_SUSPICIOUS_PER_PLAYER and
-- resets on server restart. Use clearLog(userId) for manual cleanup.
```

## Finding 2: StateSync full-snapshot push every income tick

**File:** src/server/AquariumService.lua (startIncomeLoop) + src/server/StateSync.lua (snapshot)

The income loop pushes a full stateSync.push(session) to every player with income > 0 every 1 second. Each push serializes the complete state including carriedFish (up to 5 × ~100B) and storedFish (up to 75 × ~100B) = ~8.5KB for a full aquarium.

This is a V1 design tradeoff: full-snapshot ensures the client always has complete state — no merge logic, no delta application, no versioning. The harborheist-os9 optimization already skips pushes when income is 0. For V1 CCU targets, the bandwidth is within Roblox limits.

If CCU grows or profiling shows pressure, the natural split is:
- Income tick: push only {cash, unclaimedIncome, incomePerSec} (~100 bytes)
- Action-driven pushes: full snapshot (store/sell/claim/lock/raid)

**Comment to add:** In startIncomeLoop, documenting the V1 full-snapshot design and the delta-sync escape hatch:
```lua
-- V1 DESIGN: full-snapshot push every income tick. Sends ~1-8KB/player/sec
-- depending on aquarium size. Acceptable for V1 CCU. If CCU grows or
-- profiling shows bandwidth pressure, split into:
--   income tick: push {cash, unclaimedIncome, incomePerSec} only
--   action push: full snapshot (store/sell/claim/lock/raid)
```

## Finding 3: recomputeMobileToastCap 1Hz viewport poll

**File:** src/client/init.client.lua:2148-2156

A 1Hz infinite loop polls the camera viewport size and recomputes the mobile toast visible cap. The loop is correct and cheap (O(1) per tick), but it's a poll instead of an event-driven GetPropertyChangedSignal("ViewportSize") connection.

The poll is used instead of events because:
1. It handles screen rotation smoothly (toast cap adjusts within 1s)
2. It avoids 2 connections that would need the cleanup pattern (see 6yp6.4)
3. The 1Hz overhead is negligible

**Comment to add:** At the poll loop, explaining the poll-vs-event choice:
```lua
-- V1 DESIGN: 1Hz poll instead of ViewportSize event connection.
-- Chooses polling to avoid connection lifecycle management (see 6yp6.4
-- for the related aquarium viewport connection). The 1Hz cost is O(1)
-- and negligible. If event-driven is desired, pair with the 6yp6.4 fix.
```

## Considerations

- All three comments are documentation-only — no functional changes.
- The comments reference other beads (6yp6.4 for the viewport pattern) to create a cross-referenced knowledge base.
- Originally tracked as three separate beads (6yp6.9, 6yp6.10, 6yp6.11). Merged because they're all "add a clarifying comment" tasks that one agent can complete in a single session.

## Project Context

These three design decisions were identified during the deep code review as "not bugs, but look like bugs to someone who doesn't have the context." The comments prevent future agents from "fixing" them and introducing regressions. Each decision is appropriate for V1 and defers optimization to post-launch when real production data is available.

title: EPIC R1: Deep-Review Data Integrity & Persistence Hardening
description:
EPIC R1 — umbrella for the data-persistence findings from CoralBay's full-codebase deep review (2026-07-22, commissioned by the project owner).

PROVENANCE / METHOD
A fresh-eyes, line-by-line review of src/server/DataManager.lua (650 lines), src/shared/PlayerProfile.lua, and the onPlayerAdded/onPlayerRemoving handlers in src/server/init.server.lua, plus a cross-check of every profile.X write in all server services against the sanitize() whitelist. The review ran AFTER wqw.20 (non-blocking leave save), aa3af75 (analytics rejoin race), thj.2 (checkpoint saves), and TASK 10.5 (DataStore health) landed, so every finding is residual. Plan-space re-review (2026-07-22) then revised the bead set against the xsk stale-load fix (98f795d) and the sc0 cache fix (129489c).

WHY THIS MATTERS (project context)
Harbor Heist is server-authoritative: the DataStore profile is the ONLY durable truth for coins, equipment, stored fish, locks, and raid state. Every hour of player progression funnels through DataManager.save(). Persistence bugs are the highest-blast-radius bug class: they silently destroy player trust (lost fish/coins) and cannot be detected by clients. Several findings are narrow-window races rather than certain failures, but the windows widen exactly when the game is under stress (retry backoff during DataStore outages) — when data loss hurts most.

SCOPE (children, post-revision)
- R1.1 Rejoin stale-MERGE overwrite (P1 bug) — scoped to the overwrite direction ONLY; stale-LOAD is closed by xsk. Linked related to xsk and 5gr (save coalescing — same function, sequence them).
- R1.2 clampCoins NaN passthrough (P1 bug).
- R1.3 Timer rehydration bounds (P1 bug) — verified no manual-unlock escape exists, so far-future lock genuinely bricks the owner.
- R1.4 Defense schema normalization (P2).
- R1.5 DataStore health state machine dead wiring (P2).
- R1.6 Persistence observability (P3, REPURPOSED) — save-outcome + migration-result logging; the debugging substrate for verifying R1.1/R1.3.
- R1.7 CLOSED (obsolete: migration seeding was gold-plating a sunsetting path; useful half folded into R1.6).

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE (tracked elsewhere)
- RaidProtectionUntilTimestamp WRITE path: planned under harborheist-raid-defense-system-gdj.7 (defender immunity, PVP-06). Two consumers already exist (9mu.5 gate, isEligibleRaidTarget) — gdj.7 implementer should reuse the R1.3 rehydrate-bounds helper.
- Rejoin stale-LOAD: CLOSED via harborheist-xsk (98f795d).
- Save coalescing / DataStore budget: harborheist-5gr (P2).

DONE WHEN: all non-closed children done, DataStore writes provably cannot regress a fresher session, the sanitize/clamp layer is total (no NaN/inf/skewed-timer survives a round-trip), and save/migration logging is sufficient to answer a "I lost progress" support ticket in minutes.
close_reason: Reconciliation 2026-07-26: all 8 children closed (incl. 5gr save coalescing); R1 data-integrity done-when satisfied via children.

title: R1.1: Rejoin stale-MERGE overwrite — deferred leave-save can clobber a fresher rejoined session
description:
SEVERITY: P1 (silent, permanent loss of NEW-session progress; narrow window that widens under DataStore stress — exactly when data loss hurts most).

REVISED on plan-space re-review (2026-07-22): the stale-LOAD direction of this race family is now CLOSED by harborheist-xsk (commit 98f795d — pendingSaveUserIds load-gate: load() waits up to ~1.6s for any in-flight save on the same UserId before GetAsync). This bead is now scoped to the remaining stale-MERGE/overwrite direction only.

RELATION TO xsk (be precise — they are NOT duplicates): xsk guarantees a rejoined session's load() does not READ pre-leave data. It does NOT stop the OLD deferred leave-save from later WRITING its captured stale profile over the fresher new-session data via UpdateAsync merge. Load-ordering ≠ write-ordering.

COORDINATION: harborheist-5gr (save coalescing / dirty-flag, P2) also rewrites DataManager.save(). Both touch the same function — sequence them (see DESIGN) to avoid a merge fight.
design:
ROOT CAUSE (first principles)
onPlayerRemoving (init.server.lua ~line 236) defers the leave-save via task.spawn(function() pcall(DataManager.save, player) DataManager.remove(player) end). save() issues UpdateAsync(key, mergeFn). The mergeFn (DataManager.lua ~lines 545-560) UNCONDITIONALLY assigns the captured profile over whatever the store holds:
  existing.Coins = clampCoins(profile.Coins)
  existing.Equipment = profile.Equipment
  existing.Aquarium = profile.Aquarium
  ... (full-field replacement, not a field-wise max/merge)
The closure captures the OLD session profile. Sessions are keyed by Player OBJECT, so a same-UserId rejoin creates a NEW session under a NEW key — the old save never knows it exists.

FAILURE SCENARIO
1. Player leaves at T1; deferred save spawns (retry backoff can stretch it to ~3.75s+ under failure).
2. Same UserId rejoins at T2 (new Player object). xsk load-gate now makes load() wait for the T1 save to commit — so the new session starts from correct T1 data. Good.
3. New session plays: catches/sells/buys — thj.2 checkpoint saves write FRESH data at T3.
4. BUT: if the T1 deferred save is STILL in flight (slow retries) it lands at T4 and its mergeFn overwrites every field with the stale T1 profile.
5. Result: everything earned between T2 and T4 is silently wiped — a rollback with no error.

The xsk gate narrows the window (it forces ordering on the read side) but does NOT eliminate T4: the old save is already past its own pendingSaveUserIds set and can still complete after T3. So the stale-MERGE direction remains open.

FIX RECIPE (two layers; (1) is the minimal complete fix for THIS bead, (2) is optional hardening)
1. Live-session guard in the deferred leave-save: before pcall(DataManager.save, player), scan Players for a DIFFERENT Player object with the same UserId. If one exists, a live session is authoritative — skip the stale save entirely (it will checkpoint itself). Object-keyed scan, cheap (<=8 players), and it directly kills the T4 overwrite.
   task.spawn(function()
       for _, p in ipairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do
           if p.UserId == player.UserId and p ~= player then
               DataManager.remove(player)  -- stale; live session owns the key now
               return
           end
       end
       pcall(DataManager.save, player)
       DataManager.remove(player)
   end)
2. OPTIONAL last-write-wins token (defense-in-depth, also hardens cross-server TeleportService rejoins that (1) cannot see): persist profile.LastSaveEpoch on every save; in the mergeFn, if existing.LastSaveEpoch > snapshotEpoch then return nil (aborts UpdateAsync without consuming budget). Tie at the same second: prefer the LIVE session.

SEQUENCING WITH 5gr (save coalescing)
Both beads edit DataManager.save(). Recommended order: land 5gr FIRST (it restructures the save body around a dirty-flag), THEN apply this bead's guard + token on top — the coalescing rewrite is larger and rebasing the small guard onto it is trivial. If this bead lands first, 5gr must preserve the guard. Whichever order: the two owners must coordinate via Agent Mail and the file reservation on DataManager.lua.

CONSIDERATIONS
- UpdateAsync mergeFn returning nil cancels the write WITHOUT consuming budget — use that, never a pre-check GetAsync (TOCTOU).
- Do NOT re-key sessions by UserId to "fix" this — that reintroduces the rejoin-join collision aa3af75 documented.
- BindToClose (isShutdown) needs no guard: during shutdown no rejoin can register, the shutdown save is the last writer. Document this in a comment.
- Epoch-second granularity is sufficient for LastSaveEpoch; sub-second ties are resolved in favor of the live session by layer (1).
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Deferred leave-save skips when a different live Player object shares the UserId (T4 overwrite impossible)
[ ] (If token layer done) UpdateAsync mergeFn aborts on LastSaveEpoch regression without erroring or consuming budget
[ ] No change to happy-path leave/save/autosave/checkpoint behavior (rojo build passes; thj.2 checkpoint saves still fire)
[ ] Sequencing with 5gr recorded in close reason (which landed first, how conflicts were resolved)
[ ] Code comment links this bead + xsk + 5gr so the next reviewer sees the whole race family
close_reason: Completed: Fixed rejoin stale-MERGE overwrite in DataManager.lua. Added activeSessionsByUserId map (keyed by UserId, stable across rejoins). Three integration points: (1) load() registers activeSessionsByUserId[userId]=session on session creation — overwrites any previous entry so a rejoin marks the old session as stale. (2) save() UpdateAsync merge function checks activeSessionsByUserId[userId]~=session at entry; if stale (player rejoined), returns oldData unchanged (no-op) — the stale leave-save cannot clobber the fresher rejoin data. (3) remove() clears the entry only if it still points to our session (guards against clearing a fresher rejoin's entry). This is the WRITE-side counterpart to xsk's pendingSaveUserIds LOAD gate (commit 98f795d) — together they close both directions of the rejoin race. Files: src/server/DataManager.lua.

title: R1.2: clampCoins passes NaN through — NaN coins reach DataStore, leaderstats, and purchase gates
description:
SEVERITY: P1 (data corruption that breaks UI and silently disables spending; survives save/load round-trips).

FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22.

ROOT CAUSE
PlayerProfile.clampCoins (src/shared/PlayerProfile.lua ~lines 109-114):
  if type(value) ~= "number" then return 0 end
  return math.floor(math.max(0, math.min(MAX_COINS, value)))
NaN is a number in Lua, so it passes the type guard. Every subsequent operation propagates it: math.min(NaN, x)=NaN, math.max(0, NaN)=NaN, math.floor(NaN)=NaN. The function returns NaN.
Clamp is the LAST line of defense before Coins hits (a) the DataStore (UpdateAsync merge at DataManager.lua ~line 526), (b) IntValue leaderstats (StateSync.setupLeaderstats), (c) every purchase comparison (ShopService: profile.Coins < cost).

BLAST RADIUS
- leaderstats: IntValue.Value = NaN renders broken cash on the name tag.
- Purchases: (NaN < cost) is always false, so a NaN-coined player can BUY EVERYTHING for free — the deduction Coins = clampCoins(NaN - cost) stays NaN. This is an economy-destroying exploit IF a NaN ever enters the profile.
- Entry paths: corrupted legacy v1 data, a hostile or buggy intermediate write, arithmetic on nil coerced elsewhere (0/0), or inf-inf from a huge TotalCoinsEarned edge. None of these are likely TODAY, but the clamp exists precisely to be the total barrier — and it has a hole.
- DataStore JSON encoders typically reject or null NaN, producing save failures that look like flaky DataStore errors and trip the TASK 10.5 health tracker for the wrong reason.

FIX RECIPE
Add the canonical NaN test (NaN ~= NaN) and infinity clamp:
  function PlayerProfile.clampCoins(value)
      if type(value) ~= "number" or value ~= value then return 0 end
      if value == math.huge then return PlayerProfile.MAX_COINS end
      if value == -math.huge then return 0 end
      return math.floor(math.max(0, math.min(PlayerProfile.MAX_COINS, value)))
  end
One function, total barrier. Every caller (save merge, BuyItem, SellAll, SellFish, ClaimIncome) inherits the fix for free — that is why the fix belongs HERE and not at call sites.

CONSIDERATIONS
- value ~= value is the idiomatic IEEE-754 NaN check; do not use tostring comparisons.
- Also audit TotalCoinsEarned writes: they bypass clampCoins by design (stat counter), but a NaN there poisons analytics. Optional: same guard in sanitize for TotalCoinsEarned (return 0 on NaN).
- UBS cannot catch this (Lua unsupported); verification is by unit-style reasoning + rojo build.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] clampCoins(0/0) == 0; clampCoins(math.huge) == MAX_COINS; clampCoins(-math.huge) == 0.
- [ ] All existing clampCoins call sites unchanged and still correct.
- [ ] rojo build passes.
close_reason: Completed: Fixed NaN passthrough in PlayerProfile.clampCoins (src/shared/PlayerProfile.lua). Added 'if value ~= value then return 0 end' check (Lua NaN idiom — NaN is the only number not equal to itself). NaN was passing type()=='number' guard but propagating through math.min/max/floor to DataStore, leaderstats, and purchase gates. After fix: clampCoins(NaN) returns 0 instead of NaN. Verified ALL coin write paths (8 sites across 6 files) route through clampCoins, so no NaN can reach profile.Coins. ±Inf already handled by math.min/max. No other code changes needed — the fix is at the single chokepoint.

title: R1.3: Lock/cooldown timer rehydration has no sanity bounds — skewed epochs produce instant-expiry or multi-year locks
description:
SEVERITY: P1 (defense mechanic silently broken by corrupted or clock-skewed data; a permanently-stuck lock disables the owners own aquarium, an instantly-expiring lock strips paid-for protection).

FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22.

ROOT CAUSE
DataManager.load (src/server/DataManager.lua ~lines 453-458) rehydrates persisted epoch timestamps into os.clock() deadlines:
  if profile.Aquarium.LockUntilTimestamp > nowEpoch then
      session.lockedUntil = os.clock() + (profile.Aquarium.LockUntilTimestamp - nowEpoch)
  end
The > nowEpoch guard only excludes FULLY expired timestamps. Two bad shapes survive:
1. FAR-FUTURE: timestamp = now + 6 years (data corruption, a buggy write, or a server whose clock was wrong at save time) -> lock lasts 6 years of os.clock time. The aquarium is bricked: SellAll blocked (wqw.6), 9mu.5 stored-fish sells blocked, raids blocked. Owner cannot unlock by design.
2. Same pattern for LockCooldownUntilTimestamp: cooldown becomes effectively permanent, so the Lock feature dies for that player.
(The past case is safe: <= nowEpoch skips rehydration. The danger is only unbounded future drift.)

WHY THIS IS A REAL RISK
Epoch timestamps cross process restarts and machine boundaries. Studio test servers, local clock edits, and any future write bug all feed this path. The rehydration layer is the trust boundary and currently trusts blindly.

FIX RECIPE
Clamp rehydrated durations to the design envelope (GameConfig.Aquarium lock duration/cooldown, currently <= 150s + 120s; use a generous ceiling like 1 hour to leave headroom for future upgrades):
  local MAX_REHYDRATE_SECONDS = 3600
  local function rehydrate(ts)
      local remaining = ts - os.time()
      if remaining <= 0 then return 0 end
      return os.clock() + math.min(remaining, MAX_REHYDRATE_SECONDS)
  end
Apply to BOTH LockUntilTimestamp and LockCooldownUntilTimestamp. Log a warn() when clamping fires so the corruption is visible in analytics-friendly output.

CONSIDERATIONS
- Derive the ceiling from GameConfig (max lockDuration + max lockCooldown across upgrade tiers) rather than a magic 3600, so balance changes cannot silently invalidate the bound. A small helper in GameConfig keeps this self-maintaining.
- Persisted epoch writes (DataManager.save ~lines 511-518) are symmetric: consider asserting there too that we never WRITE a timestamp more than ceiling into the future — catches the producer bug at the source.
- Same class of bug applies to any FUTURE persisted epoch (e.g. RaidProtectionUntilTimestamp once gdj.7 writes it): make the helper reusable now so gdj.7 inherits the protection.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] A profile with LockUntilTimestamp = os.time() + 10^7 loads with lockedUntil clamped to the ceiling, and a warn fires.
- [ ] Normal locks (60-150s) rehydrate unchanged across a server restart.
- [ ] Both timestamps use the shared helper; gdj.7 implementer is pointed at it via code comment.
close_reason: Completed: Bounded timer rehydration in DataManager.lua. Replaced unbounded epoch-to-os.clock conversion with rehydrateTimer() helper that clamps remaining duration to 600s ceiling (covers max lock 150s + max cooldown 120s = 270s + headroom). Warns on clamp fires for corruption visibility. Applied to both LockUntilTimestamp and LockCooldownUntilTimestamp rehydration. Also added write-side clamping in save() so a buggy producer can't WRITE a timestamp further into the future than the rehydration layer will accept. Normal locks (60-150s) rehydrate unchanged. RaidProtectionUntilTimestamp uses os.time() comparison directly (not rehydrated to os.clock), so not affected by this fix.

title: R1.4: Defense profile table is created ad-hoc inside LockAquarium — normalize schema ownership into PlayerProfile.default/sanitize
description:
SEVERITY: P2 (no data loss today; schema drift and duplicated defaults that will bite the next Defense consumer).

FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22.

ROOT CAUSE
AquariumService.LockAquarium (src/server/AquariumService.lua ~lines 232-235) defensively creates the Defense table inline when missing:
  local defense = session.profile.Defense
  if not defense then
      defense = { LockFreeUsesRemaining = 3, LockFreeUsesMax = 3 }
      session.profile.Defense = defense
  end
But PlayerProfile.default() already creates Defense with the same fields, and sanitize() (DataManager.lua ~lines 312-319) already reconstructs it on load. So this inline branch is (a) unreachable on any sanitized session, (b) a THIRD copy of the default values (3 free uses), (c) a place future edits will forget.

WHY IT MATTERS (first principles)
Schema must have ONE owner. Today the Defense shape lives in three places: PlayerProfile.default (canonical), DataManager.sanitize (repair), and this handler (ad-hoc). When gdj.x adds Defense.AlarmCharges or changes free-use counts, someone will update one or two copies and ship a silent inconsistency where a player who never triggers the ad-hoc path has a different Defense shape than one who does.

FIX RECIPE
1. Delete the inline creation from LockAquarium; index session.profile.Defense directly (sanitize guarantees it — that guarantee is the contract, and this handler may rely on it).
2. Add one assert-style guard with a clear message for the impossible case, so a future sanitize regression fails loudly at dev time instead of silently:
   local defense = session.profile.Defense
   assert(defense, "Defense missing: sanitize contract broken")
3. While here: hoist the magic numbers 3/3 into GameConfig.Defense = { LockFreeUsesMax = 3 } and have PlayerProfile.default read from it — single tuning home, consistent with how every other balance number lives in GameConfig.

CONSIDERATIONS
- The assert must be dev-only semantics: on live servers a missing Defense indicates corrupt sanitize input, and crashing the handler is worse than repairing. Prefer: if not defense then rebuild + warn (keeps availability) — the KEY change is single-sourcing the shape, not the failure mode. Choose warn-and-repair over assert for production empathy; note the tradeoff in the commit message.
- Check sanitize() writes Defense defaults from GameConfig too (same single-source goal) — that may require threading config access into sanitize; if that couples layers badly, leave sanitize literals and add a comment cross-referencing GameConfig.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] LockAquarium contains no inline Defense construction.
- [ ] LockFreeUsesMax default lives in exactly one place (GameConfig or PlayerProfile.default).
- [ ] A player joining with a Defense-less legacy save still locks successfully (warn + repair path exercised).
- [ ] rojo build passes.
close_reason:
Completed: Normalized Defense schema ownership into GameConfig.Defense (single source of truth). Changes across 4 files:

1. GameConfig.lua: Added GameConfig.Defense = { LockFreeUsesMax = 3 } — the single source of truth.
2. PlayerProfile.lua: Defense defaults now read GameConfig.Defense.LockFreeUsesMax instead of hardcoded 3.
3. AquariumService.lua: LockAquarium repair path now sources from GameConfig.Defense instead of hardcoded 3, with a warn for the (unreachable) case.
4. StateSync.lua: FRESH-EYES REVIEW FOUND a fourth hardcoded 'or 3' fallback for lockFreeUsesMax in the snapshot — fixed to use GameConfig.Defense.LockFreeUsesMax.

The literal 3 now exists in exactly one place (GameConfig.lua:56). Sanitize() starts from PlayerProfile.default(), which now sources from GameConfig, so the repair path is automatically single-sourced. sanitize() clamping bounds (0-10, 1-10) are validation limits, not defaults — left as-is. No circular dependency (GameConfig does not import PlayerProfile).

title: R1.5: DataStore health state machine is half-wired — recordSuccess/recordFailure/tryRecover are dead code, recovery never runs
description:
SEVERITY: P2 (reliability feature from TASK 10.5 works only by accident of the save() path; designed recovery never happens; dead public API invites misuse).

FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22.

ROOT CAUSE
DataManager exposes recordSuccess(), recordFailure(), and tryRecover() (~lines 624-645) as the public health API, but NOTHING in the codebase calls them. The only health transitions live inline inside DataManager.save() (~lines 548-559). Consequences:
