1. tryRecover() is never invoked, so once isDataStoreHealthy flips false after 3 consecutive failures, it stays false until a save happens to succeed — but services may gate behavior on isHealthy() and reduce save attempts, making spontaneous recovery LESS likely. The intended cooldown-based recovery path is dead.
2. Loads (GetAsync failures in DataManager.load) do NOT feed the failure counter — a server where loads fail but saves never run reports healthy. Health currently means "save health only", which is not what the API names promise.
3. Dead exported functions are a trap: the next agent will call recordFailure from some new path and double-count, because save() already counts inline.

FIX RECIPE (choose ONE coherent design; recommendation below)
Option A (recommended — minimal, honest): make save()/load() the sole owners of health transitions.
  - Delete recordSuccess/recordFailure from the public surface (or make them local helpers called by save AND load).
  - Feed load failures into the same counter (a failed GetAsync is as much a DataStore outage signal as a failed UpdateAsync).
  - Call tryRecover() from the autosave loop once per tick (cheap, single scheduler) so recovery is actually attempted after FAILURE_COOLDOWN.
Option B: keep the public API and route ALL transitions through it (save/load call recordSuccess/recordFailure instead of inline mutation). More churn, same outcome. Only worth it if external services will report failures — currently none do.

CONSIDERATIONS
- TASK 10.5s design intent (from its commit fe7680e) was: after N consecutive failures mark unhealthy -> clients show a warning -> cooldown -> attempt recovery. The client-facing half (snapshot health flag) IS wired; the recovery half is not. This bead completes the original intent rather than redesigning it.
- Distinguish consecutive-failure semantics across save+load: a successful load should reset the counter only if we believe read-success implies write-health; safer to reset only on successful WRITE, and count both failure kinds. Document the chosen semantics in a comment.
- isHealthy() is consumed by StateSync.snapshot (client warning) — verify the flag flaps are not spamming clients; consider hysteresis (require 2 consecutive successes to flip back healthy) as a cheap stability win while touching this code.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] No dead exported health functions: every exported fn has >= 1 real caller, or is removed.
- [ ] Load failures participate in the health counter (or an explicit code comment explains why they must not).
- [ ] tryRecover (or its replacement) is invoked from a scheduled path and can flip a server back to healthy after an outage.
- [ ] Behavior under a simulated outage is documented in the bead close reason.
close_reason:
Completed: Refactored DataStore health state machine to Option A (minimal, honest). Changes in src/server/DataManager.lua:
1. Made recordSuccess/recordFailure local helpers (removed from DataManager.* public surface) — eliminates dead API that invited double-counting.
2. save() now calls recordFailure()/recordSuccess() instead of inline mutation (deduplication).
3. load() now calls recordFailure() on v2 GetAsync failure — load failures participate in the health counter. V1 migration load failures are NOT counted (v1 store is non-fatal, separate from v2 health). A successful read does NOT reset the counter (only successful writes prove write-health).
4. tryRecover() is now called from the autosave loop (once per 60s tick) — recovery actually happens after FAILURE_COOLDOWN instead of never.
5. Removed getFailureCount() from public surface (no callers — dead).
Behavior under simulated outage: 3 consecutive save/load failures -> unhealthy flag flips -> client warning via snapshot. Autosave loop calls tryRecover() every 60s; after 60s cooldown, flips healthy -> next save confirms or denies. If saves fail again, flips back unhealthy. No flapping protection added (tryRecover cooldown provides 60s stability).

title: R1.6: Persistence observability — log per-player save outcomes + v1->v2 migration result species (support/debug aid)
description:
REPURPOSED on plan-space re-review (2026-07-22). Original scope was a micro-optimization: recheck sessions[player] at task-execution time inside the autosave spawn. Dropped as low-value churn — save() already nil-guards, no user impact, and touching the autosave loop is riskier than the theoretical inefficiency it fixed.

NEW INTENT (user-facing justification): when a player reports "I lost fish/coins", support currently has almost nothing to reconstruct the timeline. Two cheap, high-signal logs close most of that gap. This is the kind of observability that turns a 2-hour guessing session into a 2-minute log read.
design:
SCOPE
1. Per-player save outcome logging: DataManager.save already warn()s on FAILURE (~line 576). Add a single print() on SUCCESS with player name + UserId + timestamp (+ optionally coin/stored-fish counts for richer forensics). Cheap (one log per save), and it makes the difference between "we have no idea what happened" and "we can see exactly when their data last persisted". Include the isShutdown flag so shutdown saves are distinguishable from checkpoint/autosave.
2. Migration result logging (folded in from closed R1.7): the v1->v2 migration print (DataManager.load ~line 405) currently logs only the SOURCE (cash/rodLevel/liveWell counts). Extend it to also log the RESULTING species list after fromRarityIndex conversion, e.g. MIGRATION v1->v2: user=X source{...} result{Bluegill x2, Carp x1}. Permanent auditability of an irreversible one-time conversion.

CONSIDERATIONS
- Keep volume sane: one line per save, not per field. If log spam becomes a concern at scale, gate the success log behind a verbose flag — but at 8 players/server and 60s autosave + checkpoint saves, volume is trivial.
- Do NOT log full profile contents (privacy/noise); counts + identifiers only.
- These logs are the debugging substrate for the R1.x correctness beads — landing them early makes verifying R1.1/R1.3 fixes in Studio much easier.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Successful save prints one line: name, UserId, os.time, isShutdown, coin + stored-fish counts
[ ] Migration log prints the result species list
[ ] No full-profile dumps; no per-field logging
[ ] rojo build passes
close_reason: Completed R1.6 persistence observability: added SAVE OK log in DataManager.save with user, time, shutdown flag, coins, and stored-fish count; improved v1->v2 migration log to print the resulting species list. Rojo build passes.

title: R1.7: v1->v2 migration species pick uses unseeded math.random — fairness + auditability of legacy fish conversion
description:
SEVERITY: P3 (theoretical fairness issue, no data loss; migration runs once per legacy player, but the conversion is permanent and un-auditable today).

FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22.

ROOT CAUSE
FishInstance.fromRarityIndex (src/shared/FishInstance.lua ~lines 84-95, landed in wqw.12) picks the replacement species for a legacy v1 rarity-index fish via pool[math.random(1, #pool)] using the global math.random stream. Two issues:
1. FAIRNESS: the global stream is shared with every other math.random call on the server. The outcome for a given legacy player depends on how many unrelated rolls happened first — not on anything about that player. Two players with identical v1 liveWells can receive wildly different-value species of the same rarity (e.g. two Uncommons with different BaseSellValue), with no design intent behind the variance.
2. AUDITABILITY: the migration print log (DataManager.load ~line 405) records the SOURCE (cash/rodLevel/liveWell counts) but not the RESULT species list. If a legacy player disputes their converted aquarium, there is no way to reconstruct what they were given.

FIX RECIPE
1. Use a dedicated Random.new() instance seeded per-player (e.g. Random.new(userId + migrationEpoch)) so conversion outcomes are a deterministic-ish function of the player, not of global RNG history. (Full determinism is optional; isolation from the global stream is the point.)
2. Extend the migration log line to include the resulting species list: MIGRATION v1->v2: user=X source{...} result{Bluegill x2, Carp x1}. One extra string.format, permanent auditability.

CONSIDERATIONS
- Do NOT seed the global math.random anywhere on the server — that would couple unrelated systems (fishing rolls use Random.new() instances already, keep it that way).
- Seeding with os.time() alone reintroduces predictability across servers booting in the same second; userId in the seed breaks that symmetry.
- This only affects the ONE-TIME migration path; runtime fish creation already goes through proper Random instances (verified in the fishing-domain review, invariant #6).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Migration species selection uses a per-player Random instance, not global math.random.
- [ ] Migration log records the resulting species list.
- [ ] A v1 fixture profile migrates to the same species set given the same seed inputs (documented in close reason).
close_reason: Obsolete on plan-space re-review (2026-07-22): the v1->v2 migration is a bounded, sunsetting one-time path (legacy players migrate once, then never again). Per-player seeding adds complexity for near-zero user-facing value; global math.random is already OS-seeded and the migration path holds no exploit surface (server-side, no client input, one-shot). The genuinely useful half — logging the migration RESULT species list for support/audit — was folded into R1.6 (repurposed as the persistence observability bead). Avoid: don't gold-plate a path that is disappearing.

title: DEFENSE-SANITIZE-BOUNDS: sanitize clamps Defense free-use fields to hardcoded 10 instead of GameConfig.Defense.LockFreeUsesMax (3)
description:
## Finding (verified in code 2026-07-24, RainyLynx-Jul24 fresh-eyes review)

src/server/DataManager.lua:348-356 — the DEEP SANITIZE Defense block clamps with a hardcoded magic-number upper bound of 10:

  clean.Defense.LockFreeUsesRemaining = math.clamp(math.floor(data.Defense.LockFreeUsesRemaining), 0, 10)   -- line 351
  clean.Defense.LockFreeUsesMax        = math.clamp(math.floor(data.Defense.LockFreeUsesMax), 1, 10)          -- line 354

The single source of truth is GameConfig.Defense.LockFreeUsesMax = 3 (src/shared/GameConfig.lua:55-56), which PlayerProfile.default already uses for the default Defense shape (PlayerProfile.lua:102-104) and AquariumService's missing-Defense rebuild uses (AquariumService.lua:246). sanitize is the LAST line of defense against corrupted/exploited DataStore data (DataManager.lua:82 comment), yet it lets LockFreeUsesRemaining values of 4..10 survive untouched (clamped to themselves), inflating the free-lock-use budget above the configured max of 3.

## Root cause
Residual of R1.4 (egf.4, closed): the Defense SHAPE was single-sourced to GameConfig, but the sanitize CLAMP BOUNDS were left as literal 10. No other sanitize clamp uses a hardcoded magic-number upper bound — the equipment/aquarium loops derive bounds from #GameConfig.Upgrades.X, and the quest-progress clamp uses q.target (DataManager.lua:122). Only these two Defense lines are wrong.

## Impact
Low frequency, bounded blast radius: LockFreeUsesRemaining only ever DECREMENTS from 3 in normal play (AquariumService.lua:272), so values >3 only arrive via DataStore corruption/migration. But sanitize exists precisely to neutralize that class of input. A corrupted or maliciously-crafted save with LockFreeUsesRemaining=10 grants the player up to 10 free aquarium locks instead of the configured 3, bypassing the soft-gate cooldown escalation (the "no free uses -> 2x cooldown" path at AquariumService.lua:265-267 is only reached at 0).

## Fix (minimal)
Replace the literal 10 with GameConfig.Defense.LockFreeUsesMax on both lines. GameConfig is already required and used throughout sanitize (e.g. line 146), and GameConfig.Defense.LockFreeUsesMax is provably a number when sanitize runs (PlayerProfile.default() — called at line 133 — already reads it).

  clean.Defense.LockFreeUsesRemaining = math.clamp(math.floor(data.Defense.LockFreeUsesRemaining), 0, GameConfig.Defense.LockFreeUsesMax)
  clean.Defense.LockFreeUsesMax        = math.clamp(math.floor(data.Defense.LockFreeUsesMax), 1, GameConfig.Defense.LockFreeUsesMax)

## Test plan
Add a regression case to test/specs/DataManagerSanitize.spec.lua (DataModel bucket): feed Defense = { LockFreeUsesRemaining = 10, LockFreeUsesMax = 10 } and assert both clamp to GameConfig.Defense.LockFreeUsesMax (3); also assert a value of 2 passes through unchanged (lower-bound sanity). NOTE: sanitize is DataModel-bound (requires game:GetService for FishInstance/FishDefinitions), so this spec runs under --datamodel (Roblox Studio) and is NOT verifiable on this Linux box — record per AGENTS.md as NOT-verified-on-Linux. Linux verification: scripts/run_tests.sh --pure (no regression to pure modules) + luau-analyze/selene on changed files (no NEW errors vs baseline). UBS N/A for .lua.
close_reason:
Fixed in commit a00e5a4 (pushed harbor-heist/main). DataManager.lua sanitize Defense clamps now use GameConfig.Defense.LockFreeUsesMax (3) instead of hardcoded 10 on both LockFreeUsesRemaining ([0,max]) and LockFreeUsesMax ([1,max]). A corrupted/malicious save with free-use values 4..10 no longer survives the defense layer. Updated test/specs/DataManagerSanitize.spec.lua: the two existing 999->10 assertions now assert the config max, plus two egf.8 regression cases (4..10 gap clamps to max; in-range values pass through unchanged).

VERIFICATION (headless Linux): scripts/run_tests.sh --pure -> EXIT 0 (coverage gate green, all modules at threshold). luau-analyze: DataManager error multiset identical vs HEAD (zero new); spec +6 baseline it/expect 'Unknown global' (no new error types). selene: identical rule categories on DataManager; spec +6 undefined_variable (same rule). UBS n/a (no Lua scanner).

NOT verified on Linux (needs Roblox Studio per AGENTS.md): the DataModel sanitize spec behavioral run (test/specs/DataManagerSanitize.spec.lua runs under --datamodel). Studio follow-up: confirm sanitize({Defense={LockFreeUsesRemaining=7,LockFreeUsesMax=8}}) yields 3/3, and 999 yields 3/3.

title: EPIC R2: Deep-Review Economy Unification & Config Validation
description:
EPIC R2 — umbrella for the fishing/economy findings from CoralBays full-codebase deep review (2026-07-22).

PROVENANCE / METHOD
Line-by-line review of src/server/FishingService.lua, src/shared/GameConfig.lua, FishDefinitions.lua, FishInstance.lua, ZoneDefinitions.lua, and RodService.lua AFTER wqw.4 (bite window 3.5s) and wqw.24 (cast luckBonus inflates effective bite zone to ceiling 0.85) landed. The review VERIFIED 11 core invariants correct (zone nesting, server-authoritative accuracy tiers, re-roll 15% hard floor, luck stacking, cleanup on leave, os.clock/os.time discipline, protocol desync guards). The findings below are the residual issues.

WHY THIS MATTERS (project context)
The economy is the retention engine: stored fish generate passive income, income buys upgrades, upgrades catch rarer fish. If the three income definitions (GameConfig.Rarities[].incomePerSec, FishDefinitions.Species[].IncomePerMinute, Economy.IncomeToValueRatio) disagree — and they currently disagree by up to 16x on the same fish — then every tuning pass lies to someone: either the shop UI, the audit log, or the actual accrual. Silent divergence is worse than a wrong number. Separately, the wqw.24 ceiling math is correct TODAY but only because the config happens to satisfy two unenforced inequalities (ceiling > every rod zone size; perfect zone nested in good zone). A future balance edit can silently invert the skill incentive.

SCOPE (children)
- B.1 Income-field consumption audit (P1) — read-only inventory of which definition is actually live.
- B.2 Unify income to a single source of truth (P1, blocked by B.1).
- B.3 Startup income invariant assertion (P2, blocked by B.2).
- B.4 Startup config-validation harness (P2) with subtasks B.4.1 (ceiling vs rod zones), B.4.2 (perfect subset of good), B.4.3 (rarity-order monotonicity).
- B.5 Dynamic RARITY_ORDER derivation (P3).

DESIGN INTENT (for future self)
The review recommendation is BaseSellValue x IncomeToValueRatio as the single source (PRD V1 passive-income model: income derived from value, capped by MaxUnclaimedIncome). But B.1 must confirm what is actually consumed before B.2 deletes anything — GameConfig.Rarities[].incomePerSec may be dead config, or may have a consumer outside the reviewed files (e.g. docs, shop UI strings). Verify, then cut.

DONE WHEN: exactly one function computes income-per-time for a fish, every config invariant that the minigame math assumes is asserted at server boot, and deleting a rarity from GameConfig cannot silently desync FishDefinitions.
close_reason: Reconciliation 2026-07-26: all 8 children closed; R2 economy unification done-when satisfied via children.

title: R2.1: Audit which of the three income definitions is actually live (consumption inventory)
description:
TYPE: read-only investigation + written report (no code changes). Blocks R2.2.

FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22 (fishing domain, finding HIGH-1).

BACKGROUND — THE THREE DEFINITIONS
Income-per-time for a stored fish is currently DEFINED in three places that disagree by up to 16x on the same fish:
1. GameConfig.Rarities[].incomePerSec (src/shared/GameConfig.lua ~lines 8-12): Common=0.2/sec => 12/min.
2. FishDefinitions.Species[].IncomePerMinute (src/shared/FishDefinitions.lua): e.g. Bluegill (Common) = 1/min. Consumed by FishInstance.new -> fish.IncomePerMinute -> StateSync.incomePerSec (the LIVE accrual path, verified: AquariumService income loop reads stateSync.incomePerSec).
3. GameConfig.Economy.IncomeToValueRatio (0.05): implies BaseSellValue x 0.05 => Bluegill(15) = 0.75/min.

The LIVE path today is #2 (FishInstance.IncomePerMinute, summed in StateSync.incomePerSec with tier multipliers). #1 and #3 are suspected dead-or-misleading config, but this was only verified for the reviewed files — a consumer may exist in shop UI strings, client display code (init.client.lua income previews), docs, or analytics.

WHY AUDIT BEFORE CUTTING (first principles)
Deleting config that a UI label reads produces silent wrong-tooltips (the worst kind: players make decisions on false numbers). Keeping dead config that looks authoritative guarantees the next balance pass edits the wrong table. The only safe move is an exhaustive consumer inventory first.

SCOPE OF AUDIT
- rg for: incomePerSec, IncomePerMinute, IncomeToValueRatio, incomePerMinute across ALL of src/ (server, client, shared), docs/, PRD.md, scripts/.
- For each hit classify: LIVE (affects accrual), DISPLAY (affects UI text), DOC (documentation), DEAD (no consumer).
- Special attention: src/client/init.client.lua (income preview labels), ShopService/shop UI (does any upgrade description quote income numbers derived from a different definition?), StateSync.snapshot fields sent to client.

DELIVERABLE
A comment on this bead (or short docs note) listing every reference with its classification, plus the recommended single source of truth for R2.2. Recommendation going in: keep #2 (FishInstance carries IncomePerMinute, because per-species variation is a design feature — a tank of Commons should differ by species), DERIVE it from BaseSellValue x IncomeToValueRatio at FishInstance.new time (kills the hand-maintained duplication), and DELETE Rarities[].incomePerSec. But the audit may reveal constraints that flip this.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Every textual reference to the three fields is classified LIVE/DISPLAY/DOC/DEAD.
- [ ] The chosen single source is justified against PRD V1 passive-income model (income derived from value, capped by MaxUnclaimedIncome).
- [ ] R2.2 can start with zero open questions.
close_reason: Completed: Full income definition audit. Found 3 definitions disagree by 12-18x. #2 (FishDefinitions.IncomePerMinute) is the LIVE source. #1 (Rarities[].incomePerSec) has 1 DISPLAY consumer (client:1179, shows wrong numbers ~12x high) and is DEAD for accrual. #3 (IncomeToValueRatio) is pure DEAD config with zero consumers. R2.2 can proceed: keep #2, delete #1+#3, fix client:1179 display, no balance changes. Audit comment posted.

title: R2.2: Unify fish income to a single source of truth (kill the 16x divergence)
description:
SEVERITY: P1 (economy correctness: tuning edits made against the wrong table silently do nothing — or worse, the UI quotes rates the accrual never pays).

Blocked by R2.1 (audit must complete first). FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22 (HIGH-1).

GOAL
Exactly ONE function/field computes income-per-time for a fish. Everything else derives from it or is deleted.

EXPECTED SHAPE (subject to R2.1 findings)
1. FishInstance.new computes IncomePerMinute = BaseSellValue x GameConfig.Economy.IncomeToValueRatio (rounded sensibly, min 0 or a documented floor) unless FishDefinitions overrides it per-species for deliberate design variance (document the override as the exception path).
2. Delete GameConfig.Rarities[].incomePerSec (or, if the audit finds a live consumer, convert that consumer to the unified value first, then delete).
3. Any DISPLAY consumer (shop/income UI) reads the same computed value the accrual uses — no parallel math client-side. If the client needs it, StateSync.snapshot must send it (check snapshot first; it may already send incomePerSec).
4. Migration: existing stored FishInstance records persist IncomePerMinute. Decide + document: (a) leave legacy values (players keep grandfathered rates — simpler, kindest), or (b) recompute on load in sanitize (consistency, but silently nerfs/buffs existing players). Default to (a) with a code comment; (b) only with a migration log line.

CONSIDERATIONS
- MaxUnclaimedIncome cap (GameConfig.Economy, 50000) and tier multipliers (N13 aquarium, N17 dock) are DOWNSTREAM of the per-fish value and unaffected — do not touch them here.
- Balance impact: switching Bluegill from hardcoded 1/min to 15x0.05=0.75/min is a nerf to Commons; the audit table from R2.1 should include the before/after per-species delta so the balance owner can adjust IncomeToValueRatio in the same PR if they want parity. THAT DECISION BELONGS TO THE BALANCE OWNER — this bead unifies the plumbing and surfaces the numbers; it does not pick the economy level.
- Keep FishInstance.validate in sync if IncomePerMinute becomes derived (it may currently require the field to exist; derived-at-construction keeps it present, so likely no change).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] One definition site; all consumers use it (accrual == display == audit log).
- [ ] Dead fields removed or explicitly marked deprecated with a removal bead.
- [ ] Legacy-player decision implemented + documented.
- [ ] Before/after per-species income table attached to the bead close reason for the balance owner.
- [ ] rojo build passes; income loop math unchanged for unaffected species.

(3) Fixed client:init.client.lua:1179 — removed misleading per-rarity incomePerSec display (showed 12-18x wrong values); total incomePerSec from StateSync.snapshot already shown at line 1148. Legacy decision: (a) keep existing values — no income rate change, no migration needed. Before/after table: ALL species income rates UNCHANGED (no derivation applied — hand-maintained values kept as-is per audit recommendation). Only dead config removed and misleading display fixed. title: R2.3: Startup assertion — income invariant (accrual path can never disagree with the canonical definition again)
description:
SEVERITY: P2 (regression fence for R2.2; prevents silent re-divergence).

Blocked by R2.2. FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22.

INTENT
R2.2 fixes the divergence once. This bead makes it IMPOSSIBLE TO REINTRODUCE: a server-boot self-check that fails loudly (warn/error in Studio, non-fatal in production) if the invariant breaks.

WHAT TO ASSERT (finalize per R2.2 outcome)
For every species in FishDefinitions: computed IncomePerMinute == canonical formula result (within rounding tolerance). If R2.2 keeps per-species overrides, assert instead: every override is whitelisted in an explicit OVERRIDES table with a comment justifying it (no stealth hand-tuning).
Also assert GameConfig.Economy.IncomeToValueRatio is in a sane band (0 < ratio <= 0.5) — a typo like 5.0 would 100x the economy overnight.

CONSIDERATIONS
- Boot-time, not runtime: run once in init.server.lua after services load (or in a GameConfig.validate() called first). Fail with a loud warn listing every violating species; do not hard-crash a production server (availability), DO hard-fail in Studio (fast feedback). Pattern: if RunService:IsStudio() then error(...) else warn(...) end.
- This pairs naturally with the R2.4 config-validation harness — implement as ONE GameConfig.validate() with named checks so R2.4.1-3 add their assertions to the same function. Coordinate the file reservation if both beads run concurrently (both touch GameConfig.lua or a new validate module).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Boot check exists, named, and runs on every server start.
- [ ] Introducing a deliberate divergence in a test branch produces the expected loud failure in Studio.
- [ ] No measurable boot cost (it is an O(#species) arithmetic loop).

Pattern: error() in Studio (fast feedback), warn() in production (availability). O(#species) cost — negligible. title: R2.4: Startup config-validation harness — assert the inequalities the minigame math silently assumes
description:
SEVERITY: P2 (prevention: today the math is correct ONLY because config happens to satisfy unenforced constraints; a future balance edit can silently invert skill incentives).

FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22 (findings MEDIUM-1, MEDIUM-2, LOW-3).

BACKGROUND — THE ASSUMED INVARIANTS
wqw.24 made the effective bite zone interpolate from the rod base zone up to GameConfig.MiniGame.biteZoneCeiling (0.85) driven by cast luckBonus, via math.clamp(effectiveZone, baseZone, ceiling) (FishingService.lua ~line 335). The clamp is only incentive-preserving when ceiling >= baseZone for EVERY rod. Separately, the accuracy-tier logic (~lines 232-245) classifies perfect-first, then good — correct only when the perfect zone is strictly nested inside the good zone (perfectSize <= goodZoneWidth, currently 0.30-0.40 vs 0.5). Both inequalities hold TODAY and are enforced by NOTHING. A balance pass that shrinks the ceiling below a rod zone size makes perfect casts REDUCE success rate; one that grows a rod zone past the good width misclassifies tiers. Both failures are SILENT (math.clamp and if/elseif do not complain).

DESIGN INTENT
One GameConfig.validate() (new function in GameConfig.lua or a small shared/ConfigValidate module), called once at server boot from init.server.lua, Studio-fatal / production-warn (same pattern as R2.3 — share the helper). Each check is a named assertion with a message that says WHAT broke and WHERE to fix it. Subtasks R2.4.1 / R2.4.2 / R2.4.3 define the three initial checks; future config invariants should be added here by convention (mention in the module header comment).

WHY A HARNESS INSTEAD OF THREE INLINE ASSERTS
Inline asserts rot next to code that changes; a named, boot-time validation entry point becomes the documented place where config contracts live, and gives CI/Studio a single failure surface. Cost: one file, one call. Benefit: every future balance edit is machine-checked.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] GameConfig.validate() (or equivalent) runs at boot; contains the three subtask checks, each with a descriptive failure message.
- [ ] Studio boot fails loudly on a deliberately broken config; production warns and continues.
- [ ] Module header documents the convention: new config invariants get added here.
close_reason: Completed: GameConfig.validate() now contains 6 named checks covering income invariants (R2.3: checks 1-3) and minigame/economy math invariants (R2.4: checks 4-6). All subtasks (dt9.4.1, dt9.4.2, dt9.4.3) closed. Header comment documents convention: new config invariants go here as named checks. Studio-fatal, production-warn pattern. Called from init.server.lua at boot.

title: R2.4.1: Assert biteZoneCeiling >= every rod minigameZoneSize
description:
Subtask of R2.4 (config-validation harness). FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22 (MEDIUM-1).

INVARIANT: for every entry in GameConfig.RodDefinitions, minigameZoneSize <= GameConfig.MiniGame.biteZoneCeiling.

WHY: FishingService (~line 335) computes effectiveZone = clamp(baseZone + luck-scaled bonus, baseZone, ceiling). If ceiling < baseZone for any rod, the clamp returns ceiling for ALL luck levels on that rod: perfect casts give ZERO bonus (incentive inversion), and worse, the effective zone could drop BELOW the honest base zone — skilled play literally punished. Current values are safe (rods 0.30/0.35/0.40, ceiling 0.85); this check keeps them safe forever.

IMPLEMENTATION: in GameConfig.validate(), loop RodDefinitions, assert with message naming the rod level and both values, e.g. "config: rod 3 minigameZoneSize 0.90 exceeds biteZoneCeiling 0.85 — raise ceiling or shrink rod zone".

ACCEPTANCE: deliberate config break (ceiling=0.25) fails Studio boot with the named message; valid config passes.
close_reason: Completed: Added Check 4 to GameConfig.validate() — asserts biteZoneCeiling >= every rod minigameZoneSize. Violation message explains the incentive inversion (perfect casts get zero luck bonus) and where to fix it.

title: R2.4.2: Assert perfect zone nested inside good zone for every rod
description:
Subtask of R2.4 (config-validation harness). FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22 (MEDIUM-2).

INVARIANT: for every rod, minigameZoneSize <= GameConfig.MiniGame.goodZoneWidth (currently 0.5), AND goodZoneWidth < 1.0 (zones must fit inside [0,1] with the centering margins from FishingService ~line 113: center drawn from [halfGood, 1-halfGood]).

WHY: the tier classifier (~lines 232-245) checks perfect first, then good. Perfect-wider-than-good breaks the nesting assumption: the zone-center draw range (derived from halfGood) can push the wider perfect zone out of [0,1], and tier boundaries stop matching what the client renders (client receives perfect+good bounds via CastState and renders both; misnested zones = misleading UI + wrong luck bonuses). Current values safe (0.30-0.40 <= 0.5); keep them safe.

IMPLEMENTATION: two named asserts in GameConfig.validate(): (a) per-rod perfect<=good, (b) 0 < goodZoneWidth < 1. Messages name the rod/values. BONUS (cheap, same loop): assert zone-center draw interval is non-empty: halfGood <= 1 - halfGood, i.e. goodZoneWidth <= 1.

ACCEPTANCE: deliberate break (rod zone 0.6) fails Studio boot naming the rod; valid config passes.
close_reason: Completed: Added Check 5 to GameConfig.validate() — asserts (a) goodZoneWidth < 1.0 (centering math stays valid) and (b) every rod minigameZoneSize <= goodZoneWidth (perfect zone nested inside good zone). Violation messages explain the tier classifier break and where to fix.

title: R2.4.3: Assert rarity weight/order monotonicity across GameConfig.Rarities and FishDefinitions.RARITY_ORDER
description:
Subtask of R2.4 (config-validation harness). FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22 (LOW-3).

INVARIANT: FishDefinitions.RARITY_ORDER (hardcoded map Common=1..Legendary=5, ~line 288) must agree with the ARRAY ORDER of GameConfig.Rarities, because two independent code paths scale luck by ordinal: GameConfig.rollRarity uses the array index i, FishDefinitions.getRandomInZone uses RARITY_ORDER[name]. Reordering Rarities (or renaming a rarity) without touching the hardcoded map silently desyncs species weighting from rarity rolling — e.g. luck starts buffing the WRONG bucket.

ALSO CHECK (same pass, cheap): rarity weights are non-increasing down the array (Common heaviest) — an inverted weight (Legendary weight > Common weight) would flip the economy and is exactly the kind of typo a balance edit produces.

IMPLEMENTATION: build the ordinal map FROM GameConfig.Rarities inside validate() and deep-compare to RARITY_ORDER; assert weights monotonic non-increasing. Messages name the mismatching rarity. NOTE: R2.5 (dynamic RARITY_ORDER) makes the first check obsolete-by-construction; if R2.5 lands first, implement only the weight-monotonicity half and close this bead noting the overlap.

ACCEPTANCE: swapping two entries in GameConfig.Rarities fails Studio boot naming the desynced rarity; weight inversion fails likewise; valid config passes.
close_reason: Completed: Added Check 6 to GameConfig.validate() — (a) builds ordinal map FROM GameConfig.Rarities array order and deep-compares to FishDefinitions.RARITY_ORDER (catches reorder/rename desync between the two luck-scaling code paths), (b) asserts weights are non-increasing (Common heaviest — inverted weight flips economy).

title: R2.5: Derive FishDefinitions.RARITY_ORDER from GameConfig.Rarities (delete the hardcoded duplicate)
description:
SEVERITY: P3 (robustness; no live bug today). FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22 (LOW-3).

ROOT CAUSE: FishDefinitions.lua (~line 288) hardcodes RARITY_ORDER = { Common=1, ..., Legendary=5 }, duplicating the array order of GameConfig.Rarities. Two consumers scale luck by ordinal and must agree (rollRarity uses array index; getRandomInZone uses the map). The duplication exists only because the map predates a derive-at-boot helper.

FIX: at module load in FishDefinitions, build the map by iterating GameConfig.Rarities (name -> index), replacing the literal. One small loop; zero runtime cost after boot; makes R2.4.3s desync check obsolete-by-construction (keep that beads weight-monotonicity half).

CONSIDERATIONS: FishDefinitions already requires GameConfig (verify import order — no circular require: GameConfig must not require FishDefinitions; check before implementing. If a cycle appears, export a small init function instead and call it from init.server.lua before services start). Update the module header comment to document the derivation.

ACCEPTANCE: RARITY_ORDER is computed, not literal; deleting/reordering a rarity in GameConfig propagates correctly; rojo build passes; coordinate with R2.4.3 owner to avoid double-implementing the desync check.
design:
SEVERITY: P3 (robustness; no live bug today). FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22 (LOW-3). REVISED on plan-space re-review: dropped the circular-require concern — verified GameConfig.lua contains ZERO require() calls (pure data module), so FishDefinitions -> GameConfig is acyclic by construction. No init-order hazard exists.

ROOT CAUSE
FishDefinitions.lua (~line 241) hardcodes RARITY_ORDER = { Common=1, Uncommon=2, Rare=3, Epic=4, Legendary=5 }, duplicating the array order of GameConfig.Rarities. Two consumers scale luck by ordinal and must agree: GameConfig.rollRarity uses the array index i; FishDefinitions.getRandomInZone uses RARITY_ORDER[name]. Reordering or renaming a rarity in GameConfig without editing the hardcoded map silently desyncs species weighting from rarity rolling (luck buffs the wrong bucket).

FIX (mechanical, ~5 lines)
At module load in FishDefinitions, build the map by iterating GameConfig.Rarities (name -> index) instead of the literal:
  local RARITY_ORDER = {}
  for i, rarity in ipairs(GameConfig.Rarities) do RARITY_ORDER[rarity.name] = i end
Keep the exported FishDefinitions.RARITY_ORDER name so existing consumers (line 262) are untouched.

WHY THIS IS SAFE
- GameConfig is a pure data module (no requires) -> no load-order dependency.
- FishDefinitions already reads GameConfig elsewhere (verify; if it does not currently require it, adding the require is still cycle-free per above).
- The derived map is identical to the literal today (Common..Legendary = 1..5), so behavior is unchanged — this is a refactor, not a balance change.

RELATION TO R2.4.3
R2.4.3 (rarity-order sync assertion) checks that the hardcoded map matches the config. Once THIS bead lands, the map can never disagree by construction, making that assertion's first half obsolete. R2.4.3's weight-monotonicity half (weights non-increasing down the rarities array) remains independently valuable and stays. Coordinate: whichever lands first, the other adjusts; link recorded as related.

ACCEPTANCE: RARITY_ORDER computed not literal; deleting/reordering a rarity in GameConfig propagates correctly; rojo build passes; R2.4.3 owner notified via Agent Mail to descope the desync half.
close_reason: Completed: RARITY_ORDER now derived from GameConfig.Rarities in FishDefinitions.lua; removed obsolete desync half from GameConfig.validate (monotonicity check retained). Rojo build passes.

title: BUG 15.1 [FIXED]: DataManager nil-deref on first join (data.dailyQuestKey)
description:
SEVERITY: CRITICAL — 100% reproducible crash on EVERY new player's first join.

ROOT CAUSE: DataManager.load() (line 335) read `data.dailyQuestKey` from the raw saved-data parameter, but `data` is nil for brand-new players (no DataStore entry) or when the datastore load fails. Indexing nil throws "attempt to index nil with 'dailyQuestKey'", crashing the session initialization.

WHY IT WAS MISSED: The sanitize() call above it (`local profile = sanitize(saved)`) looks like it handles everything, so the later `data.dailyQuestKey` reads seem safe. But `data` is the original function parameter, not the sanitized output. This only crashes on first join or datastore failure — easy to miss in testing if you always have existing save data.

FIX APPLIED (N2): Read from `profile.dailyQuestKey` (the sanitized result, guaranteed non-nil) instead of `data.dailyQuestKey`.

This is a NEW bug class (#12 in the server-authority-gap-checklist): raw-parameter dereference in load functions. Added to the skill's permanent checklist.

RELATED: No existing EPIC 14 task covered this. Supersedes the round-1 assumption that load paths were safe.

title: BUG 15.2 [FIXED]: Legacy liveWell migration overwritten by unconditional sanitizeStoredFish(nil)
description:
SEVERITY: CRITICAL — silent total fish loss for v1 saves with a partial Aquarium table.

The round-1 review (EPIC 14, TASK 14.2) identified this class and added a "fix" at line 172, but the guard was in the WRONG PLACE — it re-ran sanitizeStoredFish when `aq.StoredFish` WAS a table (redundant), instead of guarding line 146 where the actual clobbering happened.

FIX APPLIED (N3): Made line 146 conditional (`if type(aq.StoredFish) == "table" then`). Removed the redundant line-172 block.

This is checklist item #3 (Legacy Migration Overwrite) — the same class as round-1, but the round-1 fix was incomplete. The lesson: when adding a guard, verify it guards the ACTUAL overwrite site, not a redundant re-execution.

title: BUG 15.3 [FIXED]: Quest rewards never credited — session.cash does not exist
description:
SEVERITY: CRITICAL — quest completion shows "+$X" toast but credits ZERO coins, AND errors silently ("arithmetic on nil value").

ROOT CAUSE: QuestService.processList (line 87) wrote `session.cash += q.reward`. The session object (DataManager.lua:311-339) has no `cash` field — money lives at `session.profile.Coins`. The `session.cash +=` operation creates a new transient field that is never read by anything and never persisted. Worse, `+=` on nil errors with "attempt to perform arithmetic on a nil value" inside the quest loop.

FIX APPLIED (N4): Replaced with:
  session.profile.Coins = PlayerProfile.clampCoins(session.profile.Coins + q.reward)
  session.profile.TotalCoinsEarned = session.profile.TotalCoinsEarned + q.reward

This routes through clampCoins (matching every other coin-grant path) and tracks lifetime earnings. Added `require(PlayerProfile)` import to QuestService.

IMPACT: Every daily and weekly quest (11 templates, 3 daily + 2 weekly slots) was silently broken. Players could see the completion notification but received no reward. The error happened inside a loop in a potentially task.spawn'd context, so it may have silently broken ALL quest progression (not just the completing quest).

title: BUG 15.4 [FIXED]: Lock/Alarm/Capacity upgrade system non-functional (5-file chain broken)
description:
SEVERITY: HIGH — 3 of 5 shop upgrade categories were unbuyable AND non-functional even if purchased.

ROOT CAUSE: A 5-file chain of broken connections:
  1. PlayerProfile.default() had NO LockLevel/AlarmLevel fields (sanitize dropped them)
  2. DataManager.sanitize() wrote them to top-level `clean.lockLevel` (orphan fields, not in schema)
  3. ShopService.BuyItem returned `bad_kind` for "lock"/"alarm" (only handled rod/bait/aquarium)
  4. Client sent kind="capacity" but server only accepted "aquarium" (kind mismatch)
  5. Client built shop rows from GameConfig.Upgrades.Capacity (3 entries) but server sold from GameConfig.AquariumUpgradeTiers (4 entries, different prices)
  6. AquariumService read `victimSession.alarmLevel` (nonexistent session field) — alarms never triggered
  7. AquariumService lock-duration scaling was a stub (`if UpgradeLevel > 1 then -- future`)
  8. StateSync.snapshot didn't expose any upgrade levels — client always saw 0
  9. RodService.read `session.rodLevel` (nonexistent) — rod visual always level 1

FIX APPLIED (N5-N10):
  - Added LockLevel, AlarmLevel to PlayerProfile.Aquarium schema
  - Sanitize persists them in the nested Aquarium table + maps legacy top-level fields
  - ShopService handles "lock", "alarm" kinds with proper catalog + currentLevel dispatch
  - Client sends "aquarium" (not "capacity") and uses AquariumUpgradeTiers catalog
  - Client KIND_META and refreshShop use "aquarium" key consistently
  - AquariumService.handleSteal reads profile.Aquarium.AlarmLevel
  - AquariumService.LockAquarium scales duration/cooldown from Upgrades.Lock[lockLevel]
  - StateSync.snapshot exposes upgradeLevel, lockLevel, alarmLevel
  - RodService reads profile.Equipment.EquippedRodLevel
  - Removed dead KIND_CATALOGS/getCatalog from ShopService

This is checklist item #13 (Client-Server Kind/String Mismatch) and #14 (Cosmetic Field On Nonexistent Session Attribute). Both added to the permanent checklist.

title: BUG 15.5 [FIXED]: onFishCaught quest hook never called + rarity type mismatch
description:
SEVERITY: HIGH — 3 of 11 quest templates (catch_rarity) could never progress.

ROOT CAUSE: QuestService.onFishCaught(session, rarityIndex) was defined but never called anywhere. Even if it HAD been called, it expected a numeric rarity index, but FishInstance.Rarity is a STRING ("Common", "Rare", etc.). title: BUG 15.6 [FIXED]: Unclamped coin write on steal-fence (AquariumService:282)
description:
SEVERITY: HIGH — the ONLY coin-granting path in the codebase that bypassed clampCoins.

ROOT CAUSE: When an attacker's aquarium is full and they fence a stolen fish for coins, AquariumService.handleSteal did `attackerSession.profile.Coins = attackerSession.profile.Coins + stolenFish.BaseSellValue` — raw write, no clamp, no TotalCoinsEarned update.

EXPLOIT: Near the MAX_COINS ceiling (999,999,999), a large fencing payout could overflow past the cap. Also, a crafted/hijacked BaseSellValue (if sanitize regressed) could go negative — this was the one path that wouldn't clamp to >= 0.

FIX APPLIED (N12): Route through PlayerProfile.clampCoins + update TotalCoinsEarned.

This is checklist item #9 (Unclamped Economy Writes). The round-1 review caught most sites; this one was added later (the steal-fence path) and missed the clamp.

title: BUG 15.9 [FIXED]: TOCTOU race in steal resolution — stale index could steal raid-protected fish
description:
SEVERITY: CRITICAL (latent) — raid-protected Legendary fish could be stolen despite IsRaidProtected check.

FOUND BY: Background audit subagent (C6 in its report). The parent pass missed this because the race window is currently safe (single-threaded Luau, no yields between eligibility check and table.remove). But the code is FRAGILE — any future refactor that adds a yield (task.spawn, remote call) between snapshot and remove would make it exploitable.

ROOT CAUSE: handleSteal builds an `eligible` list of INDICES (positions in victimFish) for non-raid-protected fish. After the rng roll picks `stolenIndex = eligible[N]`, `table.remove(victimFish, stolenIndex)` removes at that index. If the victim sold/stored a fish between the eligibility snapshot and the remove (via a concurrent SellAll or StoreSingleFish), the indices shift, and `table.remove(victimFish, 3)` could now point at a DIFFERENT fish — possibly a raid-protected Legendary.

FIX APPLIED (N15): Capture the fish REFERENCE (not index) at selection time. Re-find it in the live list via identity comparison (`fish == targetFish`), re-validate `not fish.IsRaidProtected`, then remove. If the target vanished or became protected, fail-safe as a miss rather than stealing the wrong fish.

title: EPIC 10: Security & Anti-Exploit Hardening
description:
PRD security/anti-exploit section (lines 477-484). The current code already has good server-authoritative patterns (nil guards, bounds checks, capacity re-checks, distance validation). This epic formalizes it into an AntiExploitService + adds rate limiting, suspicious-action tracking, and audit logging.

WHY P0: exploits destroy game economies and trust. PRD: 'No client can change currency, rarity, inventory, or raid result.' All valuable transactions server-confirmed.

## BACKGROUND & JUSTIFICATION
Part of the Harbor Heist V1 build — migrating the current prototype to full PRD compliance (see PRD.md). The current codebase is a working server-authoritative prototype with 5 rarity tiers, basic cast/store/sell, passive income, and basic theft/lock PvP. The PRD demands a richer experience: structured data, 12-20 species, timing minigame, claimable income, collection book, upgrade tree, scheduled opt-in raids, onboarding, analytics, and anti-exploit. Every bead serves the overarching goal: a cozy fishing-aquarium game with optional bounded PvP heists that creates social stories without griefing.

## PRD TRACEABILITY
See PRD.md for the authoritative spec. PRD requirement IDs (e.g. FISH-01, AQUA-03, PVP-05) are referenced in task acceptance criteria.

- [ ] All remotes rate-limited
- [ ] Suspicious actions logged
- [ ] No dup/negative/exploit path exists
- [ ] Raid transfers atomic
- [ ] Failure handling user-visible

title: TASK 10.4: Transaction atomicity (no dup on partial failure)

Two fixes: (1) resolveRaidSuccess: wrapped fish transfer (table.remove from victim + table.insert/fence to attacker) in pcall — on throw, fish is rolled back to victim at original index, transfer_failed logged via auditLog, never duplicated/lost. (2) requestRaidAttempt: reordered challenge math BEFORE commitAttackerCooldowns — a throw in challenge building no longer burns cooldowns with no raid to play. Post-transfer side effects (immunity, bookkeeping, notifications, saves) correctly excluded from the transaction scope. Rate limiting, single-resolution, TOCTOU re-validation, and position clamping already verified correct from gdj.14.

title: EPIC 30: Design System Foundation — Spacing, Typography, Colors, Components
description:
**BACKGROUND & RATIONALE:**

The Harbor Heist client currently lacks a cohesive design system. After reviewing 5,324 lines of init.client.lua, we found:
- 20+ different padding values (4, 6, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 24, 32px)
- 12+ text sizes with no clear ratio (9-30px)
- Inconsistent corner radii (5, 10, 12, 14, 16, 999px)
- Hardcoded color values throughout instead of semantic tokens
- No button hierarchy (all buttons look the same)

**WHY THIS MATTERS:**
Premium apps like Stripe, Linear, and Vercel achieve their polished feel through systematic design. Without a foundation, every new UI element requires ad-hoc decisions that drift from consistency. This epic establishes the primitives that everything else builds on.

**IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGY:**
1. Define constants at the top of init.client.lua (after the existing UI table)
2. Use 4px/8px grid for all spacing
3. Use 1.25 ratio for typography (12, 15, 19, 24, 30px)
4. Create semantic color tokens (surface.primary, surface.secondary, text.primary, etc.)
5. Define corner radius hierarchy (sm=8, md=12, lg=16, xl=20, pill=999)
6. Create button variants with consistent styling

**DEPENDENCIES:**
This is the foundation epic. All other UI/UX epics depend on this being complete first, because they'll use the new design system primitives.

**CONSIDERATIONS:**
- Must maintain backward compatibility with existing UI
- Should be a gradual migration (new code uses system, old code updated in follow-up passes)
- Mobile and desktop may need different scales
- Color tokens must work for both light and dark themes (future-proofing)

**SUCCESS CRITERIA:**
- All new UI code uses design system constants
- Zero hardcoded color/spacing values in new code
- Clear visual hierarchy in typography and components
- Button variants clearly distinguish primary/secondary/ghost/danger actions

title: EPIC 20: UI/UX Audit Remediation — Player-Facing Polish & Core-Loop Repair
description:
Umbrella epic for the 2026-07-23 fresh-eyes UI/UX audit of the entire player-facing experience.

## Origin & method
A full manual audit read every line of the client UI (src/client/init.client.lua, 3042 lines), the shared UI-driving config (GameConfig, FishDefinitions, ZoneDefinitions, FishVisuals), and the server services whose contracts the UI renders (Fishing, Aquarium, Raid, Shop, Quest, Collection, StateSync, DockManager, init.server). Git history/blame was used to separate regressions from long-standing issues and to confirm suspected bugs against server contracts rather than guessing.

## Findings (17 total)
- CRITICAL (2): bite minigame never starts (BiteEvent arity regression — fishing is unplayable); desktop action bar clips on <=768px-wide viewports.
- HIGH (6): FISH button has no lifecycle states; cast-while-casting is silent; HUD income shows +$0.0/sec all early game; catch success is a vertically-clipped toast; three minigame overlays stack uncoordinated on the same screen position; claimable income invisible from the HUD.
- MEDIUM (9): SELL ALL liquidates tank+bag unconfirmed; lock status absent from raid targets; raid targets never auto-refresh; lock button copy leaks implementation detail; onboarding prompt hardcoded offset can collide on small mobile screens; collection book uses placeholder F/? icons; no inventory sorting; no persistent cast-zone guidance; minor polish (first-join cash count-up, unbounded toast stack, unreadable raid hint text, unclamped desktop panels).

## Sequencing rationale
1. EPIC 21 first: the P0 core-loop regression blocks play AND blocks verification of every other fishing-flow improvement.
2. EPICs 22-24 next: the feedback layers (cast lifecycle, overlay arbitration, HUD economy visibility) are what make the loop feel alive — these map directly to the PRD UX principles (immediate fishing feedback; always-visible Coins/capacity/claimable income).
3. EPICs 25-26: safety and clarity (unconfirmed SELL ALL is a rage-quit vector; raid panel transparency is a PRD PVP-04 requirement).
4. EPICs 27-29: polish and discoverability — the difference between functional and premium.

## Non-goals for this umbrella
- No visual rebrand: keep the existing design-token system (UI palette, Gotham font scale, EASE_* tweens) — it is already consistent and good.
- No new gameplay features beyond what findings require.
- Preserve the rebuild-guard signature patterns (inventory/collection lists) and the server-authoritative contracts; UI work must not weaken anti-exploit boundaries.

## PRD alignment
PRD First five minutes requires catch -> store -> earn -> upgrade inside the opening session and time-to-first-catch under 2 minutes. Finding 1 makes that impossible today; findings 3-8 are the difference between a funnel that retains and one that leaks at every step.

title: EPIC 21: P0 Core-Loop Repair — Bite Minigame Regression
description:
THE core-loop-breaking bug from the audit (finding 1). Fishing is currently unplayable end-to-end.

## What is broken
The server fires the bite with TWO arguments (FishingService.lua:213): remotes.BiteEvent:FireClient(player, zoneId, BITE_WINDOW_SECONDS). The client handler declares ONE parameter (init.client.lua:3003): Remotes.BiteEvent.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(windowSeconds) ...). windowSeconds therefore receives the zoneId STRING ("StarterPier"). runMinigame assigns minigameWindow = that string, and the first frame of the sweep loop hits `elapsed > minigameWindow` -> runtime error "attempt to compare number < string" -> the spawned loop dies instantly, the FISH ON! minigame frame never becomes visible, and every bite times out server-side (SubmitCatchInput is never invoked by the player).

## Git forensics (verified via blame, not speculation)
- 869d93a (fishing rework) had the CORRECT two-arg signature: function(zoneId, windowSeconds).
- d5505ac ("client UI nil-safety + cleanup") collapsed the handler to one arg AND dropped the minigameWindow local.
- 2c07147 ("Fix client UI regressions from d5505ac") restored the minigameWindow local but MISSED the handler signature — so the regression shipped.
Lesson for future self: when a cleanup commit touches remote handlers, diff the handler arity against every FireClient call site. Arity drift between FireClient args and handler params fails SILENTLY in Luau until a value is used in a typed operation.

## Why P0 above everything
PRD success metrics (time-to-first-cast < 60s, time-to-first-catch < 2 min, first-session funnel) are unachievable. Every fishing-flow UX improvement in EPICs 22-23 cannot even be verified until this lands. Nothing else in this umbrella should start before TASK 21.1.

## Scope
Fix the signature, add a regression guard so this class of bug is caught mechanically next time, and leave a manual verification runbook for the catch flow.

title: TASK 21.1: Fix BiteEvent client handler signature (one-line P0 fix)
description:
Restore the two-argument BiteEvent handler so the bite minigame actually runs.

## The fix
init.client.lua:3003 — change:
    Remotes.BiteEvent.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(windowSeconds)
to:
    Remotes.BiteEvent.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(zoneId, windowSeconds)
Server contract (FishingService.lua:213): FireClient(player, zoneId, BITE_WINDOW_SECONDS). Keep the zoneId parameter NAMED (not _) even though it is unused today — it documents the wire contract and enables future zone-specific presentation. This is exactly what the original rework commit 869d93a had.

## TRUE failure signature (corrected 2026-07-23 plan-space review)
The original bead text said the frame "never appears" — wrong. runMinigame sets minigameFrame.Visible = true BEFORE the sweep loop starts (init.client.lua:2646), so the FISH ON! frame DOES appear — frozen. The marker never moves (stuck at x=0, outside the zone), the loop dies on its first comparison (number > string), so: no timeout expiry, minigameActive stays true (blocking ALL future bites via the early return at 2642), and any tap on the frozen frame submits markerPos=0 -> hit=false -> guaranteed miss. The symptom a tester sees: "the FISH ON! box pops up but the marker never moves and every catch fails" — sticky across casts. This is why the acceptance criteria below require a MOVING marker; a visible frame alone proves nothing.

## Also in scope (same class of bug, cheap to verify while here)
Walk every Remotes.*.OnClientEvent handler in init.client.lua and diff its parameter list against the matching server FireClient call site: StateChanged (1 arg), Notify (2 args), RaidWindowChanged (3 args, verified vs RaidService.lua:760), CastState (3 args; the (false, 0) / (false, 0, nil) fires are handled by the else branch), BiteEvent (2 args), OpenAquarium/OpenShop (0 args), QuestProgressChanged (1 arg). The audit already checked these and found BiteEvent to be the only mismatch — record the re-verification result in a closing comment.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Bite minigame frame appears AND the marker VISIBLY SWEEPS back and forth (a frozen frame is the bug, not the fix)
- [ ] Tapping with the marker inside the zone catches a fish end-to-end in Studio play-solo (fish lands in bag)
- [ ] Letting the minigame time out hides the frame and notifies (loop alive)
- [ ] No "attempt to compare" errors in client log
- [ ] Handler-arity walk documented in a closing comment
close_reason: Fix landed in commit e5c7295 (BiteEvent handler arity: function(zoneId, windowSeconds)). Handler-arity walk completed by DarkElk; regression guard in hvfh.1.2 (commit b1a51ab). Runtime verification runbook is TASK 21.3 (separate bead). Marking closed — code is committed and in the tree; stale in_progress status corrected by RainyLynx.

title: TASK 21.2: Regression guard for remote-payload shape (BiteEvent + handler arity)
description:
Make this CLASS of bug fail loudly next time instead of silently killing the core loop.

## Why this task exists
The P0 regression survived TWO code reviews (d5505ac introduced it, 2c07147 partially fixed the same commit and still missed it) because nothing mechanical checks that client handler arity matches server FireClient arguments. Luau binds extra args to nil and missing args positionally; the failure only manifests at runtime when a mistyped value hits a typed operation. That is too late.

## PRIMARY deliverable: static arity contract check (decided in plan-space review 2026-07-23)
A small script (pure runner or CI shell step) that:
1. ast-grep/rg every server-side FireClient/FireAllClients call per remote name and counts payload arguments (excluding the player arg).
2. ast-grep/rg every client OnClientEvent:Connect(function(...) handler and counts declared params.
3. Fails the build on any mismatch where a client handler declares FEWER params than the server sends (more params is safe — they bind nil).
Source of truth for the pairing: Remotes.lua EVENT_NAMES + the client Remotes folder enumeration (init.client.lua:12-15). Runs in the existing CI pipeline alongside TestEZ — deterministic, no game instance needed, catches the drift at lint time.

## STRETCH (only if EPIC 19 harness reaches client UI state)
E2E case: fire a synthetic BiteEvent with the real payload shape and assert the minigame frame becomes Visible AND marker.Position changes within N seconds. Higher fidelity but depends on harness capabilities that are still being built (harborheist-pe9a). Do NOT block this bead on the harness — the static check ships regardless. title: EPIC 22: Fishing Feedback & Cast Lifecycle UX
description:
Audit findings 3, 4, 5, 6: the cast-to-catch lifecycle is a 6-10 second black box and its emotional payoff is a clipped toast.

## Background
- The FISH button distinguishes only casting true/false (init.client.lua:2392-2398), and `casting` spans the ENTIRE bite wait (rod castTime 2-4s + random 2-6s, FishingService.lua:109-110). No waiting-for-bite state, no cooldown feedback, no bite-ready state.
- doFish (init.client.lua:2736) silently returns when casting — the button feels dead exactly when the player is most tempted to press it.
- incomeLabel renders +$%.1f/sec (init.client.lua:2382) — a starter tank at 2 coins/min displays +$0.0/sec for the whole early game, hiding that the aquarium earns anything.
- A catch (even Legendary) is a single top-toast line; server strings like "You caught a Legendary Abyssal Eel! (worth $500)" (FishingService.lua:454) wrap to 2 lines in a fixed 40-42px toast with TextWrapped=true and clip vertically. PRD explicitly requires "cast cue, bite cue, timing feedback, catch reveal, and rarity presentation".

## Why it matters
This is the retention core: the PRD first-session funnel depends on the loop FEELING responsive and rewarding. The game currently hides its two biggest dopamine beats (a bite arriving, a rare catch landing) behind silence and a clipped toast.

## Design intent for future self
Server already pushes the edges we need (CastState true/false at FishingService.lua:144/187; structured catch result from SubmitCatchInput returning { ok, speciesId, rarity, value } at FishingService.lua:457). All fixes are client-side presentation; do NOT add new remotes, and do NOT re-derive economy values client-side (R2.2/dt9.2 lesson: StateSync snapshot is the single source of truth).

title: TASK 22.1: FISH button lifecycle states (idle / waiting / bite-ready)
description:
Give the primary action button a real state machine instead of a binary casting flag.

## Current behavior
render() (init.client.lua:2392-2398) shows "CASTING"/"..." greyed whenever the casting flag is true — and that flag spans the ENTIRE 6-10s bite wait. There is no visual difference between "cast flying", "waiting for a bite", and "A FISH IS BITING".

## Target states and EXACT transition edges (verified against server event order)
- idle -> waiting-for-bite: on CastState(true). Subtle animated state, e.g. "WAITING…" with a slow stroke pulse.
- waiting -> idle: on CastState(false) with no bite (cast cancelled / left zone / hands full).
- waiting -> bite-ready: CastState(false) fires FIRST then BiteEvent fires (verified: FishingService.lua:187 precedes :213 in the same deferred callback). So: on BiteEvent, enter bite-ready REGARDLESS of the flag state. "FISH ON!" in the warn accent.
- bite-ready -> idle: when the LOCAL minigame closes (tap or timeout — onMinigameTap / the expiry path in runMinigame). NOT on any CastState event; none is coming.

## Explicitly descoped (plan-space review 2026-07-23)
The original draft included a "rejected/cooldown red flash" state. REMOVED: cast rejections (hands full / wrong zone / rate-limited) reach the client ONLY as Notify toasts — RequestCast is a RemoteEvent with no return value, so there is no rejection signal to drive a button state. Options were a new remote (scope creep, server change for a nicety) or string-matching Notify text (fragile — violates the same no-string-parsing principle documented on TASK 22.4). The server toast IS the rejection feedback; the button does not need to mirror it.

## Constraints
- No new remotes: CastState and BiteEvent already provide every edge needed.
- Single state variable, transitions only on server events — never per-frame text churn in render().
- Mobile parity: the mobile stack shows the action key + short label (init.client.lua:2178-2193); the state must read on a 60px round button (color/pulse, not just text).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All three states visually distinct on desktop AND mobile
- [ ] bite-ready survives the CastState(false)-before-BiteEvent ordering (state test documented)
- [ ] No toast duplication with server notifications
close_reason: Implemented FISH button state machine (idle/waiting/bite-ready); headless-verified (tests 100/0/0, arity 8/8, selene zero-new, isolated lune logic pass). Visual acceptance (3 distinct states on desktop+mobile, pulse animates) deferred to EPIC 19 E2E / Studio play-solo per the 21.1/21.3 pattern.

title: TASK 22.4: Catch reveal card for Rare+ and first catches
description:
The biggest dopamine beat in the game is currently a clipped 3.6s toast. PRD demands "catch reveal and rarity presentation".

## Target behavior
A centered reveal card on catch success for Rare/Epic/Legendary (and for EVERY first-session catch regardless of rarity): species display name (fishDisplayName helper already exists, init.client.lua:874-880), rarity-colored frame/glow, sell value + income/min line, EASE_POP scale-in, auto-dismiss ~2.5s, tap-to-dismiss. Common/Uncommon keep the lightweight toast (rarity inflation would cheapen the moment). Mobile: width 1,-24 matching the minigame overlays.

## Data source (important, avoids string parsing)
SubmitCatchInput already RETURNS structured data to the invoking client: { ok, speciesId, rarity, value } (FishingService.lua:457). Build the card from that invoke result — do NOT parse the server notify string, and do NOT add a new remote. The server toast stays as the ambient notification.

## First-catch detection (added in plan-space review — avoid the race)
Do NOT read state.onboarding.HasCaughtFirstFish to decide "first catch": the invoke result and the state push race each other, and the flag may arrive after the card decision. Instead track a local catchesThisSession counter incremented on each ok=true SubmitCatchInput result; counter == 1 -> always show the card. Local, deterministic, no race.

## Coordination (hard dependency)
The card MUST register with the overlay arbitration manager from TASK 23.1 (as a display-only, non-modal entry) rather than appear as a fourth uncoordinated overlay. If 23.1 is not done, this task waits — that sequencing is the whole point of EPIC 23.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Rare+ catches show the reveal card; Common/Uncommon do not
- [ ] Card never overlaps an active minigame overlay (arbitration respected)
- [ ] First successful catch of a session ALWAYS gets the card (local counter, no server-flag race)

title: EPIC 23: Minigame Overlay Arbitration
description:
Audit finding 7: three timed-input overlays fight for the same pixels and the same clicks with zero coordination.

## Background
- Cast overlay (init.client.lua:2262) and raid minigame (init.client.lua:1935) both anchor at vertical center (0.42 mobile / 0.58 desktop); the legacy bite minigame frame (init.client.lua:2591) is also dead-center.
- Each minigame independently connects to the GLOBAL UserInputService.InputBegan — the cast overlay (2983), the raid minigame (2062), and the bite minigame twice (2716 + 2724). A single click during overlapping activity can be consumed by the wrong game (e.g. a raid tap resolving a fishing bite).
- The cast overlay and raid minigame are near-identical code (marker tween, glow, zones at 2259-2353 vs 1932-2009) — duplicated wiring that has already diverged once (the BiteEvent regression).

## Why it matters
Raid windows are time-bound (5 min) and raids are server-deadline-bound (8s) — an overlay collision during a raid is not a cosmetic glitch, it loses the player their raid attempt. Conversely a raid overlay must never be preempted by a fishing one. Priority order for future self: raid > bite > cast.

## Scope
One central manager owning which timed-input overlay is active, one input router, mutual exclusion rules, and unified visuals. The catch-reveal card (TASK 22.4) must register with this manager rather than become a fourth uncoordinated overlay.

title: TASK 23.1: Central minigame/overlay manager with single input router
description:
One owner for "which timed-input overlay is active", replacing four independent global InputBegan listeners.

## Problem recap (audit finding 7)
Cast overlay (init.client.lua:2983), raid minigame (2062), and bite minigame (2716 + 2724 — two listeners) each hook UserInputService.InputBegan independently. Overlapping activity means a click can resolve the WRONG game. All three overlays also anchor to the same screen-center region.

## MODEL (revised in plan-space review 2026-07-23 — initiation gating, NOT preemption)
The original draft specified preempt-by-priority (raid > bite > cast). Rejected: preemption either eats an in-flight catch (minor but real player loss) or requires queue-with-server-deadline machinery (the raid attempt deadline starts when RequestRaidAttempt is processed server-side — an 8s queued overlay is a race against the server clock). The key realization: BOTH overlays are PLAYER-INITIATED (cast via F, raid via the panel RAID button), so nearly every collision can be prevented at initiation, before any server commitment exists:

1. Gate CAST initiation: doFish refuses (with toast "Finish the raid first!") while the raid minigame is active. RequestCast has not fired, nothing committed server-side.
2. Gate RAID initiation: the RAID target button refuses (with toast "Reeling in a fish — one moment!") while cast/bite is active. RequestRaidAttempt has not fired, no server deadline started.

title: EPIC 24: HUD & Economy Visibility
description:
Audit findings 8, 17 (cash count-up, toast stack): the HUD hides money the player has earned and lies on join.

## Background
- PRD UX principle, verbatim: "The player always sees their current Coins, rod, aquarium capacity, and claimable income." Today claimable income appears ONLY as the CLAIM button label inside the aquarium panel (init.client.lua:2494), and the in-world dock sign shows fish count + stored value but no income (DockManager.lua:683). A player with $800 waiting gets zero indication until they open the tank.
- animateCashTo counts up from displayedCash=0 on the first snapshot (init.client.lua:213-259) — a returning player with $50k watches a fake $0 -> $50,000 spin-up and a bogus "+$50,000" gain floater on every join.
- Toasts are fixed-height (40-42px) with TextWrapped (init.client.lua:305-333): any 2-line message clips vertically; rapid events (catch + discovery + quest + raid window) stack unbounded into a 300px column covering top-center.

## Why it matters
Passive income IS the tycoon fantasy (PRD: aquarium as visible passive-income source). If the number is invisible, the fantasy is invisible. The join count-up actively trains players to distrust the balance display.

## Constraints for future self
unclaimedIncome is already in every StateSync snapshot — no server change needed for the HUD element. Never re-derive income client-side (R2.2/dt9.2: snapshot is the single source of truth).

title: TASK 24.3: Toast system hardening (fit, cap, glanceability)
description:
Toasts are the primary server-to-player channel and they clip, flood, and all look alike.

## Problems (verified)
- Fixed 40-42px height + TextWrapped (init.client.lua:305-333): 2-line server strings (e.g. "You caught a Legendary Abyssal Eel! (worth $500)") clip vertically.
- Unbounded stacking in a 300px host (284-297): catch + discovery + quest + raid-window events pile into a column covering top-center.
- Color is the ONLY category signal; a red raid warning and a red error look identical at a glance.

## Scope
(a) Auto-size toast height: AutomaticSize Y + min height 40/42 + internal padding, so 2-line messages fit. Keep width fixed. (Accent bar sizes relative to toast height already — verify it still scales.)
(b) Cap visible toasts at 3; queue the rest FIFO; drain on dismiss. Raid-victim and DataStore-warning toasts jump the queue (severity beats arrival order).
(c) Category icon/chip in the accent bar (catch/quest/raid/warn/info) — color-plus-label satisfies the PRD accessibility rule (never color alone).

## Category plumbing (decided in plan-space review — server-side, backward-compatible)
Do NOT infer category client-side from color or message text (fragile; violates the no-string-parsing principle). Extend the Notify contract with an OPTIONAL 3rd payload arg: Remotes.notify(player, message, color, category) (Remotes.lua:27 is a two-line wrapper — add and forward). showNotification(message, color, category) defaults to "info" when nil, so every existing call site keeps working unchanged. Migrate the highest-value call sites to pass a category (catch/raid-victim/quest/lock/datastore); the rest can trickle in later — this task only requires the contract + defaults.

## Note
TASK 22.4 moves Rare+ catches off toasts onto the reveal card, which relieves (b); implement (b) anyway — quests and raid events still burst.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Longest known server strings render fully (test the catch and raid-victim messages)
- [ ] 6 rapid events never show more than 3 toasts; queue drains in order
- [ ] Category chip renders from the new optional arg; nil-category toasts still render fine (backward compat)
close_reason: Completed: Toast system hardening with 3 parts implemented. (a) Auto-size height: AutomaticSize.Y on toast frame + text label, min 40/42px. (b) Cap 3 visible with FIFO queue: MAX_VISIBLE_TOASTS=3, activeToastCount tracking, toastQueue with drainToastQueue on dismiss. Severe categories (raid-victim, datastore) jump to queue front via table.insert(q,1,entry). (c) Category chip: TOAST_CATEGORIES maps all server categories to uppercase labels (CATCH/QUEST/RAID/RAID!/LOCK/ECON/NEW!/CAST/MISS/SAVE/INFO) rendered as bold accent-colored label. Backward-compatible: nil category defaults to INFO. All 11 server category strings covered. Quality gates: pure-spec tests 100 pass/0 fail, remote arity contract holds (Notify 3-3), coverage gate 55/55. Code-verified, not Studio-verified.

title: EPIC 25: Aquarium Panel Safety & Clarity
description:
Audit findings 9, 12: one tap can liquidate your entire income engine, and the defense controls speak implementation, not player.

## Background
- SELL ALL in MY AQUARIUM (init.client.lua:794) calls RequestSellFish, which liquidates ALL stored live-well fish PLUS all carried fish (AquariumService.lua:127-180) with no confirmation and no undo. The codebase already half-acknowledged the trap: a comment at init.client.lua:826-829 explains why the bag panel has NO sell-all — yet the more destructive version sits in the aquarium panel one tap away. Selling your tank destroys your passive income engine; for a casual player who misreads the button this is a rage-quit-level event.
- Lock button copy (init.client.lua:2448-2450): "LOCK (90s) [2/3 free]" / "[no free]". Players have no model for what a "free use" is; "[no free]" reads like an error state. Server truth (AquariumService.lua:243-263): 3 free uses with normal cooldown, then locks still work but with 2x cooldown — a soft gate, not an error.
- The raid opt-in gate ("10 catches OR an upgrade", DEC-4) is hardcoded client-side in TWO places (init.client.lua:1893 and 2465), duplicating server logic that will drift.

## Why it matters
PRD positions the aquarium as the emotionally valuable centerpiece; the UI should protect that attachment, not put a self-destruct button next to the claim button. Clarity in defense controls is also a PvP-fairness issue (PRD PVP-03/PVP-04: players must understand their lock tools).
close_reason: Reconciliation 2026-07-26: all 3 children closed (25.1-25.3); aquarium panel safety complete.

title: TASK 25.1: SELL ALL confirmation guard in the aquarium panel
description:
One tap currently liquidates every stored income-earning fish plus the whole carried bag, no confirm, no undo.

## Evidence
SELL ALL (init.client.lua:794) -> RequestSellFish -> AquariumService.lua:127-180 sells ALL StoredFish (unless locked) + ALL carried fish. The bag panel deliberately omits sell-all for exactly this reason (comment at init.client.lua:826-829) — yet the aquarium panel, the emotional centerpiece per PRD, keeps the nuclear option one tap from CLAIM.

## Decision (made deliberately, revisit only with reason)
Option (a) two-step confirm, CLIENT-ONLY: first tap re-arms the button to "SELL ALL $X? TAP TO CONFIRM" showing the exact payout computed from the current snapshot; 3s window; second tap invokes. Zero server-contract change, preserves the locked-tank special case ("Stored fish untouched — aquarium locked", which already reads well).
Option (b) split SELL BAG vs SELL TANK with a scope param — cleaner long-term but changes the server contract and needs a migration of player muscle memory.
CHOSEN: (a) for V1. If the team later wants (b), file it as a new bead with server work scoped.

## Details
- Payout preview must reflect lock state (locked => carried-only payout, matching AquariumService.lua:145-151).
- Re-arm must reset on any state push that changes the payout (new catch/store/sell) so the confirmed number is never stale.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Accidental single tap can no longer sell anything
- [ ] Confirm label always shows the exact current payout and lock-scope
- [ ] Locked-tank path still sells carried only, with the existing explanatory toast
close_reason: Completed: SELL ALL now requires a two-step confirm. First tap arms the button with exact payout + lock-scope label ('SELL ALL $X? TAP' or 'SELL BAG $X? TAP' when locked). Second tap fires RequestSellFish. 3s auto-disarm timeout. Disarms on: payout-changing state push (catch/store/sell/lock toggle), panel close. Payout computed from new storedFish snapshot field (added to StateSync, same pattern as carriedFish). Zero sell-handler change. Includes pre-existing uncommitted changes from another agent: animateCashTo first-render snap (EPIC 24 finding 8), runMinigame type guard, BiteEvent comment cleanup.

title: TASK 25.3: Single-source the raid opt-in gate via snapshot
description:
The "10 catches OR an upgrade" eligibility rule (DEC-4) is hardcoded client-side in TWO places (init.client.lua:1893 and 2465) — and also hardcoded server-side in AquariumService.isNewPlayerProtected (totalCatches >= 10, no config constant). Three copies of one rule: a guaranteed drift vector.

## Fix (revised in plan-space review — avoid the circular require)
The original draft said "computed server-side where the rule actually lives (validateAttacker path)". DANGER: StateSync cannot require RaidService or AquariumService — both already require StateSync (income cache invalidation + pushes), so a reverse require is a Luau circular dependency that loads partial module tables. CORRECT approach: single-source the gate at the CONFIG level, which every service may read freely:
1. Add to GameConfig.Raid: unlockTotalCatches = 10 (and keep the upgrade-or semantic documented alongside).
2. AquariumService.isNewPlayerProtected reads GameConfig.Raid.unlockTotalCatches instead of the literal 10.
3. StateSync.snapshot adds raidEligible (bool) and raidUnlockCatches (number, for the "7/10" progress text) computed from profile data + GameConfig — no service requires needed.
4. Both client call sites (raid panel opt-in mirror + aquarium panel opt-in button) render snapshot fields only; the constants and the upgrade-check logic disappear from the client.

## Why bother (future-self justification)
Every prior client/server duplication in this codebase eventually lied to players: the minigame zone hardcode (round-3 fix), the dead per-rarity income display (R2.2), the capacity-shop kind mismatch (N10). The pattern is consistent: server owns rules, client owns rendering. Cheap insurance of the same kind.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Gate constant exists exactly once (GameConfig.Raid); client contains no eligibility logic
- [ ] Locked-state progress text still shows catches progress (e.g. "7/10 catches or an upgrade")
- [ ] Server gate behavior unchanged (existing authority tests keep passing)
close_reason: Completed: DEC-4 raid eligibility gate single-sourced via GameConfig.Raid.unlockTotalCatches=10. Server: AquariumService.isNewPlayerProtected reads GameConfig.Raid.unlockTotalCatches (line 398). StateSync.snapshot exposes raidEligible (bool) and raidUnlockCatches (number) computed from profile+config (lines 134-135). Client: both call sites (init.client.lua:1978 and 2713) render snapshot fields only — no client-side eligibility logic remains. Acceptance criteria met: constant exists once in GameConfig, progress text shows catches count, server authority unchanged.
