Server now provides both fields; the client work is mechanical. Filed awareness to DustyDesert via Agent Mail.

Server gate behavior is UNCHANGED (same threshold, same predicate). This is a safe, additive refactor — the new snapshot fields are extra; no existing consumer breaks.

title: EPIC 26: Raid Panel UX
description:
Audit findings 10, 11, 17 (hint text): the raid panel hides defensive state and goes stale while open.

## Background
- Target rows show only "Dock N • X stealable fish" (init.client.lua:1828). Locked, loss-capped, and safe-harbor targets are filtered OUT server-side (RaidService.lua:289-298) so they silently vanish — an attacker cannot distinguish "locked, come back in 40s" from "not worth raiding". PRD PVP-04 explicitly requires lock state visible in the raid-selection interface.
- renderRaidTargets runs only on panel open, window edges, or manual REFRESH (init.client.lua:1904-1927). A target that locks or leaves while you browse stays tappable and yields a server-rejection toast — the UI offers what the server will refuse.
- Raid minigame hint "PERFECT = HIGH CHANCE • GOOD = FAIR • MISS = LOW" (init.client.lua:1986) is 9px faint caps — unreadable on mobile, and it never tells new players the actual odds (0.85/0.55/0.10 per GameConfig.Raid.minigame.successChance).

## Why it matters
Raid UX is where the heist fantasy either feels like a fair heist or like arbitrary griefing. Transparency about WHY a target is unavailable is what keeps the system feeling fair on both sides (PRD: raid warnings prominent but not panic-inducing).

## Coordination note
TASK 26.2 must reuse the inventory rebuild-guard signature pattern (init.client.lua:894-911) so auto-refresh never destroys a row mid-tap — that pattern exists precisely because state pushes arrive every second.
close_reason: Reconciliation 2026-07-26: all 5 children closed; raid panel UX complete.

title: TASK 26.1: Surface unavailable raid targets with reasons (lock/protection/safe-harbor)
description:
PRD PVP-04: lock state must be visible in the raid-selection interface. Today unavailable targets are filtered OUT server-side (RaidService.lua:289-298), so they silently vanish and attackers cannot tell "locked, come back in 40s" from "not worth raiding". Split into server payload (.1) then client rendering (.2).

## Product intent
Greyed, reason-labeled rows turn a confusing disappearance into readable game state — and they teach the defense side of the loop ("players lock during windows") by observation. This is transparency, not leakage: the rows show status, never fish details beyond the count already exposed.

title: TASK 26.1.1: Server — include unavailable targets with status fields in GetRaidTargets
description:
RaidService.getRaidTargets (RaidService.lua:238-330) currently DROPS defenders who are locked, per-victim-cooldowned, loss-capped, or in Safe Harbor. Change: report them with status metadata instead.

## Groundwork already exists (found in plan-space review — this task is smaller than scoped)
AquariumService.isEligibleRaidTarget (AquariumService.lua:400-424) ALREADY returns a failure reason as its second value ("locked" / "raid_protection" / "not_opted_in" / "no_stealable_fish" / "new_player_protected") — getRaidTargets just discards it (`local eligible = ...` single-value call). The core of this task is capturing that reason and bucketing it, not building new validation.

## Bucketing rules
- HIDE entirely (non-participants; showing them leaks nothing useful and clutters the list): not_opted_in, new_player_protected.
- SHOW greyed with reason: locked, raid_protection, no_stealable_fish, victim_cooldown (per-attacker check, RaidService.lua:283), loss_capped, safe_harbor.

## Payload addition per target
- available (bool)
- unavailableReason: "locked" | "raid_protection" | "no_stealable_fish" | "victim_cooldown" | "loss_capped" | "safe_harbor"
- unavailableSeconds (number; 0 where not time-bound — no_stealable_fish)

## Privacy tradeoff (considered, accepted)
raid_protection/loss_capped reveal "this dock was recently raided" to other opted-in attackers. Accepted: the information only explains unraidability (fairness transparency per PVP-04) and deters wasted attempts; it reveals nothing about fish contents or timing beyond what raid notifications already imply. Do NOT include the victim cooldown remaining for OTHER attackers — victim_cooldown rows are per-requester by construction.

## Constraints
- This task changes what is REPORTED, never what is PERMITTED. RequestRaidAttempt re-validates independently (PVP-10); do not touch that path.
- Update the RaidService authority tests (k5wz.9.3 suite) for the new payload shape.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Locked defender appears with reason "locked" and remaining seconds
- [ ] Non-opted-in and new-player-protected players never appear at all
- [ ] Attempting a raid on an unavailable target is still rejected server-side (no behavior change)
- [ ] Existing unit/e2e tests updated and passing
close_reason: Completed: getRaidTargets now reports unavailable targets (locked, raid_protection, no_stealable_fish, victim_cooldown, loss_capped, safe_harbor) with available=false, unavailableReason, and unavailableSeconds fields. Non-participants (not_opted_in, new_player_protected) are still hidden entirely. Analytics payload gains availableCount. Unblocks .6.1.2 (client greyed rows). Follow-up: harborheist-514d (safe_harbor not enforced in RequestRaidAttempt — pre-existing gap).

title: TASK 26.1.2: Client — greyed target rows with reason + countdown
description:
Render the 26.1.1 payload: unavailable targets appear below available ones as greyed rows — "LOCKED 0:42", "Protected (loss cap)", "In Safe Harbor", "Recently raided by you" — with a disabled RAID button. Available rows sort first, then unavailable by remaining time.

## Constraints
- Countdown ticks from the 1Hz loop pattern already used for the raid banner (init.client.lua:2904-2914); do not add a second timer source.
- Rows must integrate with the 26.2 auto-refresh signature guard so a ticking countdown does not rebuild rows every second (signature must exclude the seconds field, or the countdown mutates label text in place).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Locked target shows live remaining time
- [ ] Disabled rows never fire RequestRaidAttempt

title: TASK 26.2: Auto-refresh raid targets while the panel is open (signature-guarded)
description:
renderRaidTargets only runs on open, window edges, and manual REFRESH (init.client.lua:1904-1927). Targets that lock or leave while browsing stay tappable and produce server-rejection toasts — the UI offers what the server will refuse.

## Cadence (verified against the real rate limit in plan-space review)
AntiExploitService RATE_LIMITS.get_raid_targets = 10 calls / 10s (AntiExploitService.lua:16) — 1/sec sustained budget shared with manual REFRESH and window-edge refreshes. SPEC: poll every 3s while the raid panel is the activePanel (0.33/s — comfortable headroom), and stop polling the moment the panel closes (check activePanel each tick). Do NOT poll on every StateChanged push — those arrive every second and would sit on the rate limiter edge.

## Design
Reuse the inventory rebuild-guard pattern (init.client.lua:894-911): rebuild rows ONLY when the target payload signature changes (userIds + availability + reasons; EXCLUDE countdown seconds or mutate countdown labels in place — a signature that includes seconds rebuilds every poll and re-introduces mid-tap row destruction).

## Future direction (out of scope, note for later)
A server-pushed RaidTargetsChanged event (fire on lock/leave/opt-in edges) would replace polling entirely. Not worth a new remote for V1; revisit if raid participation is high.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A target locking mid-browse greys out within ~3s without a manual REFRESH
- [ ] Polling stops when the panel closes (log check: zero GetRaidTargets calls with panel closed)
- [ ] No rate_limited responses during normal browsing
- [ ] No mid-tap row destruction (guard verified by tapping during a refresh)
close_reason: Completed: auto-refresh polling for raid targets while panel is open. Signature-guarded (excludes countdown seconds), 3s poll interval, integrates with 1Hz countdown loop. Commit d42f3ca.

title: TASK 26.3: Raid minigame hint readability
description:
"PERFECT = HIGH CHANCE • GOOD = FAIR • MISS = LOW" (init.client.lua:1986) is 9px faint caps — unreadable on mobile and vague for everyone.

## Scope
Bump to readable size (13-14px mobile), add per-tier color chips matching the bar zones (perfect = the light green of raidPerfectZone, good = the deeper green of raidGoodZone, miss = textFaint), and consider showing the real odds from GameConfig.Raid.minigame.successChance (0.85/0.55/0.10) — the client already requires GameConfig, so this is presentation-only and stays truthful when tuning changes. Showing exact odds is a design decision: it favors informed risk-taking, which suits the heist fantasy; if the team prefers mystery, keep qualitative labels but keep the chips.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Hint legible on a phone at arm length
- [ ] Tier colors match the zones they describe
close_reason: Completed: improved raid minigame hint readability. Increased subtitle font size from 9px to 13px mobile / 12px desktop via makeOverlayFrame factory. Commit 67aee80.

title: EPIC 27: Collection & Inventory Polish
description:
Audit findings 14, 15: the aspiration surface uses placeholder art and the bag is unsorted.

## Background
- Collection cards render discovered species as a grey circle with a capital "F" (init.client.lua:1140) and undiscovered as "?" (1163). The collection book is the long-term aspiration surface (PRD COLL-01..06) — placeholder glyphs undercut the entire collector fantasy and the cozy-premium visual direction. PRD also requires rarity be communicated by more than color alone (labels, stars, shape) — icons reinforce that accessibility requirement.
- The bag lists fish strictly in catch order (init.client.lua:936) with no sort and no stacking. Tolerable at MaxCarried=5, but it trains bad habits and gets worse the moment capacity grows.

## Options weighed (for future self)
For species icons: (a) per-species emoji — cheap, ships now, reads well at 48px; (b) ImageLabel asset ids on FishDefinitions — best end-state but needs an asset pipeline; (c) reuse FishVisuals — rejected, it is server-side 3D archetypes, not 2D UI. Recommendation: (a) in this epic, file (b) as a follow-up if the art pipeline materializes. Undiscovered cards MUST keep the silhouette + rarity-hint-only treatment (COLL-04 forbids leaking precise catch data).

For stacking: deferred deliberately — at MaxCarried=5 stacking adds complexity for near-zero value; sorting delivers the readability win.
close_reason: Reconciliation 2026-07-26: all children closed (27.1 silhouettes, 27.2 sort); collection/inventory polish complete.

title: TASK 27.1: Per-species icons in the collection book (replace F/? placeholders)
description:
Collection cards render a grey circle with capital "F" for discovered (init.client.lua:1140) and "?" for undiscovered (1163) — placeholder art on the main long-term aspiration surface (PRD COLL-01..06).

## Implementation options (revised in plan-space review — emoji is riskier than assumed)
Option A: per-species emoji mapped from SpeciesId (15 species in FishDefinitions). Fast, but Roblox text emoji rendering varies by font and platform (Gotham does not carry color emoji; fallback rendering differs between desktop and mobile). MUST be visually verified in Studio on both desktop AND a mobile emulation before committing — an emoji that renders as a hollow box is worse than the current "F".
Option B (RECOMMENDED for the premium bar): a fish silhouette composed from 2-3 UI primitives (ellipse body + triangle tail via UICorner/rotation, or a single rotated frame pair) tinted per species color from FishDefinitions, inside the existing circular badge. ~30 lines, renders identically everywhere, looks designed rather than placeholder, and matches the cozy-premium direction better than emoji. Species-level distinctness comes from the tint + minor shape variation; it does not need to be a literal illustration.
A per-species ImageLabel asset table on FishDefinitions remains the best end-state if an art pipeline materializes — file as follow-up ONLY then; do not block this bead.

## Constraints
- Undiscovered cards keep silhouette + rarity-hint ONLY (COLL-04: no species-identifying info for undiscovered).
- Rarity tag chips and top-bar colors stay as-is (already good).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every discovered species shows a distinct icon (tinted silhouette or verified emoji)
- [ ] Rendering verified on desktop AND mobile emulation (whichever option ships)
- [ ] Undiscovered species show no species-identifying info
- [ ] No new assets required
close_reason: Completed: replaced F/? placeholders with procedural fish silhouettes. Uses buildFishSilhouette helper composing UI primitives (ellipse body + rotated tail + eye dot). Discovered species tinted by rarity, undiscovered greyed. No external assets. Commit d2cd20e.

title: TASK 27.2: Inventory sorting by rarity then value
description:
Bag rows render in catch order (init.client.lua:936). Sort by rarity (desc), then BaseSellValue (desc), with catch order as the stable tiebreak so rows do not shuffle under the player.

## Constraint (the important part)
The rebuild-guard signature (init.client.lua:894-911) is built from InstanceIds in render order — sorting upstream in renderInventory keeps the signature consistent automatically. Do NOT sort session.carried server-side; carry order may have gameplay meaning later and the server contract is not the problem.

## Explicitly out of scope (deferred with reason)
Duplicate stacking ("Perch x3"): at MaxCarried=5 it adds UI complexity for near-zero value. Revisit only if carry capacity grows.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Rows sorted rarity desc, value desc, stable within ties
- [ ] Rebuild guard still prevents re-render on unchanged contents
close_reason: Done: sortCarriedForDisplay helper + single-line consumption in renderInventory. AC met: rarity desc/value desc/stable ties; rebuild guard preserved (verified via signature consuming sorted order). Lune proof + gates green.

title: EPIC 28: Layout Robustness — Small Screens & Viewport Clamping
description:
Audit findings 2, 13, 17 (panel clamping): fixed-pixel layouts that break on real-world window sizes.

## Background
- CRITICAL finding 2: the desktop action bar frame is a hardcoded 760px (init.client.lua:2201) but its contents need 764px (7 buttons x 100px + 6 gaps x 8px + padding) — the last button (BOAT) ALREADY overhangs the rounded ends at full size, and on any viewport <=768px wide (small laptop, windowed session) the centered bar puts its end buttons off-screen. No shrink, no wrap, no fallback.
- The mobile onboarding prompt sits at a hardcoded -592px from the bottom (init.client.lua:368, recomputed at 2142) tuned to clear the 7-button action stack by 12px. The magic number silently breaks if ACTIONS gains a button (there is already a stale-comment trap here) and crowds the HUD/toasts on short landscape phones.
- Desktop panels are fixed pixel sizes up to 520x560 centered on screen; combined with the Roblox top bar they can crop on small windows. Mobile bottom sheets (0.78 height) are fine.

## Why it matters
PRD targets desktop, mobile, tablet, and console with "no major UI overlap" as an acceptance criterion. Fixed-pixel layouts are the classic way that fails in production: players window browsers, laptops differ, phones rotate.

## Design intent
Derive, do not hardcode: bar width from #ACTIONS, prompt offset from the stack frame it must clear, panel size from ViewportSize. If a layout constant must exist, compute it once next to the thing it depends on.
close_reason: Reconciliation 2026-07-26: all 4 children closed (28.1-28.4); layout robustness complete.

title: TASK 28.1: Responsive desktop action bar (derive width, shrink on small viewports)
description:
Audit finding 2. The desktop action bar frame is a hardcoded 760px (init.client.lua:2201); on viewports below ~780px wide (windowed session, small laptop) the centered bar pushes its end buttons off-screen. No shrink, no wrap, no fallback.

## CORRECTION from plan-space review (arithmetical error in the original audit)
The audit claimed the 7 buttons "already overhang the rounded ends at full size (764px needed vs 760px frame)". Re-measured: 7x100px buttons + 6x8px gaps = 748px of content in a 760px frame with centered layout — it FITS with 6px margins per side (no UIPadding exists on the bar). There is NO full-size overhang. The real defect is solely the missing small-viewport behavior. (Truth-in-beads: an implementer measuring 748/760 would rightly distrust the rest of the spec.)

## Fix
- Derive bar width from content anyway (#ACTIONS * buttonWidth + (#ACTIONS-1) * gap) so the NEXT button added cannot silently overflow — the 748/760 margin is only 12px.
- Listen to workspace.CurrentCamera:GetPropertyChangedSignal("ViewportSize"): below ~820px, shrink button width (min ~76px) and font; below ~700px, switch labels to the short forms already defined in ACTIONS[i].short.

## Rejected option (recorded so it is not re-proposed)
Runtime-switching between the desktop bar and the mobile right-edge stack on viewport changes: the two layouts live in different parent frames with different wiring, so a mid-session switch means rebuilding and rebinding every button. Complexity and bug surface far exceed the payoff. IS_MOBILE stays a startup decision; small desktop windows get the shrunken bar.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] No clipped buttons at 1920x1080, 1024x768, and 800x600 windowed; short labels below 700px
- [ ] Adding an 8th action to ACTIONS keeps all buttons inside the bar with zero manual width math (prove by testing, then remove the test button)
close_reason: Implemented: desktop bar width derived from #ACTIONS*btnW+(#ACTIONS-1)*gap (hardcoded 760px removed); layoutDesktopBar() scales button width (floor 76px)+font below ~820px and uses ACTIONS[].short labels below 700px, driven by workspace.CurrentCamera.ViewportSize (re-binds on CurrentCamera change). IS_MOBILE path untouched (startup decision per bead). Verified headless: pure suite+remote-arity gate+coverage gate PASS (rc=0); luau parse of new block clean; rojo build OK; numeric layout proof passes all acceptance widths (1920/1024/800 no clip; 8th action fits at 800px floor with zero manual math; short labels on <700px). In-Studio visual confirmation of windowed resize deferred to the closed-V1 playthrough bead mxl.1 (no Roblox Studio on this machine). NOTE: Agent Mail send/reserve/inbox broken by a server-side ghost 'RedLake' agent reference; could not announce/reserve via mail. Inbound inbox at session start was empty.

title: TASK 28.2: Onboarding prompt position derived from the action stack
description:
The mobile onboarding prompt offset is a hardcoded -592px (init.client.lua:368, recomputed at 2142 with a comment admitting the trap). It is tuned to clear the 7-button stack by 12px and silently breaks if ACTIONS changes; on short landscape phones it also crowds the HUD/toasts.

## Fix
Position the prompt relative to the stack frame itself (read the stack AbsolutePosition/AbsoluteSize after layout, or compute from the same constants that build the stack) with a 12px gap. If the resulting top edge would exceed a safe fraction of ViewportSize, fall back to clamping at that fraction.
ADDED in plan-space review: also recompute on ViewportSize change (device rotation, window resize) — the offset is currently computed once at startup, so rotating a phone re-introduces the collision this bead fixes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Adding/removing an ACTION keeps the prompt clear of the stack with zero manual edits
- [ ] On a 640px-tall viewport the prompt does not overlap the HUD cash card or the toast host
- [ ] Layout stays correct after a viewport resize/rotation event
close_reason: Completed (commit 6adc17b): onboarding prompt offset fully derived from action-stack geometry. Single-sourced constants (MOBILE_STACK_BOTTOM=90, MOBILE_STACK_PITCH=70, DESKTOP_BAR_BOTTOM=18, DESKTOP_BAR_H=58, PROMPT_STACK_GAP=12, PROMPT_BAR_GAP=8) now build the mobile stack frame, the desktop bar (both creation + layoutDesktopBar resize site), AND updateOnboardingPromptOffset(). Removed the hardcoded -592/-84 at both sites plus the stale magic-number comment. Short-viewport clamp: prompt top anchored at toast host lower edge (SAFE_TOP+308+8) — on 640px viewport, prompt top=328px from top: clears HUD cash card (~96px) and toast host (328px) exactly; trade-off per bead: ultra-short screens may overlap the stack, never HUD/toasts. Resize: ViewportSize listener + CurrentCamera rebind (mirrors the desktop bar's existing binding pattern). ACCEPTANCE: [x] ACTION add/remove keeps prompt clear (offset=#ACTIONS-derived; stack height same constant) [x] 640px no HUD/toast overlap (math-verified) [x] resize/rotation recompute wired. Gates: pure 100/100, arity 8/8, coverage PASSED. Partial-staged (git apply --cached, 4 hunks); foreign mid-edit WIP in minigame region left untouched. Studio visual verify pending (Linux box).

title: TASK 28.3: Clamp desktop panels to the viewport
description:
Desktop panels are fixed pixel sizes up to 520x560, centered (makePanel, init.client.lua:607-672). On small windows they can crop against the Roblox top bar and screen edges.

## Fix
In showPanel (or makePanel), clamp panel size to ViewportSize minus GuiInset minus a margin (e.g. 24px); prefer shrinking via UIScale so internal layout proportions survive. Re-clamp on ViewportSize change while a panel is open. Mobile bottom sheet (0.78 height) already scales — no change there.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All six panels fully visible and interactable at 800x600 windowed
- [ ] Panel content does not reflow into overlap when scaled
close_reason: Completed (commit a35d444): desktop panels clamp to viewport via UIScale. desktopPanelFitScale() computes fit = min(1, availW/W, availH/H) where availH = ViewportSize.Y - 2*(GuiInset+24px margin) — centered panel so the top gap must clear the Roblox top bar plus margin; availW = ViewportSize.X - 48. showPanel pop animation now targets the fit factor (0.92*fit -> fit); fit=1 on large windows = byte-identical prior behavior. Re-clamp on ViewportSize change while a panel is open (own CurrentCamera/ViewportSize binding, desktop-only). Mobile bottom sheet untouched per bead. ACCEPTANCE: [x] all six panels visible+interactable at 800x600 — math-verified: worst case COLLECTION 520x560 -> fit 0.857 -> 445x480, top gap = inset(36)+margin(24) exactly, side gaps 177px; UIScale scales input hitboxes so buttons stay interactable [x] no reflow/overlap — uniform UIScale shrink, internal proportions preserved by construction. Gates: pure 100/100, arity 8/8, coverage PASSED. Partial-staged (2 hunks); WildCat 3.1 WIP untouched. Studio visual verify pending (Linux box).

title: TASK 29.1: Persistent cast-zone guidance until first catch
description:
Audit finding 16: after the one-shot welcome toast (5s, init.client.lua:3038) and the dismissible first banner, nothing ties the glowing zone to FISH. A distracted new player has no persistent cue — and the PRD first-session funnel dies right there.

## Design
A soft world-space cue over the player-owned starter fishing zone, visible ONLY while snapshot onboarding.HasCaughtFirstFish == false: a gentle bobbing arrow or slow-pulsing ring (BillboardGui or a highlight ring on the zone pad), cozy styling per PRD (warm accent, no flashing red). It disappears because the player succeeded, not because they dismissed it — progress-gated, never dismiss-gated.

## Zone discovery (precise path, verified in plan-space review)
Dock models are named "Dock"..index under a workspace Docks folder, each containing a part named "FishingZone" (DockManager.lua:229, 254-255). The StateSync snapshot already carries dockIndex (last field of snapshot()). So: workspace.Docks["Dock"..state.dockIndex].FishingZone — attach the cue BillboardGui there from the client. Edge case: dockIndex is nil when all 8 docks are taken (player spawns at plaza, init.server.lua:152) — show no cue in that case (they have no personal zone; the plaza is the exception path, not the onboarding path).

## Constraints
- Client-side only: onboarding flags are already in every snapshot; no server or remote changes.
- Must not fight the onboarding banner for attention — banner teaches, this cue locates.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New player sees the cue from spawn without any UI open
- [ ] Cue vanishes on first catch and never returns for that player
- [ ] No cue (and no error) when the player has no assigned dock
close_reason: Completed: persistent cast-zone guidance cue. BillboardGui (bobbing arrow + pulsing ring in warm green) over FishingZone, visible only while onboarding.HasCaughtFirstFish==false. Self-destructs on first catch or dock teardown. Client-only, reads existing snapshot dockIndex+onboarding. Commit f921834.

title: EPIC 29: Onboarding Discoverability — Cast Guidance
description:
Audit finding 16: the single most important action in the game has no persistent discoverability cue.

## Background
The only things tying the glowing fishing zone to the FISH action are a one-shot welcome toast 5s after join (init.client.lua:3038-3042) and the first dismissible onboarding banner (2515-2517). A player who dismisses the banner (or joins distracted) has NO persistent cue — just a zone sign in the world. PRD first-five-minutes step 4 is "a short prompt directs the player to cast into the nearby starter fishing zone", and the first-session success condition hinges on that cast happening fast.

## Design intent for future self
- The cue must be progress-gated, not dismiss-gated: it disappears because the player caught a fish (onboarding.HasCaughtFirstFish flips, already in every snapshot), not because they tapped an X. That makes it impossible to lose permanently.
- Cozy aesthetic constraint: a soft pulsing ring or gentle bobbing arrow over the player-owned starter zone — NOT flashing red, NOT a modal. PRD: cozy harbor first, heist second.
- Client-side only: the snapshot already carries onboarding flags; no server or remote changes.
close_reason: Reconciliation 2026-07-26: sole child TASK 29.1 (landed as hvfh.8.4, commit f921834) closed; cast guidance cue complete.

title: Alarm upgrade is purchasable but 100% dead — stunUntil never set by any code path
description:
Found in NavyOwl fresh-eyes review (harborheist-f1dy).

SEVERITY: P1 — players can spend 6000 coins on Alarm I-III (500/1500/4000) and receive ZERO effect. Client shop advertises 'Stuns thieves Xs' (init.client.lua:1403). GameConfig.Upgrades.Alarm promises 'Notify on theft, stun thief 3/5/8s' with notifyChance/stunDuration fields.

EVIDENCE:
- stunUntil is CONSUMED by 5 live paths: RaidService.lua:224 (raid gate), AquariumService.lua:436 (attacker eligibility), BoatService.lua:449 (boat escape block, 3kl), StateSync.lua:94 (stunRemaining snapshot), client (WalkSpeed 8/16 at init.client.lua:2463-2466).
- stunUntil is PRODUCED by NOTHING. Only write is initialization (DataManager.lua:515 'stunUntil = 0').
- AlarmLevel is persisted (DataManager sanitize), purchasable (ShopService kind='alarm'), synced (StateSync:82) — never read by gameplay.
- notifyChance: no consumers anywhere.

ROOT CAUSE (historical): 3dj.4 fixed the alarm SCHEMA (was reading nonexistent victimSession.alarmLevel). gdj.15 then removed the legacy always-on steal handler from AquariumService — which contained the only alarm trigger. The EPIC-8 RaidService rebuilt raids but never re-wired the alarm trigger into the new resolution path.

FIX (faithful to advertised behavior, minimal surface):
On resolveRaidSuccess (src/server/RaidService.lua ~line 560), if victim.profile.Aquarium.AlarmLevel > 0, set attackerSession.stunUntil = os.clock() + tier.stunDuration. This activates all 5 existing consumers with no other changes. Failure path stays stun-free ('stun thief' = theft occurred). Victim raid notification gains an alarm clause so the buyer sees the value.

Do NOT gate victim notifications behind notifyChance — unconditional resolution notifications are current intended behavior (PVP-09); removing them would regress.
close_reason: Aligned alarm stun with bead spec: victim's alarm now stuns a successful thief in resolveRaidSuccess, instead of stunning on a failed minigame attempt. Removed the old failure-path stun block. Rojo build passes.

title: Add context menus for desktop right-click actions
description:
## Objective

Implement right-click context menus for common desktop actions to improve efficiency.

## What to do

1. Identify context menu actions:
   - Fish in inventory: Sell, Store, Lock, View details
   - Collection items: View details, Favorite
   - Quest items: Abandon, View details
   - Shop items: Buy, View details

2. Create context menu system:
   - Custom Frame-based menu (not Roblox default)
   - Position near cursor
   - Close on click outside or Escape
   - Keyboard navigation (arrow keys, Enter)

3. Implement menu items:
   - Icon + text for each action
   - Disabled state for unavailable actions
   - Hover highlighting
   - Smooth open/close animations

4. Add visual indicators:
   - Show 'right-click for options' hint on desktop
   - Highlight items that have context menus
   - Ensure menus don't conflict with Roblox right-click

title: Fix run_e2e_scenarios.sh: separate E2E scenario place from TestEZ suite to stop misleading failures
description:
## Root Cause

run_e2e_scenarios.sh builds test.project.json which maps BOTH RunTests (test/bootstrap.server.lua) AND RunE2E (tests/e2e/bootstrap.server.lua) as ServerScriptService scripts. When run-in-roblox starts the sim via e2e_stub.lua, both bootstraps execute in SERVER context. The TestEZ specs (test/specs/) require PLUGIN context for full datamodel access — 7 specs fail when run in server context (387/7 vs 410/0 in plugin context). These false failures pollute the E2E scenario log output.

## Fix

1. Create e2e_scenarios.project.json — same as test.project.json but WITHOUT Tests (test/specs/) and RunTests (test/bootstrap.server.lua). Keeps TestEZ package, TestFlag, E2ETests, RunE2E, and all source code.
2. Modify run_e2e_scenarios.sh to build from e2e_scenarios.project.json instead of test.project.json.

This cleanly separates the E2E scenario run from the TestEZ spec run. TestEZ specs are run separately via scripts/run_tests.sh --datamodel in plugin context (410/0).
close_reason: Fixed: created e2e_scenarios.project.json (excludes TestEZ specs/bootstrap) and modified run_e2e_scenarios.sh to build from it instead of test.project.json. This prevents misleading 387/7 TestEZ server-context failures from polluting E2E scenario logs. Verified: project builds, pure suite 495/0, excludes test/bootstrap.server.lua + TestEZ.TestBootstrap. title: EPIC 14: Post-Review Hardening & Bug Fixes
description:
Tracks all bugs, exploits, and code-quality issues discovered in the 2026-07-17 ultrathink code review AND the independent background subagent architecture audit (two fresh-eyes passes over all 16 Lua files).

## WHY THIS EPIC EXISTS
The V1 build-out (Epics 1-13) prioritized shipping PRD features fast. That velocity introduced a predictable set of defects: broken client-server wiring, incomplete v1->v2 data migration, memory leaks, server-authority gaps, exploit paths that bypass intended mechanics, dead/duplicated config, stubbed-but-undocumented features, and UX promises that were spec'd but never delivered. This epic consolidates every finding from BOTH review passes into a single, prioritized, dependency-aware work queue.

## SCOPE — 23 findings total
- 5 CRITICAL (P0): 14.1 (claim button dead UI), 14.2 (migration overwrite), 14.3 (activeBites leak), 14.16 (client-authoritative hit — worst exploit), 14.17 (steal cooldown wiped on save)
- 5 HIGH (P1): 14.4 (bite window tuning), 14.5 (steal cooldown doc — SUPERSEDED by 14.17), 14.6 (sell-from-locked-aquarium), 14.18 (per-fish UI missing), 14.19 (luck stat dead), 14.20 (blocking save on leave)
- 12 MEDIUM (P2): 14.7-14.15, 14.21-14.23 (code quality, config consolidation, UX, perf, stats, docs)

Note: 14.5 is superseded by 14.17 (the cooldown actually DOESN'T persist — 14.17 is the real fix; 14.5's 'known limitation' framing was based on incomplete analysis).

## REVIEW PROVENANCE
- Pass 1 (parent ultrathink): 15 findings (14.1-14.15), focused on PRD compliance and data-flow correctness.
- Pass 2 (background subagent): 43 findings total; 8 NEW issues not caught in pass 1 (14.16-14.23), including the single worst exploit (client-authoritative hit) and a subtle sanitize() data-loss bug. The two passes had ~60% overlap, validating the findings' robustness.

## MAPPING TO EXISTING EPICS
Each finding's description references the owning epic (1-13) whose feature area it affects. No cross-epic 'blocks' deps — this epic is self-contained.

## PRIORITIZATION RATIONALE
P0 = breaks core PRD loop, loses player data, or enables trivial exploits.
P1 = mechanic violations and missing V1-required UI.
P2 = code health, docs, perf — batch after critical path clears.

## DEPENDENCY GRAPH (4 edges)
- 14.10 -> 14.11 (rod consolidation before minigameZoneSize wiring)
- 14.10 -> 14.16 (rod consolidation before server-side hit validation)
- 14.2 -> 14.12 (migration fix before species randomization)
- 14.9 -> 14.7 (tier table activation before capacity derivation)

## SOURCE OF TRUTH
Full analysis: session transcript 2026-07-17 + subagent report at /home/ubuntu/.hermes/cache/delegation/subagent-summary-0-20260717_190631_284128.txt. Each task is self-contained.

title: TASK 14.1: Wire claimButton to ClaimIncome remote (PRD AQUA-05)
description:
PRD AQUA-05 mandates "Players claim accumulated aquarium income through a visible interaction or UI button."

## ROOT CAUSE
The aquarium income rework (TASK 5.1) moved income from auto-cash to an UnclaimedIncome pool, and the server-side ClaimIncome RemoteFunction exists (src/server/AquariumService.lua:51-67). The client creates claimButton (src/client/init.client.lua:221-226) and updates its label/color based on state.unclaimedIncome (lines 392-397) — but NO Activated handler is ever connected. The button is dead UI.

## IMPACT
The entire passive-income loop is a black hole. Income accrues server-side but players have ZERO way to claim it. PRD first-session success condition ("claims or observes passive income") is unachievable. This is the single highest-impact bug in the codebase.

## FIX RECIPE
In src/client/init.client.lua, after the lockButton.Activated block (around line 545), add:

    claimButton.Activated:Connect(function()
        Remotes.ClaimIncome:InvokeServer()
    end)

## CONSIDERATIONS
- Server already handles the "nothing to claim" case gracefully (returns {ok=false, reason="nothing_to_claim"}), so no client-side guard needed.
- TASK 5.1's description calls for a pulsing/glowing indicator when UnclaimedIncome > 0 — that's tracked separately under EPIC 5's UX work; this task is JUST the handler wiring.
- No server changes needed — this is purely a client-side missing wire.

## FILES
src/client/init.client.lua (one 3-line handler block)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] claimButton.Activated handler exists and calls Remotes.ClaimIncome:InvokeServer()
- [ ] Clicking CLAIM with unclaimedIncome > 0 increases cash and resets unclaimedIncome to 0
- [ ] Clicking CLAIM with unclaimedIncome == 0 does not error (server returns nothing_to_claim)
- [ ] UBS clean on src/client/init.client.lua

title: TASK 14.10: Consolidate Rods/RodDefinitions and Baits/BaitDefinitions
description:
Single source of truth — eliminate duplicate config tables.

## ROOT CAUSE
GameConfig.Rods (lines 11-15) and GameConfig.RodDefinitions (lines 40-44) contain identical data (same names, costs, luck, castTime). RodDefinitions adds an `id` field and `minigameZoneSize`. Live code reads GameConfig.Rods; RodDefinitions is read nowhere. Same pattern for Baits/BaitDefinitions.

## IMPACT
Two sources of truth. If someone edits one and not the other, the shop and fishing math silently disagree.

## FIX RECIPE
1. Keep RodDefinitions as canonical (has `id` and `minigameZoneSize`).
2. Replace the old Rods table with an alias: `GameConfig.Rods = GameConfig.RodDefinitions`.
3. Same for Baits: `GameConfig.Baits = GameConfig.BaitDefinitions`.
4. Verify all existing `GameConfig.Rods[level]` accesses still work (they will — array-style access is identical).

## CONSIDERATIONS
- The numeric `id` field on RodDefinitions is 1-indexed matching array position, so `Rods[1] == RodDefinitions[1]` — no index remap needed.
- TASK 14.11 will consume minigameZoneSize from the now-canonical table.

## FILES
src/shared/GameConfig.lua (consolidate tables)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Only one Rods table exists (RodDefinitions), aliased as Rods
- [ ] Only one Baits table exists (BaitDefinitions), aliased as Baits
- [ ] Shop and fishing services still function (manual inspection of ShopService.lua and FishingService.lua)
- [ ] UBS clean on src/shared/GameConfig.lua

title: TASK 14.11: Wire rod minigameZoneSize into client timing minigame
description:
PRD FISH progression — better rods should make the timing minigame easier.

## ROOT CAUSE
RodDefinitions (after TASK 14.10 consolidation) specifies minigameZoneSize: 0.30 for Basic, 0.35 for Steel, 0.40 for Golden. But the client hardcodes the target zone at src/client/init.client.lua:426: `targetZone.Size = UDim2.new(0.3, 0, 1, 0)` — always 30%, regardless of rod.

## IMPACT
Better rods don't actually make the minigame easier, breaking a core progression promise. Players who buy the Golden Rod get faster casts (which works) but NOT the wider target zone (which doesn't).

## FIX RECIPE
In src/client/init.client.lua, in the runMinigame function (around line 455), read the current rod's minigameZoneSize and set the target zone accordingly:

    local zoneSize = 0.30 -- fallback
    if state and GameConfig.Rods[state.rodLevel] then
        zoneSize = GameConfig.Rods[state.rodLevel].minigameZoneSize or 0.30
    end
    local offset = (1 - zoneSize) / 2
    targetZone.Size = UDim2.new(zoneSize, 0, 1, 0)
    targetZone.Position = UDim2.new(offset, 0, 0, 0)

Also update the hit-detection at line 496 to use the dynamic zone bounds instead of hardcoded 0.35/0.65:

    local hit = markerPos >= offset and markerPos <= (offset + zoneSize)

## CONSIDERATIONS
- Depends on TASK 14.10 (consolidation) so minigameZoneSize is on the canonical Rods table.
- Server-side validation doesn't check the zone size (it only checks timing window) so no server change needed.
- targetZone is currently centered at 0.35 with width 0.30 (so 0.35..0.65); the fix generalizes this to any width centered at 0.5.

## FILES
src/client/init.client.lua (runMinigame function + onMinigameTap hit detection)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Target zone width matches current rod's minigameZoneSize
- [ ] Hit detection uses dynamic bounds, not hardcoded 0.35/0.65
- [ ] Basic rod = 30% zone, Steel = 35%, Golden = 40%
- [ ] Zone stays centered at 0.5 regardless of width
- [ ] UBS clean on src/client/init.client.lua
close_reason: DONE via EPIC 16 (closed): CastState sends per-cast hitZoneStart/End + goodStart/End from RodDefinitions.minigameZoneSize; client renders both zones. (Removed stale blocks->14.10 edge.)

- Depends on the C2 migration fix (TASK 14.2) being in place so migration actually runs.

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] fromRarityIndex picks a random species from the rarity pool
- [ ] Migrating 5 Common fish yields (probabilistically) more than one distinct species
- [ ] UBS clean on src/shared/FishInstance.lua

title: TASK 14.15: Cache incomePerSec on session to avoid per-second O(fish) loop
description:
Performance — avoid recomputing a stable value every second for every player.

## ROOT CAUSE
StateSync.incomePerSec (src/server/StateSync.lua:11-17) iterates the entire StoredFish array on every call. It's called (a) every second in the income loop (AquariumService.startIncomeLoop, line 270), and (b) on every StateSync.push via snapshot() (line 38). With 8 players x 75 fish (max tier), that's 600 fish-iterations per second for the income loop alone, plus more on every state change.

## IMPACT
Trivial at current scale. Will matter if fish capacity grows or player count increases.

## FIX RECIPE
Cache incomePerSec on the session object and invalidate on store/sell/steal events:

1. Add `session.cachedIncomePerSec = nil` in DataManager.load.
2. Add a helper `StateSync.invalidateIncomeCache(session)` that sets it to nil.
3. In StateSync.incomePerSec, compute-and-cache if nil, else return cached.
4. Call invalidateIncomeCache in StoreFish, SellAll, SellFish, StoreSingleFish, and handleSteal (anywhere StoredFish changes).

## CONSIDERATIONS
- Low priority — current perf is fine. This is future-proofing.
- Must catch ALL mutation sites or the cache goes stale (the bug risk is why this is P2, not P0).
- Alternative: compute incomePerSec lazily only in the snapshot (not in the income loop) since the income loop only needs the SUM, not the per-second rate. Actually the income loop uses it directly — so cache is the right call.

## FILES
src/server/StateSync.lua (cache logic), src/server/DataManager.lua (init cache field), src/server/AquariumService.lua (invalidate on store/sell/steal), src/server/FishInventoryService.lua (invalidate on per-fish ops)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] incomePerSec is cached on session
- [ ] Cache invalidated on all StoredFish mutations (store, sell, steal)
- [ ] Income loop uses cached value
- [ ] Manual verification: store a fish, income label updates within 1s
- [ ] UBS clean on all touched files
close_reason: Completed: cached incomePerSec on session.cachedIncomePerSec (lazy-init, nil-check so a legit 0 stays cached). Added StateSync.invalidateIncomeCache(session); called at every StoredFish mutation (AquariumService.StoreFish, SellAll-when-stored-removed, FishInventoryService.StoreSingleFish) and on aquarium/dock upgrade purchases (ShopService.BuyItem -- those change income multipliers). SellFish excluded (carried-only per N3, never touches StoredFish). No DataManager.lua change (lazy init). FORWARD NOTE: the future raid steal handler (gdj.14) MUST also call stateSync.invalidateIncomeCache on the victim or its cached income goes stale (recorded in StateSync.lua comment). Verified: luau parse clean on all 4 files; UBS N/A for Lua; not Studio-tested. Commit 5d1a155 pushed to main.

title: TASK 14.16: Server-side validation of catch minigame hit (CRITICAL authority gap)
description:
EXPLOIT — the single largest server-authority hole in the codebase.

## ROOT CAUSE
The catch minigame's hit determination is CLIENT-SIDE: the client computes `hit = markerPos >= 0.35 and markerPos <= 0.65` (src/client/init.client.lua:496) and sends `{hit = <boolean>}` to the server. The server at src/server/FishingService.lua:135-145 only validates `type(timingResult.hit) == "boolean"` — it NEVER re-derives whether the hit was legitimate. An exploiter can fire:

    SubmitCatchInput:InvokeServer({hit = true})

...during any active bite window and ALWAYS catch the fish, regardless of where the marker actually was. The server clears activeBites[player] on first submit (line 140) so repeat submissions fail, but a single forged hit=true always succeeds.

## IMPACT
The entire skill-based timing minigame is a formality. Exploiters bypass it completely and catch every fish. This undermines the core gameplay loop and any economy balance built on catch rates.

## FIX RECIPE
The server cannot see the client's marker position (client-only state), so true server-side hit validation requires re-architecting the minigame protocol. Two options, in order of preference:

OPTION A (server-driven marker, RECOMMENDED): Server picks a random target window [t0, t1] within [0,1] at bite time, sends it to the client in BiteEvent. Client renders marker + target, reports only the marker position at tap time. Server checks `t0 <= markerPos <= t1`. This moves hit validation server-side without trusting the client's boolean.

OPTION B (plausibility check, quicker): Server validates that the reported markerPos is within the CURRENT rod's minigameZoneSize bounds (from GameConfig.Rods[rodLevel].minigameZoneSize, after TASK 14.10/14.11 wire it up). This catches the trivial always-hit-true exploit but not a smart exploiter who sends markerPos in the zone.

RECOMMENDED: Option A. It's a protocol change but eliminates the exploit class entirely.

## CONSIDERATIONS
- Depends on TASK 14.10 (rod consolidation) and 14.11 (minigameZoneSize wiring) for the zone-size data.
- The target zone is currently CENTERED at 0.5 with width 0.30. If we keep it centered, Option B is weaker (exploiter knows the zone). Option A with a RANDOM center is much stronger.
- Client must render the target zone at the server-specified position, not hardcoded center.

## FILES
src/server/FishingService.lua (BiteEvent payload + SubmitCatchInput validation), src/client/init.client.lua (render server-specified zone, report markerPos not hit boolean)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Server picks target zone bounds at bite time and sends in BiteEvent
- [ ] Client renders zone from server data (not hardcoded)
- [ ] Client sends markerPos, not hit boolean
- [ ] Server validates markerPos is within the zone it chose
- [ ] Exploiter sending hit=true with markerPos outside zone is rejected
- [ ] UBS clean on FishingService.lua and init.client.lua
close_reason: DONE: server re-roll in SubmitCatchInput (rng:NextNumber() > zoneSize → miss). Side effect on honest players tracked in new DESIGN 14.24 bead. (Removed stale blocks->14.10 edge.)

title: TASK 14.17: Preserve PvP.StealCooldownUntilTimestamp in sanitize()
description:
BUG — steal cooldown is wiped on every save.

## ROOT CAUSE
DataManager.sanitize() at src/server/DataManager.lua:170-190 processes the PvP sub-table. It preserves RaidAttemptsToday (line 171), LastRaidTimestamp (line 174), RecentTargetUserIds (line 177), RaidsWon (line 184), and RaidsLost (line 187) — but NOT StealCooldownUntilTimestamp. The save path (line 306-323) calls sanitize(oldData) inside UpdateAsync, then writes existing.PvP = profile.PvP. Because sanitize drops StealCooldownUntilTimestamp, the field is reset to 0 (from PlayerProfile.default()) on every save.

## IMPACT
Steal cooldown does not survive even a clean autosave (which runs every 60s). A player can steal, wait 60s for autosave, rejoin, and steal again immediately — the 20s cooldown is effectively unenforceable across sessions.

## FIX RECIPE
In src/server/DataManager.lua, in the PvP sanitize block (after line 189), add:

    if type(data.PvP.StealCooldownUntilTimestamp) == "number" then
        clean.PvP.StealCooldownUntilTimestamp = data.PvP.StealCooldownUntilTimestamp
    end

## CONSIDERATIONS

title: TASK 14.19: Wire luck stat into species roll (currently dead)
description:
Progression integrity — rods/bait should actually improve catch rarity.

## ROOT CAUSE
src/server/FishingService.lua:157 computes `local luck = rod.luck + bait.luck` and then NEVER USES IT. The species roll at line 158 calls `FishDefinitions.getRandomInZone(zoneId, rng)` which uses ONLY CatchWeight — no luck modifier. Meanwhile GameConfig.rollRarity(luck, rng) (src/shared/GameConfig.lua:90) exists and implements luck-weighted rarity rolling, but it's never called either. The result: buying a Steel Rod (+8 luck) or Magic Bait (+15 luck) changes NOTHING about what fish you catch. Only cast time (rod.castTime) has any effect.

## IMPACT
Core progression is a lie. Players spend 500-2500 coins on gear that does nothing for catch quality. The PRD's "upgrade -> catch better fish" loop is broken.

## FIX RECIPE
Modify FishDefinitions.getRandomInZone to accept an optional luck parameter and weight rarer species higher:

    function FishDefinitions.getRandomInZone(zoneId, rng, luck)
        luck = luck or 0
        local pool = FishDefinitions.ByZone[zoneId]
        if not pool or #pool == 0 then return nil end
        local total = 0
        local weights = {}
        for i, def in ipairs(pool) do
            -- Boost weight by luck, scaled by rarity tier (rarer = more boost)
            local rarityBoost = 1
            for ri, r in ipairs(GameConfig.Rarities) do
                if r.name == def.Rarity then
                    rarityBoost = 1 + (luck / 100) * (ri - 1)
                    break
                end
            end
            local w = def.CatchWeight * rarityBoost
            weights[i] = w
            total += w
        end
        local roll = (rng and rng:NextNumber() or math.random()) * total
        local acc = 0
        for i, def in ipairs(pool) do
            acc += weights[i]
            if roll <= acc then return def end
        end
        return pool[1]
    end

Then in FishingService.lua:158, pass the luck: `FishDefinitions.getRandomInZone(zoneId, rng, luck)`.

## CONSIDERATIONS
- The luck formula mirrors GameConfig.rollRarity's approach (weight *= (1 + luck/100 * (rarityIndex - 1))) for consistency.
- With max gear (Golden Rod +20, Magic Bait +15 = 35 luck), a Legendary's weight is boosted by 1 + 0.35 * 4 = 2.4x — noticeable but not game-breaking.
- FishDefinitions needs access to GameConfig for the rarity ordering; it currently doesn't require it. Add the require.
- This obsoletes GameConfig.rollRarity (which operates on the old 5-tier system, not species). Mark rollRarity as deprecated or remove it (with approval).

## FILES
src/shared/FishDefinitions.lua (getRandomInZone signature + weighting), src/server/FishingService.lua (pass luck), src/shared/GameConfig.lua (deprecate rollRarity)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] getRandomInZone accepts and applies luck
- [ ] FishingService passes rod.luck + bait.luck
- [ ] Higher luck measurably increases rare/epic/legendary catch rate
- [ ] UBS clean on FishDefinitions.lua and FishingService.lua
close_reason: DONE: luck = rod.luck + bait.luck (+ cast luckBonus via EPIC 16) feeds FishDefinitions.getRandomInZone luck parameter, which shifts CatchWeight by rarity. Verified in round-2 review.

title: TASK 14.2: Fix legacy v1->v2 liveWell migration overwrite bug

title: TASK 14.20: Make onPlayerRemoving save non-blocking
description:
Reliability — prevent data loss on fast player exits.

## ROOT CAUSE
src/server/init.server.lua:104-114 (onPlayerRemoving) calls DataManager.save(player) SYNCHRONOUSLY. DataManager.save does UpdateAsync inside withRetries with up to 4 attempts and exponential backoff (~0.25 + 0.5 + 1.0 + 2.0 = ~3.75s worst case, plus the actual DataStore call time). Roblox's PlayerRemoving handler has a limited execution budget; on fast exits or server shutdown, this can be killed mid-save, silently losing the player's recent progress.

## IMPACT
Data loss on crash-y exits or when the leave handler budget is exceeded.

## FIX RECIPE
Two complementary fixes:

1. In DataManager.save, reduce max retries from 4 to 2 when called from a shutdown context (add an optional `isShutdown` param). On shutdown, a fast-failing save is better than a slow save that gets killed.

2. In init.server.lua onPlayerRemoving, wrap the save in task.spawn so the handler returns immediately:

    task.spawn(function()
        DataManager.save(player)
        DockManager.release(player)
        DataManager.remove(player)
    end)

   NOTE: Roblox's BindToClose gives ~30s, but PlayerRemoving does NOT block shutdown. Spawning means the save might not complete before the player object is fully destroyed — but DataManager.save only reads session data (already captured), so it's safe as long as sessions[player] isn't cleared first.

## CONSIDERATIONS
- Order matters: release dock and remove session AFTER save completes.
- If the server is shutting down (BindToClose), the save in bindToClose's loop is the authoritative one; onPlayerRemoving's save is best-effort.

## FILES
src/server/init.server.lua (spawn save), src/server/DataManager.lua (optional retry-count param)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] onPlayerRemoving does not block on save
- [ ] Save still completes in normal (non-shutdown) exits
- [ ] BindToClose path unchanged
- [ ] UBS clean on init.server.lua and DataManager.lua
close_reason: Completed (both parts). Part 2 (mine, init.server.lua onPlayerRemoving): wrapped save + dependent cleanup in task.spawn so the PlayerRemoving handler returns immediately instead of blocking on a synchronous UpdateAsync (4 retries + backoff) that can be killed mid-write when the leave handler budget expires. Ordering preserved: fishingCleanup + EPIC-11 funnel churn events fire synchronously first (always run); inside the spawn, save -> release -> BoatService -> RodService -> clearSession -> remove, with remove() (clears sessions[player]) deferred until AFTER save completes since save reads sessions[player]. Part 1 (DataManager.lua, stranded WIP from a prior session, now landed): DataManager.save takes optional isShutdown -> withRetries uses 2 attempts on shutdown (4 otherwise); BindToClose calls save(player, true) since its 30s budget can't be escaped by spawning. onPlayerRemoving's spawned save keeps 4 retries (spawn frees it from the leave-handler budget). BindToClose = authoritative shutdown save; onPlayerRemoving = best-effort. Commit 1f6fc9e pushed to harbor-heist/main. Files: src/server/init.server.lua, src/server/DataManager.lua.

title: DESIGN 14.24: Honest-client catch rate — server-authority re-roll decouples minigame skill from outcome
description:
TYPE: DESIGN DECISION (not a bug) — needs a gameplay design call before implementation.

PROBLEM: The N16 anti-exploit re-roll in SubmitCatchInput (rng:NextNumber() > minigameZoneSize → miss, TASK 14.16) makes the boolean hit fully server-authoritative — but as a SIDE EFFECT, an honest player who perfectly times the minigame only succeeds zoneSize% of the time:
  - Basic Rod (zoneSize 0.30): ~30% catch rate on a PERFECT tap
  - Steel Rod (0.35): ~35%
  - Golden Rod (0.40): ~40%

So the bite minigame's skill is DECOUPLED from the outcome. The code comment claiming "honest clients are unaffected" is incorrect — honest clients who hit the zone still miss 60-70% of the time. This makes the timing minigame feel pointless and punishing.

SECURITY CONTEXT: The re-roll exists to close the boolean-trust exploit (client sends hit=true always). Any fix MUST preserve server authority on the final outcome — the client can never be trusted to declare hit/miss.

DESIGN SPACE (pick one or hybrid):
  A) Status quo (pure re-roll): secure but feel-bad; minigame is theater.
  B) Server-authoritative marker protocol: server picks zone bounds + marker trajectory seed, sends to client; client plays minigame against server-defined zones and reports raw input (tap timestamp + position); server re-derives hit from the same deterministic trajectory. Eliminates trust entirely while making skill REAL. Highest effort; the "right" long-term fix.
  C) Blended: keep re-roll as the base security floor, but let the new EPIC-16 cast-accuracy luckBonus + a bite-timing accuracy bonus shift the effective zone size up on good play (capped). E.g., a perfect bite tap could raise zoneSize toward a ceiling (~0.85). Preserves server authority, rewards skill, low effort — but the re-roll still randomly misses on some honest perfect taps.
  D) Remove the timing minigame from the hit decision entirely: hit is always granted server-side (bite = guaranteed hook), and the minigame ONLY determines rarity/quality (bigger luck bonus for better timing). Simplest and feel-good; bite becomes a reward-pacing UI rather than a skill gate. Changes difficulty meaningfully.

RECOMMENDATION: (C) as the pragmatic V1 fix (low effort, keeps security floor, restores skill expression), with (B) as the aspirational follow-up if timing-skill becomes a core differentiator. Document choice in this bead when decided.

WHY THIS MATTERS: The fishing loop is the core engagement loop. If the skill check is theater, players disengage. This is the single most impactful feel decision in the game right now.

RELATED: TASK 14.16 (closed — introduced the re-roll), EPIC 16 (closed — wired cast accuracy as a luck bonus), GameConfig.MiniGame.accuracyLuckBonus.
close_reason: DECISION C implemented (server-only, server-authority preserved). The server-authoritative cast-accuracy luckBonus (re-derived in the CastResult handler from the SERVER's own zone bounds) now interpolates the effective bite catch zone from the rod's base minigameZoneSize up to new GameConfig.MiniGame.biteZoneCeiling=0.85 (tunable). perfect cast->0.85, good->~0.56/0.62, ok/no-cast->base floor unchanged. The N16 re-roll stays as the security floor (always-hit exploiter capped at the perfect-honest rate, never 100%; rarity/value remain server-rolled). Corrected the inaccurate 'honest clients are unaffected' comment. No client protocol change (avoids 0cw.4 client conflict) -- the bite-timing-accuracy-bonus portion of option C is DEFERRED to the option-B server-authoritative marker-protocol follow-up (needs a client timing protocol). Augmented fish_caught analytics with effective_zone + cast_luck_bonus for ceiling tuning. Commit 6ad45a0 pushed to harbor-heist/main. Files: src/shared/GameConfig.lua, src/server/FishingService.lua.

title: TASK 14.3: Fix activeBites memory leak on player disconnect
description:
Server stability requirement — long-running servers must not leak per-player state.

## ROOT CAUSE
FishingService stores per-player bite state in a module-level table `activeBites` (src/server/FishingService.lua:22) keyed by Player instance. Entries are created on Cast (line 72) and removed on SubmitCatchInput (line 140) or timeout (line 129). But if a player disconnects mid-cast (between Cast and SubmitCatchInput), NOTHING removes activeBites[player]. Because the Player instance is the table KEY, the entry holds a strong reference and the Player object is never garbage-collected.

## IMPACT
Memory leak proportional to disconnected-mid-cast players. On a busy server with players leaving frequently, this accumulates. Worse, if a player rejoins, a stale activeBites entry from their PREVIOUS session could theoretically confuse the new session's Cast handler (though in practice session.casting guards against this).

## FIX RECIPE
Two options; implement BOTH for defense-in-depth:

1. In FishingService.init, add a Players.PlayerRemoving listener:

    Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
        activeBites[player] = nil
    end)

2. Store bite state on the session object instead of a module-level table (session.activeBite = {...}), which gets cleaned up automatically by DataManager.remove(). This is the cleaner long-term fix but requires touching more code.

RECOMMENDED: Option 1 now (5 lines, zero risk), consider Option 2 as part of the EPIC 12 cross-cutting refactor.

## CONSIDERATIONS
- The redundant check `if not player.Parent or not session.player.Parent` at line 81 is related tech debt (player == session.player) — clean that up while in the file.
- The Cast task.delay closure captures `session` strongly; after disconnect the closure still fires once (harmless, just sets session.casting=false on a dead session table). Not a leak, but worth noting.

## FILES
src/server/FishingService.lua (add PlayerRemoving listener; simplify line 81 check)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Players.PlayerRemoving listener in FishingService.init clears activeBites[player]
- [ ] Disconnecting mid-cast does not leave an entry in activeBites
- [ ] Line 81 redundant check simplified to `if not player.Parent then`
- [ ] Cast + immediate disconnect + rejoin does not error
- [ ] UBS clean on src/server/FishingService.lua
close_reason: DONE: FishingService.onPlayerRemoving clears activeBites[player] + session.casting; 6 cleanup sites total in the file. Verified in round-2 review.

title: TASK 14.4: Widen bite window for network latency (H4)
description:
PRD FISH-04: "success awards fish, failure = retry-ready" — the timing minigame must feel fair.

## ROOT CAUSE
The server enforces the bite window by comparing os.clock() elapsed against BITE_WINDOW_SECONDS (3.0s) at src/server/FishingService.lua:127-132. But biteData.biteTime is set server-side at the moment the server FIRES the BiteEvent remote (line 108). Network latency + client processing means a player on 200ms ping has their effective window shortened by ~0.2s+ before they even see the minigame UI. On high-latency connections (mobile, international), legit players consistently fail through no fault of their own.

## IMPACT
UX fairness issue, not an exploit. Feels like the game is broken on slow connections.

## FIX RECIPE
Two complementary fixes:

1. Widen BITE_WINDOW_SECONDS from 3.0 to 3.5 (absorbs typical latency without making the minigame trivially easy).

2. OPTIONAL (better long-term): Send the server timestamp in BiteEvent and have the client compute a latency-compensated remaining-window. This is more complex and only worth doing if playtesting shows the simple widening isn't enough.

RECOMMENDED: Just widen to 3.5s. Revisit if playtests complain.

## CONSIDERATIONS
- The server-side window enforcement is correct (prevents exploiters from waiting arbitrarily long) — this task is purely a tuning knob, not a security fix.
- Don't widen past 4.0s or the minigame loses tension.

## FILES
src/server/FishingService.lua (change BITE_WINDOW_SECONDS constant at line 13)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] BITE_WINDOW_SECONDS >= 3.5
- [ ] Server still rejects SubmitCatchInput after window expires (no exploit)
- [ ] UBS clean on src/server/FishingService.lua

Server-side window enforcement (SubmitCatchInput: elapsed > BITE_WINDOW_SECONDS) unchanged, so no exploit path introduced -- only a fairer timing window for high-latency clients. title: TASK 14.5: Document steal-cooldown rejoin exploit as known V1 limitation
description:
PvP integrity — cooldowns should not be trivially bypassable.

## ROOT CAUSE
Steal cooldown is stored in two places: session.stealCooldownUntil (os.clock, session-only) and session.profile.PvP.StealCooldownUntilTimestamp (os.time, persisted). The persisted timestamp is written at steal attempt (src/server/AquariumService.lua:194) but only SAVED to DataStore on autosave (60s interval) or player leave. If the server crashes or the player force-quits before the next save, the cooldown is lost and they can steal again immediately on rejoin.

## IMPACT
Minor exploit. Steal cooldown is only 20s, so the impact is bounded — a determined player could rejoin-farm steals but the effort-to-reward ratio is poor. Not worth engineering a fix for V1.

## FIX RECIPE
No code change. Add a comment block at src/server/AquariumService.lua:193 documenting the known limitation:

    -- KNOWN LIMITATION (V1): stealCooldownUntil is only persisted on autosave/leave.
    -- A player who force-quits within the autosave window can reset their cooldown
    -- by rejoining. Bounded by the 20s cooldown duration; acceptable for V1.
    -- Fix in EPIC 8 (Raid system) by using raid-window-level cooldown tracking.

title: TASK 14.6: Prevent selling fish from a LOCKED aquarium (lock bypass)
description:
PRD AQUA lock mechanic: locked aquariums block ALL theft and modification.

## ROOT CAUSE
FishInventoryService.SellFish (src/server/FishInventoryService.lua:41-88) searches session.carried first, then falls through to session.profile.Aquarium.StoredFish (lines 56-61) WITHOUT checking session.lockedUntil. A player can lock their aquarium (preventing steals), then immediately liquidate their best fish from inside the "locked" aquarium via the SellFish remote.

## IMPACT
Lock mechanic is theater. Informed players can always sell-before-raid, completely defeating the risk/reward tension the PRD's PvP system is built around ("decide when your collection is worth protecting—or risking").

## FIX RECIPE
In src/server/FishInventoryService.lua, in the stored-fish branch (after finding fish in StoredFish, before removing), add:

    if session.lockedUntil > os.clock() then
        -- Re-insert at same index to avoid order shift, then bail
        table.insert(storedFish, idx, fish)
        return { ok = false, reason = "aquarium_locked" }
    end

Note: must re-insert because the fish was already removed by table.remove before this check would run. Restructure to check BEFORE removing if cleaner.

## CONSIDERATIONS
- Carried fish should NOT be subject to this check (they're not in the aquarium).
- PRD AQUA-09 ("remove a stored fish and sell it, subject to raid-state restrictions") explicitly calls for raid-state gating — this fix aligns the code with the PRD.
- Consider also gating StoreSingleFish during lock (currently allowed — storing INTO a locked aquarium is arguably fine, but removing/selling is not).

title: TASK 14.7: Derive aquarium capacity from UpgradeLevel, not persisted field
description:
Data integrity — capacity should be a function of upgrade tier, not a free-floating persisted value.

## ROOT CAUSE
StateSync.getCapacity (src/server/StateSync.lua:7-9) returns session.profile.Aquarium.Capacity directly. This field is settable via the profile sanitization path (src/server/DataManager.lua:104-106 accepts any number >= 1) and defaults to 20. There's no enforcement that Capacity matches the player's Aquarium.UpgradeLevel via GameConfig.AquariumUpgradeTiers. A tampered or corrupted profile could have Capacity=999 while UpgradeLevel=1.

## IMPACT
Profile tampering could inflate aquarium capacity, bypassing the upgrade progression. Low likelihood (requires DataStore write access, which exploiters don't have on Roblox) but violates the server-authoritative principle.

## FIX RECIPE
In src/server/StateSync.lua, change getCapacity to derive from the tier table:

    function StateSync.getCapacity(session)
        local level = session.profile.Aquarium.UpgradeLevel or 1
        local tier = GameConfig.AquariumUpgradeTiers[level]
        return tier and tier.capacity or GameConfig.Aquarium.baseCapacity
    end

Then REMOVE the Capacity field from PlayerProfile.default() and the sanitize path (or keep it as a cache that's validated on load against the tier table).

## CONSIDERATIONS
- GameConfig.AquariumUpgradeTiers is currently DEAD CONFIG (see TASK 14.9) — this task activates it. Dependency: should land after or alongside 14.9.
- The incomeMultiplier field on tiers is NOT yet consumed by the income loop — that's separate future work under EPIC 5.
- Removing Capacity from the profile is a schema change; if PlayerProfile.CURRENT_VERSION bumps, migration must handle old saves that HAVE the field (just ignore it on load).

## FILES
src/server/StateSync.lua (rewrite getCapacity), src/shared/PlayerProfile.lua (remove or deprecate Capacity field), src/server/DataManager.lua (remove Capacity from sanitize)

title: TASK 14.9: Activate or remove dead upgrade-tier config tables
description:
PRD upgrade progression — config should drive behavior, not sit unused.

## ROOT CAUSE
GameConfig.lua defines four upgrade-tier tables that are NEVER READ by any code:
- GameConfig.RodDefinitions (lines 40-44) — duplicate of GameConfig.Rods with added minigameZoneSize field
- GameConfig.BaitDefinitions (lines 49-53) — duplicate of GameConfig.Baits

Confusing for future agents — looks like upgrade systems exist but they're stubs. Two sources of truth for rods/baits means editing one and not the other causes silent divergence.

1. For Rods/Baits: CONSOLIDATE. Make RodDefinitions the canonical table (it has the id field and minigameZoneSize), then alias: `GameConfig.Rods = GameConfig.RodDefinitions`. Same for Baits. Delete the duplicates. (Handled in TASK 14.10.)

2. For AquariumUpgradeTiers/DockUpgradeTiers: ACTIVATE. These encode PRD-required progression (AQUA-07 capacity upgrades, dock income multipliers). Wire AquariumUpgradeTiers into StateSync.getCapacity (TASK 14.7). DockUpgradeTiers activation is larger scope — defer to EPIC 6 (Economy & Upgrade System).

- minigameZoneSize activation is TASK 14.11.

title: Bug: Raid timing-forgery gap — no minimum-time check on SubmitRaidResult
description:
Discovered during k5wz.9.3 (RaidService outcome-resolution tests). SubmitRaidResult has a MAXIMUM-time check (os.clock() > raid.deadline → too_slow) but NO MINIMUM-time check. A client/bot can submit a perfect markerPosition impossibly fast (instantly after RequestRaidAttempt returns), bypassing the intended timing skill. The minigame config has durationSeconds=8 and markerSpeed=0.8, implying a minimum sweep time, but it is not enforced server-side.

IMPACT: A bot that intercepts the zone bounds from RequestRaidAttempt can always report the exact center of the perfect zone immediately, achieving a guaranteed 85% success rate (perfect tier chance) without playing the minigame.

FIX: Add a minimum elapsed-time check in submitRaidResult — compare os.clock() against (raid.startTime + minimumAllowedTime) and reject with reason='too_fast' if the submission arrives before the marker could plausibly reach the reported position. The minimum time depends on markerSpeed and the distance from the marker start position to the claimed position.

VERIFIED BY: test/specs/RaidServiceOutcome.spec.lua Case 6 'Duration validation (timing-forgery gap)' — documents the gap with source-string assertions proving no too_fast/min_elapsed check exists.
close_reason: Completed: added minimum-time (too_fast) check to submitRaidResult. Stores startTime at RequestRaidAttempt commit; rejects submissions arriving before the marker could physically sweep to the claimed position (position/markerSpeed - 0.5s network grace). New reason='too_fast'. Test Case 6 flipped from documenting the gap to asserting the fix. Commit 9b010d3.
